headline: Islamabad, Beijing reaffirm strategic ties in Chinese minister's talks with Pakistan's leaders
subheadline: Liu Haixing, Minister of IDCPC Central Committee, holds key meetings with Shehbaz, CDF Munir, and DPM Dar
author: Web Desk
article_text:
PM links political engagement, party-to-party exchanges to better ties.
Highlights cooperation in trade, investment, connectivity, IT, agriculture.
CDF, Chinese minister discuss regional, international security developments.

ISLAMABAD: A visiting Chinese Communist Party (CPC) minister held separate meetings with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir and Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar on Monday, with discussions focusing on bilateral cooperation, political engagement and regional and international developments.

Liu Haixing, Minister of the International Department of the CPC Central Committee (IDCPC), is on his first official visit to Pakistan, which began on November 1, according to the Foreign Office.

During his meeting with the prime minister, Shehbaz stressed the importance of sustained political engagement and party-to-party exchanges to strengthen bilateral relations further.

Welcoming Liu and his delegation, the premier reaffirmed that Pakistan and China enjoyed an iron-clad, time-tested and All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership.

He said the friendship between the two countries was anchored in mutual trust, respect and deep-rooted bonds between their peoples.

Shehbaz appreciated the IDCPC's role in fostering institutional linkages and promoting cooperation between the two countries' political leadership.

He also highlighted their shared focus on advancing cooperation in trade, investment, connectivity, infrastructure development, information technology and agricultural modernisation.

Liu conveyed the greetings of the Chinese leadership and reaffirmed Beijing's commitment to further deepening its longstanding friendship with Pakistan.

Both sides also exchanged views on regional and international developments and reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining close coordination and cooperation at bilateral and multilateral forums.

The prime minister also hosted a banquet in honour of the visiting minister and his delegation.

Separately, Liu called on the CDF and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir at the General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi.

According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the two sides discussed matters of mutual interest, evolving regional and international security dynamics and bilateral relations.

They expressed their shared resolve to further strengthen the all-weather strategic cooperative partnership between Pakistan and China.

Field Marshal Munir highlighted the historic and time-tested bonds between the two countries and emphasised the importance of sustained high-level engagement, stronger institutional linkages and expanded cooperation across areas of mutual interest.

The visiting dignitary appreciated Pakistan's contributions to regional peace and stability and expressed confidence in further advancing the longstanding strategic partnership between the two countries.

In another meeting, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to further strengthening its strategic partnership with China.

The two sides discussed ways to enhance cultural ties and people-to-people exchanges, while resolving to maintain close coordination and carry forward the positive momentum in bilateral relations.

Liu also conveyed greetings from Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, which Dar warmly reciprocated. The deputy prime minister also conveyed warm greetings to Chinese President Xi Jinping on behalf of Pakistan's leadership.

The visit is part of ongoing high-level and party-to-party exchanges between Islamabad and Beijing, reflecting their commitment to strengthening their All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership.

Liu's engagements with Pakistan's political and military leadership come as the two countries continue to expand cooperation across political, economic, security and institutional domains.

headline: Gerard Way confirms MCR will start working on new album 'next year'
subheadline: My Chemical Romance's last album was 2010's 'Danger Days'
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Gerard Way just made it official: My Chemical Romance will start working on new music next year.

During the rock band’s Hollywood Bowl concert on Friday, October 30, their frontman confirmed that their next album will arrive at the latest by 2028.

“Next year, we wanna go make a record,” he told the crowd per fan-captured footage. According to Way, MCR will spend the next year in the studio and resume touring in 2028. “Hopefully, we’ll see you guys in 2028,” he teased.

READ MORE: Dallas Cowboy Cheerleaders sue MCR over staged shootout at Hollywood Bowl

Way first teased the album (which would mark their fifth studio album) on September 12 during the group’s final Long Live the Black Parade show — their first tour since reuniting in 2019. “Just know that, like, we’ve kind of really always wanted to make another record, so we hope life allows us to do that,” he said at the time, telling fans that they “deserve another record” for their never-ending support.

The group — consisting of brothers Gerard and Mikey Way, Ray Toro, and Frank Iero — broke up in 2013 but got the band back together in 2019. Since then, they’ve been touring and have yet to release another album following 2010’s Danger Days: The True Lives of the Fabulous Five.

Their only new release since then has been the 2022 single The Foundations of Decay.

headline: King Charles set for meaningful reunion in Antigua amid fresh calls to end monarchy
subheadline: Antigua’s PM delivers pointed message to Kemi Badenoch as he challenges monarchy’s future
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles is set for a reunion with a group of young Antiguans who have completed a special heritage conservation programme established by his foundation.

The King's Foundation has revealed that 8 students and 2 tutors from the country recently completed its Building Craft and Conservation Programme, which took place across two of the charity's sites in Scotland and England, Dumfries House and Highgrove Gardens.

Over four weeks, they learned traditional building techniques and sustainable construction methods under the guidance of expert tutors.

Read More: Queen Camilla makes Caribbean return in vibrant turquoise joining King Charles

Their training will now be put into practice back home, where they have joined forces on a 'Live Build' project at Government House in St John's.

Palace shared the update on Instagram, revealing that Charles will meet the students again at Government House during his visit to Antigua.

Meanwhile, the country's Prime Minister, Gaston Browne, has made clear that his government continues to have ambitions for a future without the British monarch as head of state.

Speaking to journalist Chris Ship after a meeting at his office, Browne reiterated his support for reparations over Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade.

He also criticised Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch after her comments that Britain should stop apologising for its colonial past.

Taking aim at Badenoch, the Prime Minister said: "No wonder she is the leader of the Opposition and not the Prime Minister."

Despite welcoming Charles to the summit, Browne also confirmed that he wants the country to replace the British monarch as head of state and become a republic.

article_html:
King Charles is set for a reunion with a group of young Antiguans who have completed a special heritage conservation programme established by his foundation.

The King's Foundation has revealed that 8 students and 2 tutors from the country recently completed its Building Craft and Conservation Programme, which took place across two of the charity's sites in Scotland and England, Dumfries House and Highgrove Gardens.

Over four weeks, they learned traditional building techniques and sustainable construction methods under the guidance of expert tutors. 

Read More: Queen Camilla makes Caribbean return in vibrant turquoise joining King Charles

Their training will now be put into practice back home, where they have joined forces on a 'Live Build' project at Government House in St John's.

Palace shared the update on Instagram, revealing that Charles will meet the students again at Government House during his visit to Antigua.

Meanwhile, the country's Prime Minister, Gaston Browne, has made clear that his government continues to have ambitions for a future without the British monarch as head of state.

Speaking to journalist Chris Ship after a meeting at his office, Browne reiterated his support for reparations over Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade. 

He also criticised Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch after her comments that Britain should stop apologising for its colonial past.

Taking aim at Badenoch, the Prime Minister said: "No wonder she is the leader of the Opposition and not the Prime Minister."

Despite welcoming Charles to the summit, Browne also confirmed that he wants the country to replace the British monarch as head of state and become a republic.

headline: Martha Stewart addresses backlash over her homeless Halloween costume
subheadline: The lifestyle mogul, 85, insists her intentions were to bring awareness to homelessness
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Martha Stewart has addressed the backlash over her Halloween costume depicting a homeless person.

The lifestyle mogul shared her response with Page Six on Sunday, November 1, after deleting the controversial photo from social media.

“I am distressed that my Halloween costume yesterday, which was intended to bring more awareness to the very serious subject of homelessness, has offended people, which was never my intention,” Stewart said in a statement.

READ MORE: Martha Stewart makes rare comment about her 'jerk' ex-husband

The 85-year-old businesswoman defended her intentions by highlighting her longstanding efforts to support charities addressing homelessness.

“Homelessness continues to remain one of America’s greatest challenges and ongoing crises, something that I care deeply about and I have spent a significant amount of time and effort supporting charities that combat this ongoing social epidemic,” she continued.

Stewart also reaffirmed her commitment to the cause, saying she was “committed to continuing to make a difference.”

The controversy erupted after she posted a photo of herself wearing ripped clothing, dirt on her face and holding a sign reading, “I am hungry. Help me.” The image appeared in a carousel promoting her candles before she removed it.

headline: Tom Brady makes severe mistake on live Fox broadcast
subheadline: Tom Brady swears on air after misjudging 300-yard passing games question
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Tom Brady has cursed on a live broadcast for the second time this season, after getting a trivia question about NFL passing records wrong on Sunday’s pregame show.

On 1 November, Brady appeared on Fox NFL Sunday from Detroit, where he was due to call the Vikings-Lions game.

He was asked who ranked third, behind Drew Brees and himself, in career 300-yard passing games.

Read more: Candice Swanepoel spotted with gold ring as Tom Brady romance heats up

He first guessed Brees, then seemed to realise his mistake and said “Oh, s**t”. He turned away from the camera, then looked back and smiled, and went on to name Peyton Manning, the correct answer.

Michael Strahan and Terry Bradshaw, who were on set, laughed along with the moment.

It was not the first time Brady has slipped on air this season.

In September, while covering the Commanders-Cowboys game in Arlington, Texas, he said the same thing when reacting to a replay of Jayden Daniels’ dislocated left elbow.

“Excuse me. I was not expecting to see that,” he said afterwards.

The latest incident comes after Brady was heard criticising officiating during Fox’s Packers-Lions broadcast the previous Sunday.

Brady, who is also a part-owner of the Raiders, is bound by NFL team-access restrictions that stop him from criticising officiating too strenuously.

A source said the NFL regularly talks with its broadcast partners about such matters but keeps those conversations private.

Profane content is restricted on broadcast television between 6am and 10pm, and the FCC can issue warnings, impose fines or revoke licences.

It is unclear whether the regulator will take any action over Brady’s remarks. Neither Fox nor the FCC has responded to requests for comment.

headline: SNL pays tribute to Patrick Stewart with 1994 clip three days after death
subheadline: SNL remembers Sir Patrick Stewart with title card and archive footage
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Saturday Night Live has paid tribute to Sir Patrick Stewart, airing a clip from his 1994 hosting appearance just three days after his death was announced.

The tribute came at the end of Saturday’s episode on 31 October, before the closing goodnights.

NBC re-aired a short clip from Stewart’s 5 February 1994 episode, in which he enthusiastically introduces that night’s musical guests, Salt-N-Pepa.

Read more: Patrick Stewart spoke over distant relationship with children before death

The high-energy delivery has gone viral in recent years, along with another of his musical introductions from the same show.

A title card was also shown in his memory, featuring one of the promo photos he shot during his 1994 hosting week.

The show shared the picture on social media with the caption “Remembering Patrick Stewart.”

Stewart hosted SNL only once. No new sketches were reported as part of the tribute.

Stewart died aged 86 on 28 October, with his death announced the next day. His family said he had Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia, neither of which was public before his death.

His longtime spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak, described a “brief and poignant journey” with the diseases, and said he was surrounded by family and friends.

The family asked that donations be made to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund and the Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources instead of flowers.

Tributes have poured in from across the industry, including from Sir Ian McKellen.

Marvel Studios released a still of Stewart as Professor X, calling him “a true gentleman”.

His final film performance, in Avengers: Doomsday, opens on 18 December, and Avengers: Secret Wars follows on 17 December 2027.

cleaned_text:
Saturday Night Live has paid tribute to Sir Patrick Stewart, airing a clip from his 1994 hosting appearance just three days after his death was announced.

The tribute came at the end of Saturday’s episode on 31 October, before the closing goodnights.

NBC re-aired a short clip from Stewart’s 5 February 1994 episode, in which he enthusiastically introduces that night’s musical guests, Salt-N-Pepa.

Read more: Patrick Stewart spoke over distant relationship with children before death

The high-energy delivery has gone viral in recent years, along with another of his musical introductions from the same show.

A title card was also shown in his memory, featuring one of the promo photos he shot during his 1994 hosting week.

The show shared the picture on social media with the caption “Remembering Patrick Stewart.”

Stewart hosted SNL only once. No new sketches were reported as part of the tribute.

Stewart died aged 86 on 28 October, with his death announced the next day. His family said he had Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia, neither of which was public before his death.

His longtime spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak, described a “brief and poignant journey” with the diseases, and said he was surrounded by family and friends.

The family asked that donations be made to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund and the Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources instead of flowers.

Tributes have poured in from across the industry, including from Sir Ian McKellen.

Marvel Studios released a still of Stewart as Professor X, calling him “a true gentleman”.

His final film performance, in Avengers: Doomsday, opens on 18 December, and Avengers: Secret Wars follows on 17 December 2027.

headline: Pete Davidson, ex Elsie Hewitt reunite in for daughter's first Halloween
subheadline: Baby Scottie dresses as Tony Soprano as Pete Davidson and Elsie Hewitt put split aside
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pete Davidson and Elsie Hewitt have reunited to celebrate their daughter Scottie’s first Halloween, with the whole family dressing up in Sopranos costumes more than five months after their split.

Hewitt shared the photos in an Instagram carousel on 1 November, captioned “smells like halloween”.

Scottie, who is 10 months old, was dressed as Tony Soprano in a robe, sitting in a wagon with a blue blanket on her lap, surrounded by a yellow rubber duck and stuffed ducks.

Read more: Pete Davidson returns to dad duties after controversial date outing

The set-up appeared to be a nod to Tony, played by the late James Gandolfini, relaxing in a jacuzzi.

She also held a fake cigar, and a light-up “Bada Bing!” sign, referencing the show’s fictional strip club, was attached to her wagon.

Hewitt, 30, dressed as Christopher Moltisanti, played by Michael Imperioli, in a dark red tracksuit, neck brace and dark sunglasses.

Davidson, 32, went as Paulie Walnuts, played by Tony Sirico, in track pants and a leather jacket, with silver-white wings added to his dark hair.

The couple split in May after a little over a year of dating.

In July, they issued a joint statement through their reps to Page Six on their arrangement: “We are cooperatively co-parenting our daughter whose well-being remains our top priority, and we are fully committed to working together to give her love from both of us.”

Davidson has spoken about how fatherhood has changed him.

“Scottie is my whole life,” he told Variety in September. He said he used to live or die by what people thought of him, but that everything changed when he first saw his daughter.

“As soon as I saw her for the first time, I was like, ‘Oh my God, none of this f--kin’ matters at all. It’s a job. If I get to do cool stuff, great; if not, cool, I get to be home more with my kid.’”

Read more: Sophie Rain says ‘I am the girl' behind Pete Davidson's story

headline: US midterms: Democrats lead national polls as key races remain on a knife's edge
subheadline: All 435 House seats, 35 Senate seats and 36 governorships are on ballot on Nov 3, with nearly 50m Americans having already voted
author: Raja Zahid Akhtar Khanazada
article_text:
With just a day to go before the United States midterm elections on November 3, the country's political temperature has risen sharply. The vote, the first nationwide test of President Donald Trump's second term, will decide the balance of power in both chambers of Congress, the leadership of dozens of states and the direction of federal legislation for the next two years.

National polls show Democrats ahead in the race for the House of Representatives, while seven Senate contests remain fiercely competitive and several governorships could change hands.

Nearly 50 million Americans have already cast their ballots. The central question is whether Democrats can break the Republican hold on Congress, or whether Trump's party will retain its grip.

Voters will elect all 435 members of the House, 35 senators, including 33 regular seats and two special elections, and governors in 36 states. Republicans currently hold 53 seats in the 100-member Senate. Democrats hold 45, and the two independents, Bernie Sanders and Angus King, caucus with them, giving Democrats an effective 47. To win the chamber, Democrats need a net gain of at least four seats. In the House, current membership stands at 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats, one independent aligned with Republicans and two vacancies. A majority requires 218 seats, meaning even a small shift could change control.

The generic congressional ballot, which measures which party voters prefer nationally, shows Democrats ahead. RealClearPolling's average for October 9 to 30 puts Democrats at 51.8% and Republicans at 43.3%, a lead of 8.5 points. An NBC News poll conducted from October 28 to 30 showed Democrats leading 52 to 45. Emerson College, polling from October 24 to 26, found a 52 to 42 lead, Reuters/Ipsos 53 to 44, and CBS News 53 to 45. The Harvard-Harris survey showed a narrower margin of 52 to 48. Ballotpedia's polling index of October 30 also put the Democratic lead at about eight points.

But national numbers do not translate directly into seats. House members are elected in 435 separate districts, and a party can win the national popular vote while still losing individual contests.

In its October 30 ratings, the Cook Political Report classified 222 seats as leaning towards Democrats, 195 towards Republicans and 18 as toss-ups. These figures combine its "solid", "likely" and "lean" categories and are assessments of competitiveness, not projected results. Cook shifted several districts towards Democrats in the final week of October, and media coverage of its update discussed scenarios in which Democrats could gain between 12 and 25 seats. Inside Elections and Sabato's Crystal Ball also moved several Republican-held seats into more competitive categories during October.

Cook lists 14 Republican-held or vacated seats as toss-ups. They include California's 22nd district, held by David Valadao, Colorado's 5th, held by Jeff Crank, Iowa's 2nd, open after Ashley Hinson's Senate run, and Kentucky's 6th, vacated by Andy Barr. In Michigan, the 4th district of Bill Huizenga, the 7th of Tom Barrett and the 10th, left open by John James, are all in play. The list also includes Montana's 1st, vacated by Ryan Zinke, New York's 17th, held by Mike Lawler, Ohio's 7th, held by Max Miller, Pennsylvania's 1st, held by Brian Fitzpatrick, South Carolina's 1st, Nancy Mace's former seat, Texas's 15th, held by Monica De La Cruz, and Virginia's 1st, held by Rob Wittman.

Four Democratic-held or vacated seats are also toss-ups: Florida's 14th, held by Kathy Castor, Florida's 22nd, open after Lois Frankel's departure, North Carolina's 1st, held by Don Davis, and Texas's 35th, open after Greg Casar's departure. Cook rates three Democratic seats, Alabama's 2nd, Florida's 9th and Maine's 2nd, as leaning Republican, while placing Pennsylvania's 8th and Ohio's 9th in the "lean Democrat" column. In a report on October 31, The Washington Post cited Cook's analysis suggesting that in some scenarios Democrats could reach as many as 240 seats, though these remain projections, not results.

Of the 35 Senate seats up for election, Republicans hold 22 and Democrats 13. Cook rates six Republican seats and one Democratic seat as toss-ups. In Alaska, Republican Senator Dan Sullivan faces Democrat Mary Peltola, a former congresswoman. In Iowa, where Republican Joni Ernst is not running, Republican Ashley Hinson faces Democrat Josh Turek in a race some models show as extremely close. In Kansas, Republican Senator Roger Marshall faces Democrat Adam Hamilton, and in Maine, Republican Susan Collins faces Democrat Troy Jackson in a state Democrats carried in the 2024 presidential election.

In Michigan, following Democrat Gary Peters's retirement, Muslim American Abdul El-Sayed is defending the seat against Republican Mike Rogers. In Ohio's special election, Republican Senator Jon Husted faces former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown. In Texas, Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico are vying for John Cornyn's former seat, with several October polls showing a narrow gap. Six of these seven seats are held by Republicans; only Michigan is Democratic.

Elsewhere, Cook rates North Carolina, where former Democratic Governor Roy Cooper faces Republican Michael Whatley for the seat vacated by Thom Tillis, as "likely Democrat", making it one of the party's best pickup opportunities. Democrats must also defend their seats in Georgia, where Senator Jon Ossoff faces Republican Mike Collins, in New Hampshire, where Chris Pappas faces Republican John Sununu, and in Minnesota, where Peggy Flanagan faces Republican Michele Tafoya. Cook rates all three as leaning Democratic to varying degrees.

Other notable contests include Florida's special election, where Ashley Moody faces Democrat Angie Nixon, Nebraska, where Pete Ricketts faces independent Dan Osborn, South Carolina, where Lindsey Graham faces Democrat Annie Andrews, and Mississippi, where Cindy Hyde-Smith faces Scott Colom. Most of the remaining seats are rated safe for their current party. Analysts caution that control of the Senate will hinge on net gains and losses across many races, not on any single state.

In the race for governorships, Republicans currently hold 26 and Democrats 24. Several governors are not running because of term limits or other reasons, opening up a number of contests. Cook rates Georgia, Kansas and Nevada as toss-ups, while Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ) places Nevada and Ohio in that category, a difference that shows how much the analytical models diverge.

In Georgia, former Democratic Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms faces Republican Rick Jackson for the seat of term-limited Governor Brian Kemp. In Nevada, Republican Governor Joe Lombardo faces Democratic Attorney General Aaron Ford. In Kansas, Democrat Cindy Holscher faces Republican Ty Masterson; Cook rates the race a toss-up, while DDHQ says it leans Republican. In Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton faces Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a contest DDHQ calls a toss-up and Cook rates as leaning Democratic.

Other competitive races include Alaska, where ranked-choice voting applies, as well as Iowa, Wisconsin, Michigan, Arizona, Florida, Texas, Oregon and New Hampshire. Cook rates Republican-held Alaska, Iowa and Ohio as leaning Democratic. DDHQ's overall ratings place 20 of the 36 races on the Democratic side, seven safe, nine likely and four leaning, and 14 on the Republican side, five leaning, four likely and five safe, with two toss-ups. The 14 states not holding elections will keep their current governors.

Early voting has been heavy. According to On Point Politics' tracker as of November 1, more than 49.4 million ballots had been cast across 47 reporting states, about 23.1 million by mail and 26.3 million in person. In states that report party registration, registered Democrats made up about 40.4% of early voters and registered Republicans about 32.9%, with the rest independents or members of smaller parties.

These figures reflect voters' registration, not how they voted. Large states such as Texas, California, Florida, North Carolina, Georgia and Washington do not all report the data in the same way, and the numbers offer no indication of how many more people will vote on Election Day.

At its core, the election is a referendum on the first two years of Trump's second term. Democrats are campaigning on the economy, healthcare, inflation, democratic institutions and federal policy, while Republicans are emphasising immigration, border security, taxes, energy and their party's governing priorities. The weight of these issues varies from state to state and district to district, and national polls, while pointing to a general trend, are no substitute for local contests.

The results across the House, the Senate and the governors' mansions will shape federal legislation, budgets, congressional oversight of the presidency and state-level governance for the next two years.

For now, the available evidence shows Democrats ahead nationally in the race for the House, several Republican Senate seats under serious threat and the political balance of a number of states being tested in the governors' races. The real picture will emerge only once the votes are counted.

article_html:
With just a day to go before the United States midterm elections on November 3, the country's political temperature has risen sharply. The vote, the first nationwide test of President Donald Trump's second term, will decide the balance of power in both chambers of Congress, the leadership of dozens of states and the direction of federal legislation for the next two years.

National polls show Democrats ahead in the race for the House of Representatives, while seven Senate contests remain fiercely competitive and several governorships could change hands. 

Nearly 50 million Americans have already cast their ballots. The central question is whether Democrats can break the Republican hold on Congress, or whether Trump's party will retain its grip.

Voters will elect all 435 members of the House, 35 senators, including 33 regular seats and two special elections, and governors in 36 states. Republicans currently hold 53 seats in the 100-member Senate. Democrats hold 45, and the two independents, Bernie Sanders and Angus King, caucus with them, giving Democrats an effective 47. To win the chamber, Democrats need a net gain of at least four seats. In the House, current membership stands at 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats, one independent aligned with Republicans and two vacancies. A majority requires 218 seats, meaning even a small shift could change control.

The generic congressional ballot, which measures which party voters prefer nationally, shows Democrats ahead. RealClearPolling's average for October 9 to 30 puts Democrats at 51.8% and Republicans at 43.3%, a lead of 8.5 points. An NBC News poll conducted from October 28 to 30 showed Democrats leading 52 to 45. Emerson College, polling from October 24 to 26, found a 52 to 42 lead, Reuters/Ipsos 53 to 44, and CBS News 53 to 45. The Harvard-Harris survey showed a narrower margin of 52 to 48. Ballotpedia's polling index of October 30 also put the Democratic lead at about eight points.

But national numbers do not translate directly into seats. House members are elected in 435 separate districts, and a party can win the national popular vote while still losing individual contests.

In its October 30 ratings, the Cook Political Report classified 222 seats as leaning towards Democrats, 195 towards Republicans and 18 as toss-ups. These figures combine its "solid", "likely" and "lean" categories and are assessments of competitiveness, not projected results. Cook shifted several districts towards Democrats in the final week of October, and media coverage of its update discussed scenarios in which Democrats could gain between 12 and 25 seats. Inside Elections and Sabato's Crystal Ball also moved several Republican-held seats into more competitive categories during October.

Cook lists 14 Republican-held or vacated seats as toss-ups. They include California's 22nd district, held by David Valadao, Colorado's 5th, held by Jeff Crank, Iowa's 2nd, open after Ashley Hinson's Senate run, and Kentucky's 6th, vacated by Andy Barr. In Michigan, the 4th district of Bill Huizenga, the 7th of Tom Barrett and the 10th, left open by John James, are all in play. The list also includes Montana's 1st, vacated by Ryan Zinke, New York's 17th, held by Mike Lawler, Ohio's 7th, held by Max Miller, Pennsylvania's 1st, held by Brian Fitzpatrick, South Carolina's 1st, Nancy Mace's former seat, Texas's 15th, held by Monica De La Cruz, and Virginia's 1st, held by Rob Wittman.

Four Democratic-held or vacated seats are also toss-ups: Florida's 14th, held by Kathy Castor, Florida's 22nd, open after Lois Frankel's departure, North Carolina's 1st, held by Don Davis, and Texas's 35th, open after Greg Casar's departure. Cook rates three Democratic seats, Alabama's 2nd, Florida's 9th and Maine's 2nd, as leaning Republican, while placing Pennsylvania's 8th and Ohio's 9th in the "lean Democrat" column. In a report on October 31, The Washington Post cited Cook's analysis suggesting that in some scenarios Democrats could reach as many as 240 seats, though these remain projections, not results.

Of the 35 Senate seats up for election, Republicans hold 22 and Democrats 13. Cook rates six Republican seats and one Democratic seat as toss-ups. In Alaska, Republican Senator Dan Sullivan faces Democrat Mary Peltola, a former congresswoman. In Iowa, where Republican Joni Ernst is not running, Republican Ashley Hinson faces Democrat Josh Turek in a race some models show as extremely close. In Kansas, Republican Senator Roger Marshall faces Democrat Adam Hamilton, and in Maine, Republican Susan Collins faces Democrat Troy Jackson in a state Democrats carried in the 2024 presidential election.

In Michigan, following Democrat Gary Peters's retirement, Muslim American Abdul El-Sayed is defending the seat against Republican Mike Rogers. In Ohio's special election, Republican Senator Jon Husted faces former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown. In Texas, Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico are vying for John Cornyn's former seat, with several October polls showing a narrow gap. Six of these seven seats are held by Republicans; only Michigan is Democratic.

Elsewhere, Cook rates North Carolina, where former Democratic Governor Roy Cooper faces Republican Michael Whatley for the seat vacated by Thom Tillis, as "likely Democrat", making it one of the party's best pickup opportunities. Democrats must also defend their seats in Georgia, where Senator Jon Ossoff faces Republican Mike Collins, in New Hampshire, where Chris Pappas faces Republican John Sununu, and in Minnesota, where Peggy Flanagan faces Republican Michele Tafoya. Cook rates all three as leaning Democratic to varying degrees.

Other notable contests include Florida's special election, where Ashley Moody faces Democrat Angie Nixon, Nebraska, where Pete Ricketts faces independent Dan Osborn, South Carolina, where Lindsey Graham faces Democrat Annie Andrews, and Mississippi, where Cindy Hyde-Smith faces Scott Colom. Most of the remaining seats are rated safe for their current party. Analysts caution that control of the Senate will hinge on net gains and losses across many races, not on any single state.

In the race for governorships, Republicans currently hold 26 and Democrats 24. Several governors are not running because of term limits or other reasons, opening up a number of contests. Cook rates Georgia, Kansas and Nevada as toss-ups, while Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ) places Nevada and Ohio in that category, a difference that shows how much the analytical models diverge.

In Georgia, former Democratic Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms faces Republican Rick Jackson for the seat of term-limited Governor Brian Kemp. In Nevada, Republican Governor Joe Lombardo faces Democratic Attorney General Aaron Ford. In Kansas, Democrat Cindy Holscher faces Republican Ty Masterson; Cook rates the race a toss-up, while DDHQ says it leans Republican. In Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton faces Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a contest DDHQ calls a toss-up and Cook rates as leaning Democratic.

Other competitive races include Alaska, where ranked-choice voting applies, as well as Iowa, Wisconsin, Michigan, Arizona, Florida, Texas, Oregon and New Hampshire. Cook rates Republican-held Alaska, Iowa and Ohio as leaning Democratic. DDHQ's overall ratings place 20 of the 36 races on the Democratic side, seven safe, nine likely and four leaning, and 14 on the Republican side, five leaning, four likely and five safe, with two toss-ups. The 14 states not holding elections will keep their current governors.

Early voting has been heavy. According to On Point Politics' tracker as of November 1, more than 49.4 million ballots had been cast across 47 reporting states, about 23.1 million by mail and 26.3 million in person. In states that report party registration, registered Democrats made up about 40.4% of early voters and registered Republicans about 32.9%, with the rest independents or members of smaller parties. 

These figures reflect voters' registration, not how they voted. Large states such as Texas, California, Florida, North Carolina, Georgia and Washington do not all report the data in the same way, and the numbers offer no indication of how many more people will vote on Election Day.

At its core, the election is a referendum on the first two years of Trump's second term. Democrats are campaigning on the economy, healthcare, inflation, democratic institutions and federal policy, while Republicans are emphasising immigration, border security, taxes, energy and their party's governing priorities. The weight of these issues varies from state to state and district to district, and national polls, while pointing to a general trend, are no substitute for local contests.

The results across the House, the Senate and the governors' mansions will shape federal legislation, budgets, congressional oversight of the presidency and state-level governance for the next two years. 

For now, the available evidence shows Democrats ahead nationally in the race for the House, several Republican Senate seats under serious threat and the political balance of a number of states being tested in the governors' races. The real picture will emerge only once the votes are counted.

Other competitive races include Alaska, where ranked-choice voting applies, as well as Iowa, Wisconsin, Michigan, Arizona, Florida, Texas, Oregon and New Hampshire. Cook rates Republican-held Alaska, Iowa and Ohio as leaning Democratic. DDHQ's overall ratings place 20 of the 36 races on the Democratic side, seven safe, nine likely and four leaning, and 14 on the Republican side, five leaning, four likely and five safe, with two toss-ups. The 14 states not holding elections will keep their current governors.

Early voting has been heavy. According to On Point Politics' tracker as of November 1, more than 49.4 million ballots had been cast across 47 reporting states, about 23.1 million by mail and 26.3 million in person. In states that report party registration, registered Democrats made up about 40.4% of early voters and registered Republicans about 32.9%, with the rest independents or members of smaller parties.

These figures reflect voters' registration, not how they voted. Large states such as Texas, California, Florida, North Carolina, Georgia and Washington do not all report the data in the same way, and the numbers offer no indication of how many more people will vote on Election Day.

At its core, the election is a referendum on the first two years of Trump's second term. Democrats are campaigning on the economy, healthcare, inflation, democratic institutions and federal policy, while Republicans are emphasising immigration, border security, taxes, energy and their party's governing priorities. The weight of these issues varies from state to state and district to district, and national polls, while pointing to a general trend, are no substitute for local contests.

The results across the House, the Senate and the governors' mansions will shape federal legislation, budgets, congressional oversight of the presidency and state-level governance for the next two years.

For now, the available evidence shows Democrats ahead nationally in the race for the House, several Republican Senate seats under serious threat and the political balance of a number of states being tested in the governors' races. The real picture will emerge only once the votes are counted.

headline: Hilary Duff on Lizzie McGuire: 'I'm never singing that song'
subheadline: Hilary Duff reveals why she once refused to sing 'What Dreams Are Made Of'
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Hilary Duff has revealed she was “pretty done with Lizzie at that time”, saying she was exhausted by the character and once vowed never to sing the show’s theme song again.

The 39-year-old actress and singer made the comments in a cover story for Paper magazine.

She said the pace of the show had been relentless, recalling that it ran to 30 episodes in one year and 35 in the next.

Read more: Shia LaBeouf was 'beefing' with Hilary Duff on Disney: 'Hilary had no clue'

By the time she filmed The Lizzie McGuire Movie in Italy in 2003, she said she had had enough of the role, remembering thinking: “I’m f--ing done with you.”

Duff said that at the time she was “pretty exhausted by it” and was trying to build an identity as Hilary Duff, separate from Lizzie.

“I turned into a huge star. Everyone called me Lizzie,” she said. Then she vowed: “I’m never singing that song.” She also described how strange it was “being a child star and trying to cross that bridge into adulthood.”

Her feelings have changed.

Duff now performs What Dreams Are Made Of on her tour and re-recorded it for her 2026 EP Mine.

She first sang it live this year on the Small Rooms, Big Nerves Tour. Singing it now “feels so much better”, she said, adding that as a teenager she “wasn’t in my body yet”.

“When I perform it now, I’m like, oh, I’m in this,” she said. “I get to join the celebration of what it meant to people, and what it means to me now.”

The EP features seven re-recorded hits that first appeared as bonus tracks on vinyl variants of her 2025 album, Luck… or Something.

headline: Lake Bell and Rashid Johnson go Instagram official on Halloween
subheadline: Lake Bell confirms romance with artist Rashid Johnson in Halloween “hard launch”
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Lake Bell has confirmed she is dating the artist Rashid Johnson, sharing a Halloween selfie of the pair on Instagram.

The actress, 47, posted the picture on Saturday 31 October with the caption “Happy Hallow-hard launch.” Bell wore a black stole with a matching beret, while Johnson, 48, was in a classic charcoal-coloured tuxedo.

Neither has said any more about the relationship.

Friends were quick to cheer them on in the comments. Erinn Hayes wrote that Bell was “lookin fiiiiiiiine”, Reed Moreno posted heart-eye emojis, designer Gabriela Hearst called them a hot couple, and Alice Evans wrote “Holy hotness.”

Johnson is identified as an artist. He shares a son, Julius, with his ex-wife, Sheree Hovsepian.

It is not known how long the couple have been together, and the romance has been described as a whirlwind one. Bell has not said whether Johnson has met her family.

Bell was married to Scott Campbell for seven years, and the couple, who have two children, divorced in 2020.

They co-parent amicably.

In 2022, Bell said respect and communication are key, and in a later interview she described their bond as “army buddies”.

She was briefly linked to comedian Chris Rock in 2022, and has said she does not rush to introduce her children to new partners, with she and Campbell setting boundaries around it.

Bell stars in Chair Company.

headline: Dave Bautista reveals gaining 20 pounds of muscle for 'God of War'
subheadline: Dave Bautista hits 250 pounds to play Kratos in Prime Video’s 'God of War'
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Dave Bautista has revealed he has gained another 20 pounds of muscle to play Kratos in Prime Video’s God of War series, bringing him to 250 pounds.

The 57-year-old actor shared the update in a video on his Instagram story, with the text “Gained 20 lbs for GOW” and a “250” sticker, showing his current weight.

He wore a God of War T-shirt in the clip. It follows an earlier update in September, when he said he was three weeks into weight training again and had two more months “to get to where I need to be”.

Read more: ‘My Spy' stars Dave Bautista, Chloe Coleman open up on close friendship

Bautista signed on in August to play Kratos, replacing Ryan Hurst, who was originally cast but tore a bicep on set.

Hurst’s surgery would have pushed production into 2027. Reports said Hurst had gained about 40 pounds for the role, and that at least four episodes featuring him would need to be reshot.

Bautista’s deal closed on 20 August.

Filming began in Vancouver in February, and production will reshoot all scenes with Hurst using Bautista.

Bautista’s comments suggest filming will restart in November, though one report put the return in October.

No target weight has been confirmed by the production, although one speculative estimate puts him near 280 pounds.

Prime Video has given the series a two-season order, with both seasons set to shoot back-to-back.

It adapts the two most recent God of War games, in which Kratos raises his ten-year-old son, Atreus, played by Callum Vinson, while battling the gods of the Norse pantheon.

Kratos and Atreus set out to spread the ashes of Faye, the boy’s mother and Kratos’ wife. A release date has not been announced.

Bautista has transformed his body before.

In 2024, he said he had slimmed to about 240 pounds, down from 315 for Knock at the Cabin.

His other films include My Spy and The Wrecking Crew, and he next appears in Road House 2 and the Highlander reboot.

Read more: Dave Bautista says Daniel Craig 'always happy on Knives Out' compared to 'James Bond'

The 57-year-old actor shared the update in a video on his Instagram story, with the text “Gained 20 lbs for GOW” and a “250” sticker, showing his current weight.

He wore a God of War T-shirt in the clip. It follows an earlier update in September, when he said he was three weeks into weight training again and had two more months “to get to where I need to be”.

Read more: ‘My Spy' stars Dave Bautista, Chloe Coleman open up on close friendship

Bautista signed on in August to play Kratos, replacing Ryan Hurst, who was originally cast but tore a bicep on set.

Hurst’s surgery would have pushed production into 2027. Reports said Hurst had gained about 40 pounds for the role, and that at least four episodes featuring him would need to be reshot.

Bautista’s deal closed on 20 August.

Filming began in Vancouver in February, and production will reshoot all scenes with Hurst using Bautista.

Bautista’s comments suggest filming will restart in November, though one report put the return in October.

No target weight has been confirmed by the production, although one speculative estimate puts him near 280 pounds.

Prime Video has given the series a two-season order, with both seasons set to shoot back-to-back.

It adapts the two most recent God of War games, in which Kratos raises his ten-year-old son, Atreus, played by Callum Vinson, while battling the gods of the Norse pantheon.

Kratos and Atreus set out to spread the ashes of Faye, the boy’s mother and Kratos’ wife. A release date has not been announced.

Bautista has transformed his body before.

In 2024, he said he had slimmed to about 240 pounds, down from 315 for Knock at the Cabin.

His other films include My Spy and The Wrecking Crew, and he next appears in Road House 2 and the Highlander reboot.

Read more: Dave Bautista says Daniel Craig 'always happy on Knives Out' compared to 'James Bond'

headline: Moscow's Afghan blind spot
subheadline: Russia's posture suggests that denying Washington another strategic foothold is an important consideration
author: Amir Jahangir
article_text:
Afghanistan’s diplomatic rehabilitation is advancing faster than its accountability for terrorism. Russia sees an opportunity to contain Islamic State Khorasan and deny the US a renewed strategic foothold. Pakistan sees militant networks retaining the space to organise attacks across its border.

The gap between these priorities exposes the central weakness in regional engagement with the Taliban: Kabul is gaining legitimacy without delivering security to its neighbours.

Russia’s approach centres on Islamic State Khorasan, commonly called IS-K, and the possibility of renewed American strategic access. Pakistan confronts threats involving the TTP, the Baloch Liberation Army, Al-Qaeda and associated networks. These priorities overlap, but action against IS-K cannot become a substitute for addressing organisations attacking Pakistan.

Moscow’s concerns are understandable. The March 2024 Crocus City Hall attack showed the Islamic State threat’s reach. Russia became the first country to recognise the Taliban government in July 2025, after lifting its domestic ban on the movement. Its engagement reflects an assessment that Afghanistan’s rulers can help contain a common enemy.

That calculation has a fundamental weakness. The Taliban can fight an organisation threatening their rule while sheltering and sponsoring others attacking neighbouring countries. Hostility towards IS-K establishes neither a comprehensive counterterrorism policy nor a commitment to protecting Pakistan.

Geopolitical competition reinforces this selective approach. At the October 2025 Moscow Format consultations, regional participants opposed foreign military infrastructure in Afghanistan and neighbouring states. The declaration followed US President Donald Trump’s expressed interest in recovering Bagram airbase. Pakistan also participated, demonstrating that opposition to renewed foreign basing can coexist with differences over Taliban conduct.

Moscow’s posture suggests that denying Washington another strategic foothold is an important consideration. The danger arises when keeping America out becomes more urgent than compelling Kabul to dismantle terrorist infrastructure. Pakistan cannot be expected to absorb the security costs of another power’s geopolitical calculations.

UN findings illustrate the problem. The sanctions Monitoring Team’s August 2026 report described continued Taliban support for the TTP alongside escalating attacks against Pakistan. It also recorded Taliban operations that weakened IS-K capabilities, while IS-K attacks declined inside Afghanistan and increased in Pakistan. Security within Afghanistan, therefore, offered no assurance of regional safety.

The report recorded a member state’s assessment that BLA members trained alongside the TTP under Al-Qaeda trainers in Afghanistan. Another reported shared logistical facilitation networks between IS-K and the BLA. These attributed assessments require investigation. They also demonstrate why different ideologies should not obscure the possibility of shared infrastructure. Afghanistan’s finances expose another contradiction in the narrative of an isolated regime surviving independently. According to the World Bank, domestic revenue reached 272.4 billion afghani, approximately $4.03 billion, in FY2025. This represented 19.8% of GDP and a 12.7% increase over FY 2024. Domestic tax revenue contributed 109.1 billion afghani and customs revenue 69.6 billion afghani. The Taliban possess substantial collection capacity, even within a fragile economy.

Yet improved revenue collection has not delivered external self-sufficiency. The World Bank’s February 2026 Economic Monitor recorded exports of approximately $1.7 billion over the first eleven months of FY2025 and a merchandise trade deficit of $10.4 billion. These figures imply imports of roughly $12.1 billion. The deficit was 18% larger than a year earlier, highlighting Afghanistan’s dependence on external resources.

Narcotics remain part of this economic picture. Reuters, reporting UNODC findings released on October 29, said opium cultivation expanded to an estimated 43,300 hectares in 2026, more than four times the previous year’s area. Opium sales generated an estimated $525 million. Processing, trafficking and overseas distribution generate additional value.

International assistance remains another major resource. The Kabul Institute’s aid tracker, using data through September 30, 2026, reported $8 billion in confirmed humanitarian payments since August 2021, $3.78 billion committed but unpaid, and $94 million pledged. Separately, it identified $12.04 billion in development finance commitments across 1,208 project records, with payment information unavailable in the sources examined.

Its donor breakdown listed $1.64 billion paid by the US, alongside $1.14 billion committed but unpaid. Recorded payments included $1.03 billion from Britain, $645.9 million from Germany, $602.5 million from the Asian Development Bank and $499 million from Japan.

Western governments remain financial stakeholders, while Russia pursues diplomatic influence and regional powers seek trade and security benefits. Kabul can engage these interests simultaneously. Recognition by Moscow has not removed Afghanistan’s reliance on international assistance or resolved its structural economic weaknesses.

Humanitarian support must continue reaching Afghan families. Poor disclosure warrants stronger monitoring. Diplomatic privileges and benefits accruing directly to Taliban authorities, however, should carry explicit obligations to prevent terrorism and disrupt illicit finance.

Those obligations must cover every organisation using Afghan territory to threaten neighbours. Kabul should prevent recruitment, close training facilities, disrupt financing and cooperate on identifiable suspects. Regional forums need deadlines and verification arrangements, supported by evidence Pakistan can share through protected channels.

Russia and its partners also have economic reasons to insist. The proposed Uzbekistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan railway, TAPI pipeline and CASA-1000 electricity corridor require security throughout their routes. Connectivity cannot flourish while militant networks threaten workers and infrastructure.

Moscow can oppose an American military return while supporting firm action against the TTP, BLA and associated groups. Afghanistan’s revenues, external assistance and diplomatic access should support peaceful development and bring accountability. A settlement that protects Russian strategic interests while leaving Pakistan exposed will remain unstable, however warmly Kabul is received.

The writer is a public policy expert and leads the Country Partner Institute of the World Economic Forum in Pakistan. He tweets/posts @amirjahangir and can be reached at: [email protected]

Russia sees an opportunity to contain Islamic State Khorasan and deny the US a renewed strategic foothold. Pakistan sees militant networks retaining the space to organise attacks across its border.
The gap between these priorities exposes the central weakness in regional engagement with the Taliban: Kabul is gaining legitimacy without delivering security to its neighbours.

Russia’s approach centres on Islamic State Khorasan, commonly called IS-K, and the possibility of renewed American strategic access. Pakistan confronts threats involving the TTP, the Baloch Liberation Army, Al-Qaeda and associated networks. These priorities overlap, but action against IS-K cannot become a substitute for addressing organisations attacking Pakistan.

Moscow’s concerns are understandable. The March 2024 Crocus City Hall attack showed the Islamic State threat’s reach. Pakistan also participated, demonstrating that opposition to renewed foreign basing can coexist with differences over Taliban conduct.

Security within Afghanistan, therefore, offered no assurance of regional safety.

The report recorded a member state’s assessment that BLA members trained alongside the TTP under Al-Qaeda trainers in Afghanistan. Another reported shared logistical facilitation networks between IS-K and the BLA. These attributed assessments require investigation. They also demonstrate why different ideologies should not obscure the possibility of shared infrastructure. headline: Nine people dead in Learjet crash in south Florida, say officials
subheadline: Videos on social media show jet slamming into the ground next to a road and exploding
author: Reuters
article_text:
Videos on social media show jet slamming into ground.
NTSB launches investigation into crash.
Air traffic control recording captures final moments.

A Learjet crashed on Sunday afternoon in a residential area in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board, US transportation officials said.

The private jet had taken off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement.

Videos on social media showed the jet slamming into the ground next to a road and exploding.

"It was a big-time tragedy that happened," Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said at a press conference near the crash site in Lake Worth Beach. "When you see that video, it's a jarring thing. It was like a missile coming down, and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere."

The National Transportation Safety Board said it had launched an investigation into the crash, which Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called a "horrific tragedy."

FAA records list the Bombardier-made BBDb.TO Learjet 60's owner as a Delaware corporation. Canada-based Bombardier said it would fully support the investigation and cooperate as needed.

The crash left a "massive crater" by the road near the entrance to a mobile home park, Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores said at the news conference. About 600 people were being evacuated from the area and relocated to two shelters in the county, Flores said.

Heavy rainfall and thunderstorms were occurring in the area at the time, forecaster AccuWeather said in a statement.

An audio recording from a Miami air traffic control center posted on LiveATC, a site that broadcasts air traffic control communications, captured the plane's final moments before the crash in unusual detail.

At first, someone in the plane's cockpit reported to an air traffic controller that they were "managing the ice" but faced "moderate" turbulence and were seeking "better rides".

Less than a minute later, the person said "Mayday, mayday," reporting that the plane was suddenly descending at a rate of 10,000 feet per minute.

Seconds later, the person said they were declaring an emergency, with the rate of descent accelerating to 20,000 feet per minute.

Less than 20 seconds later, the person said: "We're going to crash into the ground" before saying that the descent rate had reached 22,000 feet per minute as the plane started banking.

About 35 seconds after the initial mayday announcement, the last thing heard from the cockpit was a rapidly spoken "We're out of time."

Flight tracking website Flightradar24 said data showed the vertical descent rate at one point exceeded 32,000 feet per minute.

headline: Haley Stevens endorses Republican candidate in critical US Senate race
subheadline: Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed says "unbothered" by Stevens' announcement of endorsing Mike Rogers
author: AFP
article_text:
Most polls put El-Sayed narrowly ahead of Rogers.
Democrats term Stevens' move "despicable betrayal".
US President Trump praises Stevens for "bravery".

WASHINGTON: Democratic congresswoman in Michigan, Haley Stevens, broke ranks with her party on Sunday to endorse the Republican candidate in her state's key US Senate race against left-wing progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed.

In a startling display of party infighting just two days before the November 3 midterm election, Stevens, who lost a bruising primary to El-Sayed in August despite being backed by the Democratic establishment, said she was endorsing Republican Mike Rogers.

"This is a very close election, we all know that, but Abdul made very clear that I was not welcome in his campaign," she told reporters when announcing her endorsement.

Democrats are seeking to wrest control of both chambers of Congress from Republicans in Tuesday's midterms, with the Michigan race a key battleground that could help them flip control of the Senate.

Sunday's statement from Stevens was illustrative of internal divisions within the party, with left-wing candidates often clashing with the Democratic Party's establishment core on key issues.

El-Sayed, a candidate with a rising national profile, has been a vocal critic of the US alliance with Israel, calling for a halt to arms sales to that country.

On Sunday, El-Sayed said he was unbothered by the Stevens announcement.

"At the end of the day, I actually don't think about Haley Stevens. I think about the 9,999,998 people who are not those two," he said, referring to Stevens and Rogers.

"Because you know what, I am just less interested in the politics of it all than I am in the policy of it all."

Democratic backlash against Stevens was fast and furious.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called her move a "despicable betrayal," while the chair of the Michigan Democrats' black caucus said Stevens "revealed herself to be a sellout" who has lost her way.

If elected, El-Sayed would be the first Muslim member of the US Senate.

US President Donald Trump has often singled him out for abuse on the campaign trail, calling him a "jihadist" and claiming he wants to impose Islamic law on the United States.

Trump quickly praised Stevens for her "bravery," posting on his Truth Social platform that "Haley said what few people are willing to say."

Most polls put El-Sayed narrowly ahead of Rogers going into election day.

WASHINGTON: Democratic congresswoman in Michigan, Haley Stevens, broke ranks with her party on Sunday to endorse the Republican candidate in her state's key US Senate race against left-wing progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed.

In a startling display of party infighting just two days before the November 3 midterm election, Stevens, who lost a bruising primary to El-Sayed in August despite being backed by the Democratic establishment, said she was endorsing Republican Mike Rogers.

"This is a very close election, we all know that, but Abdul made very clear that I was not welcome in his campaign," she told reporters when announcing her endorsement.

Democrats are seeking to wrest control of both chambers of Congress from Republicans in Tuesday's midterms, with the Michigan race a key battleground that could help them flip control of the Senate.

Sunday's statement from Stevens was illustrative of internal divisions within the party, with left-wing candidates often clashing with the Democratic Party's establishment core on key issues.

El-Sayed, a candidate with a rising national profile, has been a vocal critic of the US alliance with Israel, calling for a halt to arms sales to that country.

On Sunday, El-Sayed said he was unbothered by the Stevens announcement.

"At the end of the day, I actually don't think about Haley Stevens. I think about the 9,999,998 people who are not those two," he said, referring to Stevens and Rogers.

"Because you know what, I am just less interested in the politics of it all than I am in the policy of it all."

Democratic backlash against Stevens was fast and furious.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called her move a "despicable betrayal," while the chair of the Michigan Democrats' black caucus said Stevens "revealed herself to be a sellout" who has lost her way.

If elected, El-Sayed would be the first Muslim member of the US Senate.

US President Donald Trump has often singled him out for abuse on the campaign trail, calling him a "jihadist" and claiming he wants to impose Islamic law on the United States.

Trump quickly praised Stevens for her "bravery," posting on his Truth Social platform that "Haley said what few people are willing to say."

Most polls put El-Sayed narrowly ahead of Rogers going into election day.

headline: 'I'm A Celebrity' star Wayne Sleep breaks silence on cancer diagnosis
subheadline: 'I'm A Celebrity' star Wayne Sleep has shared a devastating news, revealing that he has been diagnosed with cancer
author: Web Desk
article_text:
I'm A Celebrity star Wayne Sleep has shared a devastating news, revealing that he has been diagnosed with cancer.

The former ballet dancer and reality star, 78, updated his followers on his health on Sunday, revealing that he had been undergoing treatment.

Noting he 'hadn't been looking like his usual self', Wayne said that he is 'on the mend' and the treatment seems to be working, and he is now 'looking to the future.'

READ MORE: Mariella Frostrup set for 'I'm A Celebrity' after Jesy Nelson pulls out of ITV show

In a post on Instagram, Wayne said: 'A few people have commented that I haven't been looking quite my usual self recently, so I thought I would share an update.

'Since the summer, I have been undergoing treatment for cancer.'I'm pleased to say that the treatment appears to be working, and I am on the mend thanks to all at the Royal Marsden and am looking forward to getting back to full strength.

'I'm in good spirits and feeling positive about the future. Thank you to everyone for their kindness and concern.

'Photo here on Friday at Kew Gardens looking at the wonderful Henry Moore exhibition. Much love, Wayne x.'

Wayne's diagnosis comes 11 years after he battled prostate cancer, and he previously told The Mirror in 2016 that he first noticed signs when his PSA levels were raised back in 2010.

The dancer previously appeared on the ITV show in 2003, and has also appeared on Celebrity Big Brother and the BBC series The Real Marigold Hotel.

READ MORE: Chloe Burrows selected for 'I'm A Celebrity' after 'Love island' success

headline: Ciara Mageean, two-time Olympian, European 1500m champion dies aged 34
subheadline: Mageean represented Ireland at the 2016 Rio Olympics and 2020 Tokyo Games
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Ciara Mageean, an Irish trailblazer athlete, two-time Olympian, and European 1500m gold medallist, passed away at age 34 after a battle with cancer.

The Irish middle-distance runner, a native from Portaferry in Northern Ireland died at 6:30 a.m. on Sunday, November 1, her family confirmed in a social media post.

Mageean was considered one of the most gifted Irish athletes, with ace talent in the 1500m event.

She represented Ireland at the 2016 Rio Olympics and 2020 Tokyo Games.

Mageean didn’t participate in the 2024 Paris Games because of an Achilles injury.

Who was Ciara Mageean?

An Irish trailblazer athlete, she started her career in hurling for a local club Portaferry GAC, but soon realised her dream of representing Ireland at the Olympics.

Her running skillset was evident from her accomplishments at a junior level.

She won 1500m silvers at the 2010 World Junior Championship and the 2011 European Junior Championships.

Mageean's hopes of making her Olympic debut at London 2012 were dashed after she suffered a gruesome ankle injury.

She underwent a procedure in 2013 and, a year later, made a stunning comeback winning the 1500m title in July 2014.

Mageean made her Olympic debut in 2016, but she withdrew the 1500m heat at the semi-final stage after suffering an ankle injury.

After a series of disappointments, Mageean finally secured the big win of her career at the 2024 European Championships in Rome.

She was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer in May 2025.

Mageean tied the knot in October to her long-time partner Thomas Moran in a ceremony held in Belfast.

headline: King Charles finally gets his umbrella — watch his hilarious reaction
subheadline: King Charles 'where's the umbrella' moment in Caribbean rain catches attention
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles finally got his umbrella after repeatedly asking, "Where's the umbrella?" and showing his anger in the Caribbean rain.

The monarch and Queen Camilla took part in the Independence Day celebrations in Antigua, but the weather had other plans.

At Sir Vivian Richards Cricket Stadium, the royal couple joined officials marking Antigua and Barbuda’s 45th anniversary of independence.

READ MORE: Queen Camilla makes Caribbean return in vibrant turquoise joining King Charles

However, at the nation’s annual independence parade, a torrential downpour interrupted the event.

Queen Camilla escaped the scene after she was given a transparent dome umbrella. King Charles was getting drenched by the rain, which sparked his anger.

Later, a member of the team presented a black umbrella to the monarch.

Joking about his situation, the King told Antigua's Prime Minister, "I think I'm about to grow watercress on my suit."

READ MORE: King Charles, Prince Harry's 'secret' deal sparks public fury

According to a video released by Palace, the monarch appeared in a good mood after facing an unexpected weather situation.

headline: ICC penalises Pakistan for slow over-rate in tri-series final
subheadline: Skipper Shaheen Shah Afridi admits slow over-rate offence and accepts ICC sanction
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Pakistan have been fined 5% of their match fee for maintaining a slow over-rate during the final of the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series against Sri Lanka in Lahore on Saturday.

The hosts were found to be one over short after time allowances were taken into account by match referee Jeff Crowe of the Emirates ICC Elite Panel.

The offence falls under Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which deals with minimum over-rate offences. Under the provision, players are fined 5% of their match fee for every over their team fails to bowl within the allotted time.

On-field umpires Ahsan Raza and Wayne Knights, third umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid and fourth umpire Rashid Riaz levelled the charge.

Pakistan captain Shaheen Shah Afridi pleaded guilty and accepted the proposed sanction, avoiding a formal hearing.

headline: Jack Campbell carted off with neck injury as All-Pro's status remains uncertain
subheadline: The Lions inked Campbell last May on a four-year contract extension that will last until 2030 season
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Lions All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell was carted off the field early in the fourth quarter in the Week 8 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

He was shifted to a local hospital and reportedly will be under observation overnight for a neck injury.

The Detroit Lions won the game 19-15 over the Vikings on Sunday, November 1, 2026.

Campbell was face down on the turf and was not moving after hitting tight end T.J. Hockenson for his third tackle of the game.

He was evaluated by medical staff before being strapped to a backboard and carted off the field.

Detroit’s entire team and most of the coaching staff surrounded the cart before it shifted Campbell off the field for further examination.

Vikings head coach, Dan Campbell updated on Campbell injury postgame, saying, “We’re thinking about him.”

The former Iowa star was the No. 18 pick of the 2023 NFL Draft by the Detroit Lions.

Campbell was selected as an All-Pro selection last season after he became the first NFL player in seven years to have posted 150-plus tackles and five sacks and three forced fumbles.

The Lions inked Campbell last May on a four-year contract extension that will last until 2030 season.

The Lions will travel to Miami to face the Dolphins in Week 9 on Sunday, November 8, 2026.

headline: Queen Camilla under scrutiny after Palace issues update on key meeting
subheadline: Royal family releases update on King Charles, Queen Camilla after rain mishap
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Buckingham Palace issued a major update on King Charles' key meeting with West Indies cricket legends, but the royal fans have one major complaint.

A photo has been released showcasing the beaming monarch and Queen Camilla posing with Sir Curtly Ambrose, Sir Richie Richardson, Sir Andy Roberts and Sir Viv Richards at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium.

The moment was captured in Antigua following an Independence Day parade at the venue.

READ MORE: King Charles finally gets his umbrella — watch his hilarious reaction

The same event was interrupted due to a torrential downpour. The Queen escaped with an umbrella, leaving King Charles behind, soaking.

This moment troubled many netizens, who argued that the Queen could have offered the same umbrella to the monarch.

In the comments section, one social media user said on Instagram, "And Camilla ran away with the umbrella."

"Can a woman who leaves the king alone in the rain be a queen?" another penned.

Another video was released by Palace, featuring the King, who "opened the 'One Commonwealth, One Team' Exhibition Cricket Match Series with the ceremonial coin toss at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium in Antigua and Barbuda, a fixture the Sustainable Markets Initiative is proud to support.

"It was a moment that captured the spirit of CHOGM 2026: bringing together leaders and young talent through the shared language of sport, on the very ground that carries the name of one of cricket's greats."

headline: Meghan Markle in tears and under fire as new scandal shatters her silence
subheadline: Meghan's brief statement was enough to ignite debate
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Meghan Markle's first and only statement on the latest update about her estranged father's scandal has fueled intense speculation about the Duchess's next move.

The brief statement was enough to ignite debate. Some critics were quick to target the Duchess, claiming she may try to start a new conversation and shift the narrative away from the royal family, focusing instead on how difficult it was for her to go through her own family struggles.

Undoubtedly, she has broken her silence on years-old correspondence to clarify her position and explain one of the reasons she cut ties with her estranged father.

READ MORE: Shocking Palace connection in Meghan's father case comes to light

But according to insiders, this was not the only ordeal the former Suits star had to face long before her marriage into the royal family.

Meanwhile, one source claims Prince Harry's wife cannot stop crying over the situation, amid growing backlash about a 'MasterChef' TV role.

Meghan might have known that the truth about her father would one day become public. She waited for it to be revealed on its own, otherwise, the blame for exposing her own father could have brought her even more negative publicity.

She is said to be struggling emotionally amid her estranged father's scandal. The claims have emerged just as Meghan faces criticism over her appointment as co-host of Junior MasterChef Australia, with hundreds reportedly signing a petition demanding her removal from the program.

The allegations against her father have left her deeply distressed as she focuses on her two young children. Being a mother herself makes the allegations particularly distressing.

There is no doubt that the thought of any child being subjected to something so horrific is almost unbearable for her.

Now, Meghan needs to make a conscious decision to protect her peace by stepping away from the constant cycle of headlines and online speculation surrounding her father.

She knows what is better for her, but at this moment, creating some distance would help her protect her well-being and her family's happiness.

headline: China's Xi says Middle East should not become battleground for great power rivalry
subheadline: Beijing willing to strengthen communication with Arab countries to work together towards restoring peace, says Xi
author: Reuters
article_text:
China's Xi calls for lasting peace in Middle East.
Sultan on first trip to China by an Omani leader.
Oman seeks joint investment funds with China.

BEIJING/DUBAI: The Middle East and Gulf region should not become a battleground for great-power rivalry, and China is willing to work with Arab nations to achieve lasting peace, Chinese President Xi Jinping told Oman's sultan on Monday.

China has traditionally played a low-key diplomatic role in the Middle East, but has stepped up efforts to try to help end tensions amid the US-Israeli war on Iran, which has snarled the Strait of Hormuz and driven up global energy and shipping costs.

Xi told Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said that the world is undergoing "profound changes unseen in a century."

"The Middle East Gulf region should not become an arena for great-power rivalry and geopolitical conflict. Peace and stability in the region require joint nurturing and protection by all parties," Xi said, according to China's Foreign Ministry.

China has consistently been committed to stopping the war, and hopes to contribute "wisdom and solutions to resolving the region's security dilemmas," he added.

China is willing to strengthen communication and coordination with Arab countries, including the Gulf Cooperation Council states, to work together toward restoring peace and achieving lasting stability and security, Xi said.

Last week, China's Foreign Ministry said the country will soon be dispatching its special envoys to the Middle East to promote engagement and de-escalation.

First China trip

Haitham arrived in Beijing on Sunday for a two-day visit, the first by an Omani head of state since the countries established ties in 1978.

Haitham told Xi his government had deep appreciation for China's positions on key issues concerning the region, Omani state media reported.

"We believe that development and stability are inextricably linked," he said.

"The prosperity of nations requires an environment defined by security, peace, respect for state sovereignty, and adherence to international law — an environment where disputes are resolved through peaceful means."

He also said Oman was open to entering into a preferential bilateral trade and investment agreement with China.

"We are confident that such an agreement would open new avenues for trade and investment, facilitate and enhance commercial and investment exchanges between our two nations," Haitham said.

China is Oman's largest trade partner, with tourism and business links boosted by direct flights between Beijing and Muscat since November last year.

Oman, which exports crude oil and energy products to China, has also been looking to further develop its renewable energy supply chains and digital commerce.

The Omani leader, who was welcomed on the tarmac in Beijing by People's Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng, also emphasised cooperation between investment and financial institutions.

headline: 'Love Island' Sam Bird announces arrival of first child with wife Kailah
subheadline: The reality star kept his wife's pregnancy under wraps and stunned fans with a heartfelt announcement he shared on Instagram on Sunday
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Love Island star Sam Bird has shared delightful news, revealing that he has welcomed his first child with his wife, Kailah.

The reality star kept his wife's pregnancy under wraps and stunned fans with a heartfelt announcement he shared on Instagram on Sunday.

Sam shared that he had welcomed a baby boy named Sunny, sharing a video showing himself and Kailah with their son in his newly decorated nursery.

READ MORE: Samie Elishi, Tyrique Hyde share exciting baby news with sweet announcement

Fans rallied to share their best wishes with the couple.

They wrote: 'Whaaaaaat??? Baby bird is already here and we didn't even know!!'

'Omg this is amazing. I'm so happy for the both of you! Yall deserve all the smiles;'

'I knew she disappeared for a reason!! Congratulations mama!! Cannot wait to watch you guys grow in this next chapter.'

During his appearance on Love Island in 2018, Sam was briefly linked with Georgia Steele after leaving the show. However, he later called off their relationship, accusing her of cheating.

Sam went on to find love with now-wife Kailah, who he announced he was engaged to after eight months of dating, and they tied the knot in 2022.
