headline: China's robot makers have mastered the moves, now comes race for brains
subheadline: Firms race to train robots using real-world data and simulations
author: Reuters
article_text:
After years of building humanoid robots capable of running, dancing and performing backflips, Chinese companies are pouring resources into a different challenge: developing the AI that could make those machines useful across a wider range of jobs.

The shift is fuelling an investment boom in embodied AI, a field focused on software that allows robots to understand their surroundings, learn unfamiliar tasks and adapt without having to be programmed for every job.

Chinese embodied AI companies raised 93.5 ‌billion yuan ($13 billion) across 322 deals in the first half of 2026, five times the amount a year earlier, according to data research firm ITjuzi. Funding is increasingly reaching specialist developers of robot intelligence alongside manufacturers.

As competition drives down hardware prices, robot makers have "concluded that the margin won't come from the hardware but from the brain," said Dermot McGrath, founder of Shanghai-based technology consultancy ZenGen Labs.

The emerging sector is opening a new front in US-China tech rivalry. American companies lead in some advanced robot AI systems, while Chinese developers hope their manufacturing strength and access to real-world training data will help them challenge their US competitors, according to Reuters interviews with founders and top executives at five Chinese robotics firms, as well as industry analysts.

The country that best combines AI with machines could gain an advantage in automating factories and logistics, potentially reshaping industrial productivity and the global market for robotics technology.

"The brain is indeed the weakest link in the complete robotics stack," said Spirit AI co-founder Gao Yang.

Race for intelligence

American startups, including Physical Intelligence, Skild AI and Generalist, are developing software intended to teach robots different skills without ⁠extensive retraining.

Generalist says its GEN-1.5 model completed around 60% of simple tasks after viewing a demonstration lasting between 3 and 12 seconds. China's X Square has published research showing robots acquiring handling skills from a single human video without retraining the model for each task.

"The leading American labs are setting a demanding benchmark, particularly in how quickly robots can acquire and reuse skills," said robotics consultant Georg Stieler, who considers China's strongest startups credible competitors.

While US developers benefit from advanced AI research and greater access to powerful computing chips, Chinese companies can work closely with robot manufacturers and industrial customers to test and improve their systems.

Specialist Chinese startups, including X Square, Galaxea and Spirit AI, have each reached valuations of roughly $3 billion, according to company disclosures.

"We want robots to shift from being driven by code to being driven by common sense," said X Square co-founder and COO Yang Qian.

Established manufacturers are investing too. Hong Kong-listed UBTech advertised a chief scientist position overseeing AI model development with compensation of up to 124 million yuan ($18 million), including equity and benefits. Hangzhou-based Unitree, one of the world's largest humanoid robot makers by shipments, has about 30 researchers developing AI that predicts how objects behave, according to a person briefed by the company.

Unitree did not respond to a request for comment.

The training race

Unlike chatbots, which learn from vast quantities of internet text, robots need examples of physical interactions, from gripping objects to handling flexible wires.

Chinese companies are pursuing different approaches to collecting that information, with some employing people to demonstrate tasks, others using computer simulations, and some combining both. The field remains crowded, with no company establishing itself as the clear leader.

Spirit AI has hired around 1,000 people to record everyday and industrial activities, Gao said. ACE Robotics uses wearable sensors to capture workers' movements and grip forces ‌in stores and hotels.

Ant ⁠Group's robotics unit Robbyant said it trained a model using 160,000 hours of material, including 50,000 hours of human-guided robot movements. It also trained software on 20 robot configurations from 17 brands, aiming to use the same AI across different machines.

DexForce is taking another approach, using computer-generated environments to teach robots. Chief operating officer Nicole Yang said the company can prepare some industrial tasks for deployment within 6 to 8 hours and reported success rates above 99.9% in specified precision operations.

But simulations cannot perfectly reproduce physical interactions, said Jerry Wang of spatial intelligence company Manycore Tech, which designs simulated environments for AI training.

"Data quality is more important than data diversity, and more important than simply collecting data at massive scale," X Square's Yang said.

Chinese robot firms also face additional headwinds, including shortages of advanced Nvidia chips due to US export controls, and a squeeze on IPO funding amid regulatory concerns over inflated valuations and overcrowding.

As robots become more powerful, the shortage of advanced chips will become a serious problem ⁠for China's embodied AI industry, said Zhu Mingxuan, who leads development of JoyIn Technology's Aether robot AI.

From training to work

JoyIn and other developers are already testing whether their software can enable robots to tackle unfamiliar problems.

Zhu described an experiment in which a robot repeatedly failed to place headphones in a cupboard beyond its reach.

article_html:
After years of building humanoid robots capable of running, dancing and performing backflips, Chinese companies are pouring resources into a different challenge: developing the AI that could make those machines useful across a wider range of jobs.

The shift is fuelling an investment boom in embodied AI, a field focused on software that allows robots to understand their surroundings, learn unfamiliar tasks and adapt without having to be programmed for every job.

Chinese embodied AI companies raised 93.5 ‌billion yuan ($13 billion) across 322 deals in the first half of 2026, five times the amount a year earlier, according to data research firm ITjuzi. Funding is increasingly reaching specialist developers of robot intelligence alongside manufacturers.

As competition drives down hardware prices, robot makers have "concluded that the margin won't come from the hardware but from the brain," said Dermot McGrath, founder of Shanghai-based technology consultancy ZenGen Labs.

The emerging sector is opening a new front in US-China tech rivalry. American companies lead in some advanced robot AI systems, while Chinese developers hope their manufacturing strength and access to real-world training data will help them challenge their US competitors, according to Reuters interviews with founders and top executives at five Chinese robotics firms, as well as industry analysts.

The country that best combines AI with machines could gain an advantage in automating factories and logistics, potentially reshaping industrial productivity and the global market for robotics technology.

"The brain is indeed the weakest link in the complete robotics stack," said Spirit AI co-founder Gao Yang.

Race for intelligence

American startups, including Physical Intelligence, Skild AI and Generalist, are developing software intended to teach robots different skills without ⁠extensive retraining.

Generalist says its GEN-1.5 model completed around 60% of simple tasks after viewing a demonstration lasting between 3 and 12 seconds. China's X Square has published research showing robots acquiring handling skills from a single human video without retraining the model for each task.

"The leading American labs are setting a demanding benchmark, particularly in how quickly robots can acquire and reuse skills," said robotics consultant Georg Stieler, who considers China's strongest startups credible competitors.

While US developers benefit from advanced AI research and greater access to powerful computing chips, Chinese companies can work closely with robot manufacturers and industrial customers to test and improve their systems.

Specialist Chinese startups, including X Square, Galaxea and Spirit AI, have each reached valuations of roughly $3 billion, according to company disclosures.

"We want robots to shift from being driven by code to being driven by common sense," said X Square co-founder and COO Yang Qian.

Established manufacturers are investing too. Hong Kong-listed UBTech advertised a chief scientist position overseeing AI model development with compensation of up to 124 million yuan ($18 million), including equity and benefits. Hangzhou-based Unitree, one of the world's largest humanoid robot makers by shipments, has about 30 researchers developing AI that predicts how objects behave, according to a person briefed by the company.

Unitree did not respond to a request for comment.

The training race

Unlike chatbots, which learn from vast quantities of internet text, robots need examples of physical interactions, from gripping objects to handling flexible wires.

Chinese companies are pursuing different approaches to collecting that information, with some employing people to demonstrate tasks, others using computer simulations, and some combining both. The field remains crowded, with no company establishing itself as the clear leader.

Spirit AI has hired around 1,000 people to record everyday and industrial activities, Gao said. ACE Robotics uses wearable sensors to capture workers' movements and grip forces ‌in stores and hotels.

Ant ⁠Group's robotics unit Robbyant said it trained a model using 160,000 hours of material, including 50,000 hours of human-guided robot movements. It also trained software on 20 robot configurations from 17 brands, aiming to use the same AI across different machines.

DexForce is taking another approach, using computer-generated environments to teach robots. Chief operating officer Nicole Yang said the company can prepare some industrial tasks for deployment within 6 to 8 hours and reported success rates above 99.9% in specified precision operations.

But simulations cannot perfectly reproduce physical interactions, said Jerry Wang of spatial intelligence company Manycore Tech, which designs simulated environments for AI training.

"Data quality is more important than data diversity, and more important than simply collecting data at massive scale," X Square's Yang said.

Chinese robot firms also face additional headwinds, including shortages of advanced Nvidia chips due to US export controls, and a squeeze on IPO funding amid regulatory concerns over inflated valuations and overcrowding.

As robots become more powerful, the shortage of advanced chips will become a serious problem ⁠for China's embodied AI industry, said Zhu Mingxuan, who leads development of JoyIn Technology's Aether robot AI.

From training to work

JoyIn and other developers are already testing whether their software can enable robots to tackle unfamiliar problems.

Zhu described an experiment in which a robot repeatedly failed to place headphones in a cupboard beyond its reach.

Then engineers showed it videos of how people managed the task, and the robot pushed a box towards the cupboard and tried stepping onto it, Zhu said.

"Every time it was exploring a different behaviour," she said.

Real-world deployments in China leave no room for improvisation. Battery maker CATL said Spirit AI robots connect flexible wires during battery-pack testing at its Zhongzhou ⁠plant, reporting insertion success above 99%. Robbyant said its robots handle orders in two Shanghai pharmacies, with staff checking medicines before dispatch.

But the longer-term prize is software capable of learning new jobs without extensive adaptation. Success will depend how the same AI performs across different customers and workplaces and that will require companies to train increasingly powerful models with advanced chips.

Chinese companies are trying to reduce their computing requirements through more efficient models, synthetic data and simulations, while domestic chipmakers, including Huawei, are developing alternatives to Nvidia hardware. It remains unclear how far those efforts can offset the shortage.

'Chatgpt moment'

Unitree founder Wang ⁠Xingxing said last month the company had tested OpenAI's GPT-6 on robots with encouraging results.

He said GPT-7, if released next year, could bring robotics its own "ChatGPT moment" — a step-change in capability akin to ChatGPT's 2022 launch, which turned generative AI into a mainstream consumer and business technology.

Wang said he would consider that threshold reached when robots were able to complete 80% of tasks in 80% of unfamiliar environments from spoken instructions.

But consultant Stieler said a breakthrough in demonstrations would not necessarily mean robots were ready for broad commercial use.

"If the question is when a model first handles a broad range of unfamiliar tasks in demonstrations, the optimists may well be right," he said. "If the question is when a customer can count on it, I would add years, not months."

"Data quality is more important than data diversity, and more important than simply collecting data at massive scale," X Square's Yang said.

Chinese robot firms also face additional headwinds, including shortages of advanced Nvidia chips due to US export controls, and a squeeze on IPO funding amid regulatory concerns over inflated valuations and overcrowding.

As robots become more powerful, the shortage of advanced chips will become a serious problem ⁠for China's embodied AI industry, said Zhu Mingxuan, who leads development of JoyIn Technology's Aether robot AI.
From training to work
JoyIn and other developers are already testing whether their software can enable robots to tackle unfamiliar problems.
Zhu described an experiment in which a robot repeatedly failed to place headphones in a cupboard beyond its reach.
Then engineers showed it videos of how people managed the task, and the robot pushed a box towards the cupboard and tried stepping onto it, Zhu said.
"Every time it was exploring a different behaviour," she said.

Real-world deployments in China leave no room for improvisation. Battery maker CATL said Spirit AI robots connect flexible wires during battery-pack testing at its Zhongzhou ⁠plant, reporting insertion success above 99%. Robbyant said its robots handle orders in two Shanghai pharmacies, with staff checking medicines before dispatch.

But the longer-term prize is software capable of learning new jobs without extensive adaptation. Success will depend how the same AI performs across different customers and workplaces and that will require companies to train increasingly powerful models with advanced chips.

Chinese companies are trying to reduce their computing requirements through more efficient models, synthetic data and simulations, while domestic chipmakers, including Huawei, are developing alternatives to Nvidia hardware. It remains unclear how far those efforts can offset the shortage.
'Chatgpt moment'
Unitree founder Wang ⁠Xingxing said last month the company had tested OpenAI's GPT-6 on robots with encouraging results.

He said GPT-7, if released next year, could bring robotics its own "ChatGPT moment" — a step-change in capability akin to ChatGPT's 2022 launch, which turned generative AI into a mainstream consumer and business technology.
Wang said he would consider that threshold reached when robots were able to complete 80% of tasks in 80% of unfamiliar environments from spoken instructions.
But consultant Stieler said a breakthrough in demonstrations would not necessarily mean robots were ready for broad commercial use.

"If the question is when a model first handles a broad range of unfamiliar tasks in demonstrations, the optimists may well be right," he said. "If the question is when a customer can count on it, I would add years, not months."

headline: Harriet Phillips shuts down Meghan's claims about Princess Kate
subheadline: Princess Kate receives special honour from new member of the royal family
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Catherine, the Princess of Wales, has been honoured by a new family member, and the praise 'debunked' old claims made by Meghan Markle against the future Queen.

Princess Anne's daughter-in-law, Harriet Phillips, stated she can turn to Princess Kate for any type of guidance.

Apparently, this is a very contrasting statement to the Duchess of Sussex, who has often 'suggested' that Catherine has an unwelcoming nature.

READ MORE: William, Kate share George, Charlotte, Louis photo amid Halloween buzz

In conversation with Hello! Magazine, Peter Phillips' wife was asked about her first meeting with the Prince and Princess of Wales and their children.

Harriet shared, "I've had an incredible experience being welcomed in. We happened to be on holiday at the same place in the Scilly Isles.

"It was great because the children were all jumping into the water at the same time. It was very casual, but there is a clear level of respect there."

Harriet hailed the Princess of Wales for her kind and friendly nature.

She said, "I can look to Catherine for advice and guidance. She's very open-hearted, and I would always feel comfortable asking her if I needed advice about something."

READ MORE: Princess Kate receives gracious message from Harry ahead of key event

It is important to note that Harriet tied the knot with Peter Phillips on June 6. King Charles, Queen Camilla, the Prince and Princess of Wales, among other key royals, were present at the joyful event.

headline: Princess Anne family gets big boost as daughter-in-law lands noble role
subheadline: Peter Phillip's wife Harriet makes exciting announcement about new journey
author: Web Desk
article_text:
It is time for Princess Anne and her family to celebrate as the daughter-in-law Harriet Phillips has been honoured with a prestigious new role.

Peter Phillips' wife disclosed in conversation with Hello! Magazine that she has taken on a role as the patron of Home-Start Cotswolds.

Harriet stepped back from the NHS after fulfilling her role as a specialist nurse to champion vulnerable families and early years mental health.

READ MORE: Harriet Phillips shuts down Meghan's claims about Princess Kate

The new noble job is an extension of her years-long service as a medical expert.

Harriet first opened up about how becoming parents is equally a wonderful and overwhelming experience of life.

Just like Princess Kate, Harriet emphasised how important it is to look after a baby's well-being at an early age, and that is possible if the parents are doing well.

She added, "Having worked with Home-Start as a specialist nurse in Gloucestershire, I had seen its impact first-hand and referred families to it.

"Home-Start approached me to ask if I would consider the role, and it felt like a completely natural fit. If I can do anything to shine a light on something positive for families and children, I’m thrilled to do it."

Speaking about her role championing the charity's mission, Harriet said, "My primary role is being an advocate for the charity and raising awareness.

READ MORE: Zara Tindall sparks trouble in new conflict with King, Prince William's code

"That involves attending events, participating in meetings, appearing on its website and social media, and visiting community groups to connect with volunteers and parents directly."

headline: LHC summons Lahore DC over Imran's sisters detention, orders Noreen's meeting with daughters
subheadline: Noreen's two daughters be allowed to meet mother in Kot Lakhpat jail on Tuesday, orders court
author: Waqas Awan
article_text:
LHC directs Lahore DC to appear in person on November 4.
Noreen transferred back to jail after treatment, court told.
Govt lawyer says daughter had met Noreen on October 29.

LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Monday summoned the Lahore deputy commissioner (DC) over extensions in the detention of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan's sisters, while ordering a meeting between Noreen Niazi and her daughters.

Justice Abher Gul Khan issued the directions while hearing petitions filed by Aleema Khan's son, Shahrez Khan, and Sakeena Bibi concerning the detention of Aleema, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, as well as the latter's medical treatment.

Noreen was shifted from Lahore's Kot Lakhpat jail to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology on October 28 after experiencing heart-related discomfort.

Lawyer Rana Mudassar Umar said Noreen had experienced discomfort in her heart while detained at Kot Lakhpat jail, following which she was taken to the hospital.

Aleema, Noreen and Uzma have remained in custody since last month under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance in connection with the PTI's anti-government protest.

Noreen and Uzma were detained for 30 days on September 21, shortly before the PTI's planned September 27 protest, which was subsequently moved to October 4. Aleema's detention had taken place a day earlier, on September 20.

The Punjab government had told the court in late October that it had extended the detention of the three sisters. A government lawyer had told the LHC that the detention was extended by another 30 days on recommendation by the deputy commissioner.

During today's proceedings, the LHC directed the Lahore DC to appear in person on November 4, while ordering that Noreen's two daughters be allowed to meet their mother in jail at 10am tomorrow (Tuesday) for an hour.

The court directed the petitioner's lawyer to submit an application to the Lahore DC regarding the meeting and ordered the deputy commissioner to arrange it on the basis of that request.

During the hearing, a lawyer representing the Punjab government informed the court that Noreen had received treatment at a hospital and was subsequently transferred back to jail on doctors' advice.

The government lawyer further submitted that Noreen's daughter, Hajra Niazi, had already met her mother on October 29 during her hospital treatment.

Separately, lawyer Rana Mudassar Umar told the court that the three sisters had spent 44 days in jail without committing any offence and requested that a report in Aleema's case also be summoned by November 4.

Justice Khan responded by saying that the court would examine the matter.

PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja previously told the court that Aleema's driver had also been detained, arguing the driver was a non-political individual and requested leniency in his case.

Justice Khan said the court had sought reports in both cases and would examine them before proceeding further.

The judge also questioned why a separate petition had not been filed for the driver if his detention was a distinct concern.

"You have filed the applications together, so we will seek the reports together as well," he observed.

The petitioners had said that the initial 30-day detention period had expired before the Lahore deputy commissioner issued a notification extending the detention on October 7.

They requested the court to declare the October 7 detention notification illegal and set it aside.

Noreen was shifted from Lahore's Kot Lakhpat jail to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology on October 28 after experiencing heart-related discomfort.

Lawyer Rana Mudassar Umar said Noreen had experienced discomfort in her heart while detained at Kot Lakhpat jail, following which she was taken to the hospital.

Aleema, Noreen and Uzma have remained in custody since last month under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance in connection with the PTI's anti-government protest.

Noreen and Uzma were detained for 30 days on September 21, shortly before the PTI's planned September 27 protest, which was subsequently moved to October 4. Aleema's detention had taken place a day earlier, on September 20.

The Punjab government had told the court in late October that it had extended the detention of the three sisters. A government lawyer had told the LHC that the detention was extended by another 30 days on recommendation by the deputy commissioner.

During today's proceedings, the LHC directed the Lahore DC to appear in person on November 4, while ordering that Noreen's two daughters be allowed to meet their mother in jail at 10am tomorrow (Tuesday) for an hour.

The court directed the petitioner's lawyer to submit an application to the Lahore DC regarding the meeting and ordered the deputy commissioner to arrange it on the basis of that request.

During the hearing, a lawyer representing the Punjab government informed the court that Noreen had received treatment at a hospital and was subsequently transferred back to jail on doctors' advice.

The government lawyer further submitted that Noreen's daughter, Hajra Niazi, had already met her mother on October 29 during her hospital treatment.

Separately, lawyer Rana Mudassar Umar told the court that the three sisters had spent 44 days in jail without committing any offence and requested that a report in Aleema's case also be summoned by November 4.

Justice Khan responded by saying that the court would examine the matter.

PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja previously told the court that Aleema's driver had also been detained, arguing the driver was a non-political individual and requested leniency in his case.

Justice Khan said the court had sought reports in both cases and would examine them before proceeding further.

The judge also questioned why a separate petition had not been filed for the driver if his detention was a distinct concern.

"You have filed the applications together, so we will seek the reports together as well," he observed.

The petitioners had said that the initial 30-day detention period had expired before the Lahore deputy commissioner issued a notification extending the detention on October 7.

They requested the court to declare the October 7 detention notification illegal and set it aside.

headline: Luka Doncic scores 45 points, makes history twice as Lakers beat Raptors
subheadline: The Lakers bounced back from last week's loss to the Warriors as Doncic's 45 points contributed to a 131-125 win over the Raptors
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic makes history twice as he leads the team posting 45 points in a win over the Toronto Raptors.

The Slovenian star displayed a straight second monster game while scoring 45 points and filling up the stat sheet as he kept building his early-season argument for MVP honours.

It was the third 40-plus effort in the last four games for the NBA’s leading scorer (37.7 PPG).

The Lakers made a comeback after being defeated by the Golden State Warriors last week as Doncic put up a strong show contributing to a 131-125 win over the Raptors on Sunday, November 1, at Crypto.com Arena.

It is still unclear if Donic will return for the Monday game against the Miami Heat, as he hinted at a possible rest.

"I got to get rest, a cold tub, a massage, and rest and see you tomorrow,” Doncic said in a postgame interview with Spectrum SportsNet.

The big night arrived as Doncic made hisotry twice, giving Toronto fits, while also committing eight turnovers, swiping five steals and drawing three charges, becoming the first player to record those defensive marks in the same game since player tracking began in 2013-14.

headline: Joanna Page opens up about daughter Eva's showbiz ambitions
subheadline: The 'Gavin & Stacey' star said Eva is 'incredibly artistic' with an 'amazing singing voice
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Joanna Page has nothing but support for her 13-year-old daughter, Eva, as she hopes to pursue an acting acting career just like her mother.

The actress, 49, has been raising her four children with her actor husband, James Thornton.

The couple share children Eva, 13, Kitt,11, Noah, nine and Boe, four.

READ MORE: Joanna Page teases Love Island-style twist following epic 'Taskmaster' win

The Gavin & Stacey star said Eva is 'incredibly artistic' with an 'amazing singing voice' and has now decided she wants to go to drama school in London.

Speaking to the Daily Mail, she said: 'She wants to be an actress. It was really weird because she's incredibly artistic, but she's an amazing drawer and so I thought for a while she was going to be a costume designer or she was going to work in the art department.

'And now, suddenly overnight, she just wanted to be an actress. She's got an amazing singing voice and she's played the genie in Aladdin in school. I mean, she's done all sorts.

'She's got a brilliant voice but now she's wanting to do serious acting.

'Discussing her teenage daughter's future, the author continued: 'She's got it all lined up, wants to go to drama school, wants to go to London.

'She's told me she won't be coming home for dinner and I'm not allowed to go into London and try and hang out with her. She's very independent right now. But yeah, she full-blown wants to be an actress.'

Asked what advice she has given her, Joanna insisted the trick to acting is 'never giving up', have 'confidence in yourself' and that an 'actor is always full of lies'.

The Welsh actress said: 'Just go for it, just be confident in yourself. Don't try and change the thing which makes you different to everybody else because that's the thing which makes you unique.

'Don't try and fit in with anybody else. If you're in an audition, you use it as your time, it's your time, don't say, "Oh, thank you for seeing me". No, they desperately want you to get the job. If you walk in and they're like, "Whoa, we found the person straight away". That's amazing.

'So the ball's in your court and use that time as it's your time to show off your ability and don't be scared to try something new. As an actor, you're always full of lies.'

'So you'll say, "Yes, I can ride a horse. Yes, I can do a boxing match", both things I've done myself, then you find yourself going, I need to get lessons.

'Have confidence in yourself. I never give up because it's really, really difficult, but just keep going,' she added.

Elsewhere Joanna said she 'will always get that mum guilt' as she attempts to balance her career with raising her four children with actor husband James.

The couple share children Eva, 13, Kitt,11, Noah, nine and Boe, four.
READ MORE: Joanna Page teases Love Island-style twist following epic 'Taskmaster' win
The Gavin & Stacey star said Eva is 'incredibly artistic' with an 'amazing singing voice' and has now decided she wants to go to drama school in London.

Speaking to the Daily Mail, she said: 'She wants to be an actress. It was really weird because she's incredibly artistic, but she's an amazing drawer and so I thought for a while she was going to be a costume designer or she was going to work in the art department.
'And now, suddenly overnight, she just wanted to be an actress. She's got an amazing singing voice and she's played the genie in Aladdin in school. I mean, she's done all sorts.
'She's got a brilliant voice but now she's wanting to do serious acting.
'Discussing her teenage daughter's future, the author continued: 'She's got it all lined up, wants to go to drama school, wants to go to London.

'She's told me she won't be coming home for dinner and I'm not allowed to go into London and try and hang out with her. She's very independent right now. But yeah, she full-blown wants to be an actress.'
Asked what advice she has given her, Joanna insisted the trick to acting is 'never giving up', have 'confidence in yourself' and that an 'actor is always full of lies'.
The Welsh actress said: 'Just go for it, just be confident in yourself. Don't try and change the thing which makes you different to everybody else because that's the thing which makes you unique.

'Don't try and fit in with anybody else. If you're in an audition, you use it as your time, it's your time, don't say, "Oh, thank you for seeing me". No, they desperately want you to get the job. If you walk in and they're like, "Whoa, we found the person straight away". That's amazing.
'So the ball's in your court and use that time as it's your time to show off your ability and don't be scared to try something new. As an actor, you're always full of lies.'
'So you'll say, "Yes, I can ride a horse. Yes, I can do a boxing match", both things I've done myself, then you find yourself going, I need to get lessons.
'Have confidence in yourself. I never give up because it's really, really difficult, but just keep going,' she added.
Elsewhere Joanna said she 'will always get that mum guilt' as she attempts to balance her career with raising her four children with actor husband James.

headline: Inspired by London's Oxford Street, Karachi 'plans pedestrian-only roads'
subheadline: London pedestrianises half of Oxford street in first phase
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab has said the city plans to designate certain roads as pedestrian-only zones, drawing inspiration from London's move to pedestrianise a stretch of its iconic Oxford Street.

Wahab said the London mayor had allocated a one-kilometre section of Oxford Street exclusively for pedestrians, a move that has received widespread appreciation.

He said political parties had not created legal hurdles to the closure of Oxford Street to vehicular traffic, highlighting the importance of cooperation in implementing such urban development initiatives.

Taking inspiration from the initiative, Karachi also plans to close selected roads to traffic and reserve them for pedestrians, the mayor said.

A stretch of London's famous shopping street, Oxford Street, was made permanently traffic-free last Monday (October 26), allowing pedestrians to take over an area previously used by vehicles, including the capital's iconic red double-decker buses and black cabs.

Around half of the street has been pedestrianised in the first phase, with plans to extend the restrictions to the remaining sections depending on the success of the initiative.

headline: Meghan Markle receives upsetting update on father's health
subheadline: Thomas Markle may skip investigation after new reveal
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Meghan Markle's father Thomas has been taken to a special facility after a major health crisis, according to a new report.

In a shocking new twist, Thomas Markle Sr, who's facing serious allegations, has entered a care home for dementia patients.

The move could make it difficult for the FBI to investigate the Duchess of Sussex's father over child sex abuse allegations, according to a top lawyer.

READ MORE: Will Meghan Markle play a victim card on father's Scandal

Spencer Kuvin, a Florida-based lawyer, warned Meghan's 'cognitive issues' could prevent police from questioning him.

'You can't just barge into a memory care facility and conduct an interview. Any decent lawyer would be able to get that interview struck [off] and the FBI know that,' he said.

The 82-year-old, who's at a rehabilitation centre in Florida after having his lower left leg amputated, has now been transferred to another facility in the state specialising in 'memory care'.

He was diagnosed with dementia after his son, Thomas Markle Jr, told police he had found a stash of child sex abuse images among his father's belongings in the Philippines, where the pair had lived until former Hollywood lighting director Thomas Sr returned to the US after his amputation.

Prosecutors in the Philippines said that Markle would face the 'full extent of the law' if found guilty of possessing the images.

The FBI confirmed it had launched an investigation, with police seising child abuse images from the lock-up.

READ MORE: Harriet Phillips shuts down Meghan's claims about Princess Kate

headline: Who was Jerry Koosman? legendary pitcher who sealed Mets' World Series title, dies at 83
subheadline: Koosman is survived by his sons Michael and Shaw and daughter Danielle
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Jerry Koosman, an All-Star left-hander who got the final out of the Miracle Mets’ surprising 1969 World Series title triumph over the Baltimore Orioles, died on Sunday, November 1, 2026.

He was 83.

Mets spokesman Jay Horwitz said Koosman had been sick for about a year and died of multiple illnesses in Osceola, Wisconsin, surrounded by his children.

One of the most iconic images is Koosman leaping onto catcher Jerry Grote in celebration on the Shea Stadium mound after the moment the World Series was clinched.

The Miracle Mets had never finished with a winning record before the 1969 triumph.

Koosman appeared in 19 major league seasons, averaging 222-209 with a 3.36 ERA, throwing 140 complete games that included 33 shutouts and becoming a two-time 50-game winner.

During his 19 seasons in the MLB, he played for four teams: the Mets from 1996 to 78, posting a 140-137 record and a 3.09 ERA.

Then he pitched for Minnesota from 1979 to 1981, the Chicago White Sox from 1981 to 1983 and the Philadelphia 1984 to 1985 .

Koosman was born in Appleton, a small town in Minnesota, on December 23, 1942. He played baseball while serving in the U.S. Army at Fort Bragg in North Carolina.

He is survived by his sons Michael and Shaw and daughter Danielle. His marriage to the former LaVonne Sorum ended in a divorce.

headline: Meghan reveals big plans for Princess Lilibet - but Harry says 'no'
subheadline: Princess Lilibet's debut sparks disagreement between Harry and Meghan Markle
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Meghan Markle's latest career announcement sparked questions about the possibility of the Sussexes' kids debuting on television.

The Duchess of Sussex confirmed her appearance as a judge on Junior MasterChef Australia alongside Poh Ling Yeow.

She expressed her excitement about returning to the country after her successful cameo on the MasterChef Australia show.

READ MORE: Meghan breaks silence on holiday plans amid King Charles invite buzz

But, questions raised weather Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet joining their mother in the TV show as multiple times Meghan posted on social media about her little helpers in the kitchen.

According to New Idea, "There’s no doubt Archie, but especially Lili, would dearly love to participate. They both love making a mess with mum in the kitchen, but to do it with a bunch of other kids sounds like heaven!"

It has been understood that Meghan and her children will travel to Australia at the start of 2027 to film the show.

"It’s a short, contained shoot and the format is family-friendly, so it’s only natural that her ‘little sous-chefs’ at home would want to take part."

However, as much as Archie and Lilibet want to take part in the show, especially little Lili, the Duke of Sussex is against the idea.

An insider added, "Lilibet’s clearly inherited her mum’s love of cooking.

READ MORE: King Charles issues instruction to royals over Thomas Markle probe

"But it would be an extraordinary U-turn for them to suddenly put the full spotlight on their kids – for a TV show Down Under."

The Duchess of Sussex confirmed her appearance as a judge on Junior MasterChef Australia alongside Poh Ling Yeow.

She expressed her excitement about returning to the country after her successful cameo on the MasterChef Australia show.

READ MORE: Meghan breaks silence on holiday plans amid King Charles invite buzz

But, questions raised weather Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet joining their mother in the TV show as multiple times Meghan posted on social media about her little helpers in the kitchen.

According to New Idea, "There’s no doubt Archie, but especially Lili, would dearly love to participate. They both love making a mess with mum in the kitchen, but to do it with a bunch of other kids sounds like heaven!"

It has been understood that Meghan and her children will travel to Australia at the start of 2027 to film the show.

"It’s a short, contained shoot and the format is family-friendly, so it’s only natural that her ‘little sous-chefs’ at home would want to take part."

However, as much as Archie and Lilibet want to take part in the show, especially little Lili, the Duke of Sussex is against the idea.

An insider added, "Lilibet’s clearly inherited her mum’s love of cooking.

READ MORE: King Charles issues instruction to royals over Thomas Markle probe

"But it would be an extraordinary U-turn for them to suddenly put the full spotlight on their kids – for a TV show Down Under."

headline: Molly Mae Hague makes surprising U turn on having more children
subheadline: Despite Tommy's desire to expand their family, Molly-Mae previously shared her reluctance to have more children
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Molly Mae Hague hints at expanding her family

The influencer, 27, recently welcomed her second child, a son named Midas, in June with partner Tommy Fury.

She is already a mother to their daughter, Bambi, three.

Despite Tommy's desire to expand their family, Molly-Mae previously shared her reluctance to have more children.

However, in her latest YouTube vlog on Monday, she hinted that she might want a few more babies while holding Midas.

READ MORE: Molly-Mae Hague shares future family plans after welcoming baby no. 2

She said: 'To have another or to call it a day, who knows, but I'd love another one just like you. Do you want to be a big brother?

'Why have I gone insane? Why do I think that I want another baby?

'The stage we're in now is quite frankly definitely enough to make you not want to have another baby again, like this 4 to 5 month, it's not that fun really.

'But he is a really good boy and we love him so much and his big sister adores him.'

She added: 'I think I'd like a few more like you.'

However, in August, Molly vowed that her son Midas, who was 10 weeks at the time, will 'be her last' child.

She revealed that Midas was struggling with feeding issues, leaving him 'screaming' in intense pain.

READ MORE: Tommy Fury's family reportedly feel 'shut out' despite couple's new baby

headline: Sindh warns schools of action over violations of transport safety rules
subheadline: School vans must not carry students beyond their authorised seating capacity, reads directive
author: Rana Javaid
article_text:
The Sindh Education Department has issued safety directives to private schools, prohibiting gas cylinders and unsafe practices in vehicles used to transport students.

Acting on the provincial education minister’s instructions, the department has prohibited CNG and LPG cylinders in all vehicles used to transport students, including school vans arranged by schools or parents.

The department has also prohibited supplying petrol directly to vehicle engines through bottles, cans or other makeshift containers instead of designated fuel tanks, warning that the practice poses serious safety risks.

Under the directives, school vans must not carry students beyond their authorised seating capacity. Students are also prohibited from travelling while standing on footboards, hanging from vehicles or occupying other unsafe positions.

All vehicles used for student transportation must have valid fitness certificates issued by the Sindh Transport Department. A copy of the certificate must be kept inside each vehicle for inspection.

The department has directed private educational institutions to ensure strict compliance with the safety requirements and all relevant laws.

It warned that violations or negligence would be viewed seriously and that the concerned school administrations would face action under the applicable rules.

headline: B57+ Business Leaders' Summit advances great convergence, mobilising OIC capital for Global South resilience
subheadline: High-level leaders convene in Istanbul to strengthen investment cooperation, launch strategic initiatives and build new bridges between OIC economies and Global South markets
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The B57+ Business Leaders’ Summit 2026 concluded in Istanbul, Türkiye, bringing together senior institutional leaders, policymakers, investors and business representatives to advance economic cooperation and explore new opportunities for investment across OIC economies and the wider Global South.

Held under the theme “The Great Convergence: Catalysing OIC Capital for Global South Resilience”, the Summit was organised by the Islamic Chamber of Commerce and Development (ICCD), in collaboration with the Standing Committee for Economic and Commercial Cooperation of the Organisation of the Islamic Cooperation (COMCEC) and the Union of Chambers and Commodity Exchanges of Türkiye (TOBB).

With the strategic partnership of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation Arbitration Centre (OIC-AC), Saleh Kamel Sustainable Entrepreneurship & Enterprise Development Organisation (SKSEED), Maida Nasir Organisation for Women’s Economic Empowerment, the Islamic Chamber Holding Company (ICCD Holding) and the Statistical, Economic and Social Research and Training Centre for Islamic Countries (SESRIC), this landmark event focused on translating shared economic priorities into strategic partnerships, robust investment linkages and tangible initiatives.

Over two productive days, the Summit hosted a dynamic program of strategic roundtables, high-level panel discussions, networking engagements and partnership-building opportunities, culminating in the Business Leaders Gala Dinner, which was graced by the presence of İbrahim ŞENEL, President of Strategy and Budget at the Presidency of the Republic of Türkiye.

The Summit was also honoured by the participation of Prof Dr Ömer Bolat, Minister of Trade of the Republic of Türkiye, whose presence highlighted the government's strong support for expanding cross-border trade and fostering an enabling environment for private sector growth.

During his keynote speech, he underscored the transformative power of unifying our collective economic and intellectual resources to drive progress, stating: "If we can bring together our capital, production capacity, technology and human resources in pursuit of common objectives, we will not only enhance the resilience of our own economies, but also make a stronger contribution to the sustainable development of the Global South."

Bringing a powerful private-sector voice to the Summit, Ziad Bashir, Chairman of the Pakistan Business Council (PBC) and Member of the Prime Minister of Pakistan’s Economic Advisory Council, presented a compelling vision of the potential of information technology and artificial intelligence in Pakistan. Drawing on his extensive global perspective, he outlined how these technologies are reshaping competitiveness across emerging economies and how OIC member states can position themselves to lead, rather than follow, in the digital economy.

Bashir placed particular emphasis on the strategic importance of protecting sovereign data, cautioning that national data must not be extracted in its raw form. He urged OIC economies to ensure that their data is processed and refined locally, so that the value it generates is retained at home and builds domestic digital and AI capabilities, describing data sovereignty as central to the economic resilience of the Global South.

Setting out the strategic vision behind the B57+ Business Leaders' Summit, Abdullah Saleh Kamel, President of the Islamic Chamber of Commerce and Development (ICCD), highlighted the role of ICCD in connecting business communities, and the importance of mobilising capital for sustainable economic cooperation.

He stated: "The Business Leaders' Summit is a key platform under our B57+ Business Leaders Network, through which we seek to achieve several objectives, including bringing together diverse business communities under the direct presence and guidance of business leaders from various countries, fostering robust connections between the business communities of OIC Member States and their global counterparts, addressing major global issues, highlighting the key challenges facing our communities in trade, investment and finance, and building lasting business relationships through diverse forms of cooperation and partnership."

In this regard, M Rifat Hisarcıklıoğlu, President of the Union of Chambers and Commodity Exchanges of Türkiye (TOBB) and Vice-President of the Islamic Chamber of Commerce and Development (ICCD), delivered the welcome remarks.

Reinforcing the value of institutional cooperation in building stronger business connections and unlocking new opportunities across regions, he stated: "We must work towards deeper trade integration and stronger cooperation among our countries by removing the barriers that constrain trade and investment between us. Achieving this requires a strong and effective common platform. Both the Islamic Chamber of Commerce and Development and the B57+ Business Leaders Network must be utilised more actively and brought to greater prominence on the global agenda."

article_html:
The B57+ Business Leaders’ Summit 2026 concluded in Istanbul, Türkiye, bringing together senior institutional leaders, policymakers, investors and business representatives to advance economic cooperation and explore new opportunities for investment across OIC economies and the wider Global South.

Held under the theme “The Great Convergence: Catalysing OIC Capital for Global South Resilience”, the Summit was organised by the Islamic Chamber of Commerce and Development (ICCD), in collaboration with the Standing Committee for Economic and Commercial Cooperation of the Organisation of the Islamic Cooperation (COMCEC) and the Union of Chambers and Commodity Exchanges of Türkiye (TOBB).

With the strategic partnership of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation Arbitration Centre (OIC-AC), Saleh Kamel Sustainable Entrepreneurship & Enterprise Development Organisation (SKSEED), Maida Nasir Organisation for Women’s Economic Empowerment, the Islamic Chamber Holding Company (ICCD Holding) and the Statistical, Economic and Social Research and Training Centre for Islamic Countries (SESRIC), this landmark event focused on translating shared economic priorities into strategic partnerships, robust investment linkages and tangible initiatives.

Over two productive days, the Summit hosted a dynamic program of strategic roundtables, high-level panel discussions, networking engagements and partnership-building opportunities, culminating in the Business Leaders Gala Dinner, which was graced by the presence of İbrahim ŞENEL, President of Strategy and Budget at the Presidency of the Republic of Türkiye.

The Summit was also honoured by the participation of Prof Dr Ömer Bolat, Minister of Trade of the Republic of Türkiye, whose presence highlighted the government's strong support for expanding cross-border trade and fostering an enabling environment for private sector growth.

During his keynote speech, he underscored the transformative power of unifying our collective economic and intellectual resources to drive progress, stating: "If we can bring together our capital, production capacity, technology and human resources in pursuit of common objectives, we will not only enhance the resilience of our own economies, but also make a stronger contribution to the sustainable development of the Global South."

Bringing a powerful private-sector voice to the Summit, Ziad Bashir, Chairman of the Pakistan Business Council (PBC) and Member of the Prime Minister of Pakistan’s Economic Advisory Council, presented a compelling vision of the potential of information technology and artificial intelligence in Pakistan. Drawing on his extensive global perspective, he outlined how these technologies are reshaping competitiveness across emerging economies and how OIC member states can position themselves to lead, rather than follow, in the digital economy.

Bashir placed particular emphasis on the strategic importance of protecting sovereign data, cautioning that national data must not be extracted in its raw form. He urged OIC economies to ensure that their data is processed and refined locally, so that the value it generates is retained at home and builds domestic digital and AI capabilities, describing data sovereignty as central to the economic resilience of the Global South.

Setting out the strategic vision behind the B57+ Business Leaders' Summit, Abdullah Saleh Kamel, President of the Islamic Chamber of Commerce and Development (ICCD), highlighted the role of ICCD in connecting business communities, and the importance of mobilising capital for sustainable economic cooperation.

He stated: "The Business Leaders' Summit is a key platform under our B57+ Business Leaders Network, through which we seek to achieve several objectives, including bringing together diverse business communities under the direct presence and guidance of business leaders from various countries, fostering robust connections between the business communities of OIC Member States and their global counterparts, addressing major global issues, highlighting the key challenges facing our communities in trade, investment and finance, and building lasting business relationships through diverse forms of cooperation and partnership."

In this regard, M Rifat Hisarcıklıoğlu, President of the Union of Chambers and Commodity Exchanges of Türkiye (TOBB) and Vice-President of the Islamic Chamber of Commerce and Development (ICCD), delivered the welcome remarks.

Reinforcing the value of institutional cooperation in building stronger business connections and unlocking new opportunities across regions, he stated: "We must work towards deeper trade integration and stronger cooperation among our countries by removing the barriers that constrain trade and investment between us. Achieving this requires a strong and effective common platform. Both the Islamic Chamber of Commerce and Development and the B57+ Business Leaders Network must be utilised more actively and brought to greater prominence on the global agenda."

headline: ‘Slow Horses' Jack Lowden finally addresses his role in 'James Bond'
subheadline: Callum Turner and Josh O'Connor have also been linked to the role
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Jack Lowden reacted to the buzz about him becoming the next James Bond but the actor is keeping his cards close to his chest.

Although his name has is linked to the famous spy role, he is not ready to say really much about it.

During a recent interview with British GQ, the Slow Horses star was asked about the reports that he could be among the actors being considered for the next Bond film. Callum Turner and Josh O'Connor have also been linked to the role.

The rumours got even more attention after Gary Oldman, who works with Lowden on Slow Horses, said he was hoping his co star would get the part. He even suggested that the makers had already chosen their next Bond.

READ MORE: Saoirse Ronan reacts to husband Jack Lowden's James Bond casting rumours

Lowden was pleased by Oldman's support but did not want to make the rumours bigger.

"It's all very flattering," he said. He also called Oldman a sweetheart and said it was lovely to hear such kind words from someone like him.

For now, the actor has another exciting role ahead. He will play Mr. Darcy in Netflix's upcoming Pride and Prejudice series.

READ MORE: Gracie Abrams recreates iconic 'Romeo and Juliet' scene on 'SNL'

Lowden also shared that he does not usually expect to be the first choice for the roles he takes.

headline: Prince William moves on from Harry with special new replacement
subheadline: Prince Harry suffers fresh heartache after William discloses special bond
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Prince Harry suffered heartbreak as Prince William disclosed his replacement despite a series of reconciliation attempts by the Duke.

The future King's growing bond with Robert Irwin has been dubbed a fulfilment of that empty space which was created when Harry left the firm.

Most recently, the duo, who are passionate about protecting the environment, made a joint appearance on The Graham Norton Show alongside Cate Blanchett and Hannah Waddingham.

READ MORE: Prince Harry finally reacts to William's 'no forgiveness' rule

According to New Idea, they both lost their parents at a young age, meaning they might have "recognised the same unseen scars."

The source added, "As a father of three, William’s connection to Robert is fun-filled, energetic and naturally paternal, so he’s made a point of always being available for Robert, who couldn’t ask for a better mentor.

"William misses the playful, fun relationship he had with Harry, and Robert never had a brother, so it’s easy to see why these two are so drawn to each other."

READ MORE: King Charles, Prince Harry's 'secret' deal sparks public fury

headline: Britney Spears makes fresh accusations against her sister and ex-husband
subheadline: The Princess of Pop declares she will 'find a new family' after being treated 'like a slave' for years
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Britney Spears has no intentions of reconciling with her family any time soon.

In a new Instagram post on Sunday, November 1, the Princess of Pop made several accusations against her estranged younger sister, Jamie Lynn Spears, and ex-husband, Kevin Federline, declaring that she “will find a new family.”

“Jamie Lynn never let me hold Ivy one time when I would visit in Louisiana during covid in two week trips,” Britney, 44, wrote about Jamie, 35, and Jamie’s daughter Ivy, born in April 2018.

READ MORE: Jamie Lynn Spears announces bittersweet news after sister Britney's arrest

Furthermore, the Toxic hitmaker accused her ex-husband of hostile behaviour after the pair divorced in 2006.

“Kevin wouldn’t let me use the bathroom when I would pick my children up in their house!!!” she wrote, referring to their sons, Sean Preston, 21, and Jayden James, 20.

“They made me feel like a slave and have all their secret things they did behind my back and all I ever did was work for my dad!!!” she added, reiterating, “I will find a new family!!!”

The post was accompanied by a still from the 2003 film Uptown Girls starring Brittany Murphy and Dakota Fanning, showing Fanning’s character giving the middle finger.

Britney has offered several glimpses into her family estrangement since her 13-year conservatorship ended in 2021. She remains estranged from her father, Jamie Spears, who underwent a leg amputation in 2023.

Her relationship with Kevin has also been fraught. In her 2023 memoir, The Woman in Me, Britney claimed that “fame and money” ruined him. Federline was granted primary custody of their sons, and the singer only began rebuilding her relationship with Sean and Jayden last year.

Meanwhile, Jamie Lynn has publicly expressed affection for her older sister. In 2023, she called Britney a “good big sister” and insisted that she loved her. Jamie Lynn remains close to their father, who attended her daughter Maddie’s high school graduation in May alongside Britney’s son Sean. Britney herself was notably absent.

READ MORE: Jamie Lynn Spears' daughter explains relationship with aunt Britney Spears

headline: Duchess Sophie arrives in Antigua ahead of King Charles' meeting with Andy Burnham
subheadline: Duchess of Edinburgh attends seaside reception shortly after landing
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Duchess of Edinburgh has arrived in Antigua and Barbuda while King Charles and Queen Camilla continue their engagements amid heavy rain.

According to the Court Circular for 1 November, Sophie, who serves as Global Ambassador for the International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness (IAPB), departed Gatwick Airport for Antigua and Barbuda earlier in the day.

The Duchess wasted little time getting involved in the visit, attending a reception at Northshore Seaside Suites later that afternoon.

Read More: King set for reunion in Antigua amid fresh calls to end monarchy

Meanwhile, Charles is also preparing to meet Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham, who is expected to come face to face with the monarch during the visit.

The meeting comes amid renewed discussion about Britain's historical role in the transatlantic slave trade, with Burnham reportedly open to the prospect of a formal apology on behalf of the UK.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Andrew Parsons (@parsonsphotog)

Photographer Parsonphotog has shared a pictures of King Charles and Queen Camilla on Instagram, capturing the monarch opening the CHOGM 2026 cricket match alongside West Indies cricket legend Sir Viv Richards.

headline: Three minor earthquakes jolt California along San Andreas Fault overnight
subheadline: The most recent earthquakes along the San Andreas Fault were recorded in Loma Prieta in 1989 and San Francisco in 1906
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Three minor earthquakes have rattled across California overnight right along the San Andreas Fault, the U.S. Geological Survey reported.

The quakes were registered in the mid-magnitude 2 range across Northern and Southern California on Sunday, November 1, 2026.

A small 2.7-magnitude earthquake was detected in Petrolia at around 4:31 a.m., followed by a 2.6-magnitude shake felt in Santa Barbara near 4:39 a.m., according to a USGS Latest Earthquakes Interactive Map.

Westley was also shaken up with a magnitude 2.5 quake on Saturday night.

The most recent earthquakes along the San Andreas Fault were recorded in Loma Prieta in 1989 and San Francisco in 1906.

Local media reports highlight that six tremors with a magnitude of 2.5 have jolted the region over the last week.

The strongest, a 2.9 scale quake, jolted the same area on October 31.

According to the U.S. Geological Survey, magnitude measures the energy released at the source of the earthquake.

It now replaces the old Richter scale.

Quakes between 2.5 and 5.4 magnitude are often felt but rarely cause much damage.

According to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, earthquakes’ sudden, rapid shaking can trigger fires, tsunamis, landslides or avalanches.

They can happen anywhere but are most common in Alaska, California, Hawaii, Oregon, Puerto Rico and Washington.

According to an estimate, there are 500,000 traceable earthquakes in the world each year, and 100,000 of those can be felt, and 100 bring damage to the property and loss of lives.

Why does the San Andreas Fault draw constatnt spotlight?

The San Andreas Fault stretchs roughly 800 miles through California and marks the boundary between the Pacific and North American tectonic plates.

The region has produced significant seismic activity in the past, including the destructive 1906 San Francisco event.

With this past record in mind, even the modest secondary activity draws the spotlight from scientists and emergency planners.

Minor quakes like those recorded overnight are common along the fault and serve as reminders of ongoing plate movement.

article_html:
Three minor earthquakes have rattled across California overnight right along the San Andreas Fault, the U.S. Geological Survey reported.

The quakes were registered in the mid-magnitude 2 range across Northern and Southern California on Sunday, November 1, 2026.

A small 2.7-magnitude earthquake was detected in Petrolia at around 4:31 a.m., followed by a 2.6-magnitude shake felt in Santa Barbara near 4:39 a.m., according to a USGS Latest Earthquakes Interactive Map.

Westley was also shaken up with a magnitude 2.5 quake on Saturday night.

The most recent earthquakes along the San Andreas Fault were recorded in Loma Prieta in 1989 and San Francisco in 1906.

Local media reports highlight that six tremors with a magnitude of 2.5 have jolted the region over the last week.

The strongest, a 2.9 scale quake, jolted the same area on October 31.

According to the U.S. Geological Survey, magnitude measures the energy released at the source of the earthquake.

It now replaces the old Richter scale.

Quakes between 2.5 and 5.4 magnitude are often felt but rarely cause much damage.

According to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, earthquakes’ sudden, rapid shaking can trigger fires, tsunamis, landslides or avalanches.

They can happen anywhere but are most common in Alaska, California, Hawaii, Oregon, Puerto Rico and Washington.

According to an estimate, there are 500,000 traceable earthquakes in the world each year, and 100,000 of those can be felt, and 100 bring damage to the property and loss of lives.

Why does the San Andreas Fault draw constatnt spotlight?

The San Andreas Fault stretchs roughly 800 miles through California and marks the boundary between the Pacific and North American tectonic plates.

The region has produced significant seismic activity in the past, including the destructive 1906 San Francisco event.

With this past record in mind, even the modest secondary activity draws the spotlight from scientists and emergency planners.

Minor quakes like those recorded overnight are common along the fault and serve as reminders of ongoing plate movement.

headline: Is Sydney Sweeney the next James Bond girl?
subheadline: The next James Bond film does not have an official release date yet
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Sydney Sweeney caught the attention of the James Bond world after a former Bond girl named her as perfect choice to play the famous spy’s next love interest.

Trina Parks, 79, believes the actress has the right qualities for the role. She knows the Bond films well, as she made history in 1971 by becoming the first Black Bond girl.

She played Thumper, an assassin who appeared alongside Sean Connery in Diamonds Are Forever.

Speaking to The Telegraph, Parks praised Sweeney's acting skills and said: “Sydney would do a wonderful job. She has done quite a range of acting things and basically has got ownership of her sexual identity.”

READ MORE: ‘Slow Horses' Jack Lowden finally addresses his role in 'James Bond'

She, however, also explained what she would like to see in the next Bond film. The star believes the woman who falls for 007 should have her own voice and should not be easily impressed by his looks.

She wants Bond to work for her love instead of having many relationships.

While the next Bond girl is still mystery, the search for the new 007 is also moving forward.

READ MORE: Gracie Abrams recreates iconic 'Romeo and Juliet' scene on 'SNL'

Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and another unnamed actor have reportedly taken part in screen tests.

Meanwhile, Ben Whishaw, who played Q, believes the famous film series “needs to be reinvented completely”.

headline: Meghan Markle's bombshell truth: 'The genie can't go back in the bottle'
subheadline: The Duchess of Sussex sparks a fierce new debate after dropping a bombshell truth
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Meghan Markle has sparked a fierce new debate after dropping a bombshell truth, but now she knows there's no putting the genie back in the bottle.

The Duchess of Sussex is said to be in pain after revealing a 2019 letter, as she had no idea it would cause such an uproar.

An insider has claimed that Meghan Markle regrets introducing a previously unknown 2019 letter into the increasingly troubling story surrounding her father, Thomas Markle.

READ MORE: Meghan Markle receives heartbreaking update from US

What she intended as an explanation for their estrangement has instead opened an entirely new can of worms.

“Meghan deeply regrets bringing this letter into the public conversation. Nobody would be discussing it if she hadn’t tried to use it to explain her family breakdown and attack the press. She has made herself part of the story, and she cannot put the genie back in the bottle,” a source close to the situation told Rob Shuter.

Prince Harry's wife was reportedly presented the letter, written by Roslyn Loveless, as a key reason she cut ties with her father and kept her children away from him. But newly revealed details have raised questions about its significance.

In the end, the letter that was meant to close a painful chapter has only turned the page to a more complicated one.

For Meghan, the truth may have finally come out, but the cost of telling it is a reminder that some family wounds cannot be healed with a statement, only with time, distance and the courage to let the truth speak for itself.

headline: PTI chairman rejects Barrister Saif's claims, says all efforts made to meet Imran Khan
subheadline: Barrister Gohar says party repeatedly denied access to incarcerated founder
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Gohar terms Barrister Saif’s claims false, baseless.
Says courts, negotiations used to seek meeting.
Access to Imran was condition during talks.

PESHAWAR: PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Monday rejected party leader Barrister Muhammad Ali Saif’s claims, saying the party had made every possible effort to secure a meeting with incarcerated founder Imran Khan.

Speaking to the media in Peshawar, Gohar termed as “baseless” Saif’s assertion that PTI leaders had failed to meet Imran despite being offered an opportunity to do so.

“We made every possible effort to meet the PTI founder through the courts and negotiations, but despite all our efforts, we were not allowed even a single meeting,” he said.

Gohar said access to Imran had also been one of the party’s conditions during the negotiation process.

He rejected the assertions made by Saif during his interview, saying: “All of Barrister Saif’s claims are false. I reject them.”

Saif, during an interview on Geo News programme Jirga, had said that Allama Raja Nasir Abbas was in direct contact with important figures in the establishment, but maintained that those contacts were not aimed at securing Imran’s release.

Separately, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja linked any party decision on the proposed 28th Constitutional Amendment to a meeting with Imran.

Raja also expressed his inability to exercise control over PTI’s social media.

PTI dismisses reports of internal divisions

Moreover, PTI today dismissed reports of internal divisions, saying the entire party remained united behind its founder, his ideology and mission.

In a statement issued after a meeting of its political committee, the party said there was no grouping or division within its ranks and that its leaders and workers would continue their struggle towards their shared objectives.

The committee also discussed the country’s political situation, inflation and law and order, according to the statement.

It demanded the immediate release of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister, provincial assembly speaker and other detained parliamentarians, describing their detention as illegal.

PTI said keeping elected representatives in custody was an affront to democratic values and the public mandate.

The political committee expressed concern over reports that Imran and his wife Bushra Bibi had been shifted to hospital without their families being taken into confidence.

It demanded immediate implementation of the Supreme Court’s order regarding medical treatment for the PTI founder and called for his family to be regularly informed about his health.

The committee also demanded that Imran’s family be allowed to meet and visit him, while appropriate medical facilities and family meetings should also be ensured for Bushra Bibi.

PTI also condemned the arrest of Imran’s sisters and their treatment in custody, demanding their immediate release and permission for them to meet the former premier.

The committee raised concerns over the arrests of MNA Adil Bazai and other party leaders and workers, demanding the immediate release of all those detained under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO).

It said no individual should be subjected to retaliation over political differences.

PTI also condemned raids and vandalism at the residences of Omar Ayub, Sher Ali Arbab and Shah Ahad, saying targeting the homes and families of political opponents was condemnable.

Separately, the political committee expressed concern over the increasing incidents of terrorism in the country, describing the menace as a serious threat requiring effective and concerted measures.

The party said protecting citizens’ lives and property was a fundamental responsibility of the state.

It added that actions against terrorism should not be used for political retaliation.

article_html:
• Gohar terms Barrister Saif’s claims false, baseless.
  • Says courts, negotiations used to seek meeting.
  • Access to Imran was condition during talks.

PESHAWAR: PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Monday rejected party leader Barrister Muhammad Ali Saif’s claims, saying the party had made every possible effort to secure a meeting with incarcerated founder Imran Khan.

Speaking to the media in Peshawar, Gohar termed as “baseless” Saif’s assertion that PTI leaders had failed to meet Imran despite being offered an opportunity to do so.

“We made every possible effort to meet the PTI founder through the courts and negotiations, but despite all our efforts, we were not allowed even a single meeting,” he said.

Gohar said access to Imran had also been one of the party’s conditions during the negotiation process.

He rejected the assertions made by Saif during his interview, saying: “All of Barrister Saif’s claims are false. I reject them.”

Saif, during an interview on Geo News programme Jirga, had said that Allama Raja Nasir Abbas was in direct contact with important figures in the establishment, but maintained that those contacts were not aimed at securing Imran’s release.

Separately, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja linked any party decision on the proposed 28th Constitutional Amendment to a meeting with Imran.

Raja also expressed his inability to exercise control over PTI’s social media.

PTI dismisses reports of internal divisions

Moreover, PTI today dismissed reports of internal divisions, saying the entire party remained united behind its founder, his ideology and mission.

In a statement issued after a meeting of its political committee, the party said there was no grouping or division within its ranks and that its leaders and workers would continue their struggle towards their shared objectives.

The committee also discussed the country’s political situation, inflation and law and order, according to the statement.

It demanded the immediate release of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister, provincial assembly speaker and other detained parliamentarians, describing their detention as illegal.

PTI said keeping elected representatives in custody was an affront to democratic values and the public mandate.

The political committee expressed concern over reports that Imran and his wife Bushra Bibi had been shifted to hospital without their families being taken into confidence.

It demanded immediate implementation of the Supreme Court’s order regarding medical treatment for the PTI founder and called for his family to be regularly informed about his health.

The committee also demanded that Imran’s family be allowed to meet and visit him, while appropriate medical facilities and family meetings should also be ensured for Bushra Bibi.

PTI also condemned the arrest of Imran’s sisters and their treatment in custody, demanding their immediate release and permission for them to meet the former premier.

The committee raised concerns over the arrests of MNA Adil Bazai and other party leaders and workers, demanding the immediate release of all those detained under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO).

It said no individual should be subjected to retaliation over political differences.

PTI also condemned raids and vandalism at the residences of Omar Ayub, Sher Ali Arbab and Shah Ahad, saying targeting the homes and families of political opponents was condemnable.

Separately, the political committee expressed concern over the increasing incidents of terrorism in the country, describing the menace as a serious threat requiring effective and concerted measures.

The party said protecting citizens’ lives and property was a fundamental responsibility of the state.

It added that actions against terrorism should not be used for political retaliation.

headline: Mohammad Amir ‘registers' as UK national for Afghanistan Premier League draft
subheadline: PCB is unlikely to issue NOCs to its players for the tournament, suggest media reports
author: Web Desk
article_text:
KARACHI: Former Pakistan pacer Mohammad Amir has registered as a UK national for the Afghanistan Premier League (APL) draft, scheduled to take place in Dubai on Tuesday, according to media reports.

Amir, who currently resides in England and has acquired British citizenship, has been listed as a UK national in the draft register, with Pakistan mentioned as his country of residence. He has been placed in the Platinum category.

Amir has represented Pakistan in 36 Tests, 61 One-Day Internationals (ODIs) and 62 T20 Internationals. His last appearance for the national side came against Ireland during the ICC Men's T20 World Cup in Lauderhill, Florida, in June 2024.

Registering as a UK national could also give Amir an advantage regarding his availability for the APL, as he may not require a No-Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), unlike his former Pakistan teammates.

Meanwhile, more than 30 Pakistani cricketers, including Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub, Hasan Ali, Shan Masood, Abdullah Shafique, Faheem Ashraf and Imad Wasim, have registered for the draft.

However, the participation of Pakistani players remains uncertain amid reported diplomatic tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan. Media reports suggest that the PCB is unlikely to issue NOCs to its players for the tournament.

The Afghanistan Cricket Board's (ACB) draft register has also clarified that the participation of Pakistani players is subject to obtaining NOCs from the PCB.

The APL will feature five teams, with each franchise permitted to register a maximum of 18 players, comprising 11-12 Afghanistan players and six to seven overseas recruits.

The players have been divided into five categories, with Platinum players set to receive $100,000, followed by $65,000 for Diamond, $40,000 for Gold, $20,000 for Silver and $10,000 for Emerging players.

Each franchise will have a total player purse ranging from $650,000 to $750,000.
