headline: Taylor Swift shares sweet anecdote about friendship with Abigail Anderson
subheadline: Taylor Swift speaks about finding instant connection with childhood bestfriend
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Taylor Swift and Abigail Anderson share a decades-long friendship and the pop icon looked back to the beginning of their lifelong bond, in a new panel talk.

The 36-year-old star appeared for a conversation about Toy Story 5 and spoke about friendship, saying, it's "about finding someone who's the same genre of weird and silly as you are and what just why Bonnie and Blaise's story resonated with me so much. You know when I moved to Nashville when I was 14, you know, you're the new kid in school, you're like who who should I be friends with, these girls are cool. These girls are cool."

However, among all the cool and nice girls, "there was one girl named Abigail and she even has curly hair to like blaze and the two of us all we wanted to do was talk in Napoleon Dynamite voices and we still do this and like it's something our husbands have to put up with. And so it's just like what are you doing today?" Swift said, emulating the voice, "I don't know. What are you doing? Oh, are you playing with your cute kid? Yeah. Yeah, what's the problem with that? And so it's like, you know when you find that person who just completely sees you for the strange little genre that is you at your purest. That's that that hit me so hard watching the film."

Swifties loved getting an insight into one of the friendships the Grammy winner has written multiple songs about, and commented, "this was a documentary."

One noted, "That’s her DIBBLES VOICE!!!!" referring to the pet name for Swift's cat Olivia Benson.

While a third chimed in, "That's such a sweet friendship. I love that they still share the same silly jokes after all these years their husbands must be used to it by now," and "Abigail mention love their friendship!" wrote another.

headline: Learjet 60 crashes in Florida: Here's what went wrong
subheadline: All nine on board killed in Learjet 60 crash
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A Learjet 60 carrying nine people crashed into a roadway in Palm Beach County on Sunday, November 1, afternoon, killing everyone on board and leaving a massive crater near a mobile home park in what officials call a “cataclysmic” Florida plane crash.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. Dashcam confirmed that the jet, which departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was bound for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, went down at about 12:50 p.m. ET near Cresthaven.

Dashcam footage revealed the aircraft falling nose-first before exploding into a fireball, narrowly missing cars and homes.

Air traffic control audio captured the crew’s final moments. The pilot initially reported icing conditions, an outside air temperature of -47 degrees Celsius, and moderate turbulence.

Moments later, the pilot declared “Mayday, mayday,” reporting a descent rate of 10,000 ft per minute before warning: “We’re going to crash into the ground.”

Flight tracking data reported the descent rate exceeded 32,000 ft per minute at one point.

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said: “It was a cataclysmic plane crash. It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road.”

Officials said there were no immediate reports of injuries on the ground.

About 600 residents near the crash site were evacuated to two shelters because debris blocked the entrance to a mobile home park, said Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores.

The National Transportation Safety Board has opened an investigation. The crash is the deadliest involving a Learjet 60 and the second-deadliest U.S. plane crash this year.

headline: King Charles' health concerns put William, Catherine's key plans on hold
subheadline: Prince William, Princess Kate turn down big offer for King Charles' sake
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Prince William and Princess Kate made key changes to their plans amid concerns for cancer-stricken King Charles.

The Prince and Princess of Wales are the most important members of the monarch's team. On King's behalf, the couple represents the royal family at several distinguished events.

After Catherine announced that she is in remission from cancer, fans expected a joint royal tour of the two in Australia. Though the future Queen went on a meaningful tour of Italy, this year the Waleses' reported Australia tour was not made possible.

READ MORE: Prince William moves on from Harry with special new replacement

Now, sources claimed that the real reason behind this delay is King Charles' health issues.

According to New Idea, "William and Kate have yet to accept the Aussie PM’s invite, but Robert Irwin wants them down under just as much as any Aussie.

"William’s promised to bring the kids to the Irwin zoo one day, and Robert takes every opportunity to remind him of that."

It has been almost 10 years since the Waleses travelled to Down Under as the firm prioritised King Charles' maximum tours, keeping in mind his growing age and cancer treatment.

READ MORE: King Charles finally gets his umbrella — watch his hilarious reaction

"It’s all unnecessary, of course, because William and Kate have Australia on their schedule every year, but something always comes up that forces them to push it back," an insider added. "The King’s health has been a huge factor stopping them from committing to a big tour."

headline: Singer Steve Ellis dies at 76
subheadline: For those unfamiliar with his career, the star was the frontman with London-based pop group Love Affair
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Steve Ellis has passed away, leaving his fans mourning his loss. The singer has died at the age of 76.

The news of Ellis's death following a 'chronic illness' was confirmed in a statement shared on the singer's Facebook page.

It read: 'Dear Friends, It's with a heavy heart that we share the news of Steve's passing.

READ MORE: Ozzy Osbourne's unreleased music to feature in upcoming biopic

'After complications from a chronic illness, Steve peacefully left the world on the evening of October 30, 2026, in the presence of his loved ones.'

'Please feel free to leave your thoughts, memories, or condolences for the family in the comments below. Everlasting Love.'

For those unfamiliar with his career, the star was the frontman with London-based pop group Love Affair, who scored a No1 with their best-known single in 1968. It knocked The Beatles' Hello Goodbye off the top spot.

The band went on to have four further Top 20 hits.

headline: New mechanism allowed govt to keep petrol price Rs15 cheaper: minister
subheadline: Ali Pervaiz says refineries absorbed increase as fuel import premiums surged
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Petrol premium surged from $5 to $20.
Refineries helped absorb Rs15 per litre increase.
Minister says Nov gas arrangements already secured.

ISLAMABAD: Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said on Monday that the government’s revised pricing mechanism and cooperation from local refineries enabled it to keep petrol around Rs15 per litre cheaper than international market rates amid the US-Iran war.

Speaking about the recent changes to the petrol pricing mechanism, Malik said the regional conflict had sharply increased costs associated with fuel imports, including freight, insurance and other logistics expenses.

He said the premium on petrol stood at around $5 per barrel before the war but subsequently surged to $20 per barrel.

The minister said subsequent PSO tenders showed premiums climbing further to around $25-$30 per barrel and even higher as regional conditions deteriorated.

Malik said the government worked with local refineries to deal with the situation and contain the impact on consumers without disrupting the availability of imported petrol.

Around 70% of the country’s petrol requirement comes from the international market while locally produced petrol accounts for about 30%, according to the minister.

He said the government had to ensure that any intervention did not make imported petrol commercially unviable and consequently lead to supply shortages.

“I am grateful that they listened to our appeal and absorbed roughly a Rs15 increase that was coming due for petrol on Friday, helping the government maintain prices,” Malik said, referring to local refineries.

He said the arrangement had allowed petrol to be kept around Rs15 per litre cheaper than international market rates, adding that refineries were absorbing a burden of roughly Rs15 billion per month.

Malik said international market prices were now declining, expressing hope that the trend would lead to further improvement for consumers.

How revised petrol pricing works

The federal cabinet approved changes to the petrol pricing mechanism on October 30 amid volatility caused by the US-Iran war.

Under the revised formula, the import price of petrol is determined on the basis of the actual import cost of the relevant PSO cargo. If that cost is unavailable for daily pricing, the premium, incidentals and customs duty of the last available cargo are used instead.

For local refineries, the government has temporarily fixed the premium, incidentals and customs duty used in calculating the ex-refinery petrol price at their March 7, 2026 — pre-war — levels for 30 days.

The difference between the import price and the resulting ex-refinery price is to be surrendered by refineries under the petroleum levy account, with the resulting benefit passed on through a corresponding reduction in the petrol price.

The government has also introduced a short-term adjustment to smooth petrol price movements, incorporating the benefit arising from a premium differential into petrol prices at a rate of $2.950 per barrel per day.

Govt says no fuel shortage

Meanwhile, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said there was no fuel shortage in Pakistan and the country’s requirements were being met.

On gas supplies, the petroleum minister said arrangements for November were already in place, while the government was making arrangements to meet requirements for December and January.

headline: Russell Brand's defence makes shocking claim over 2023 documentary
subheadline: Russell's lawyer also talked about how the allegations affected his family life
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Russell Brand's trial took new turn after his lawyer made strong claims about a documentary that first brought many allegations against him into the public eye.

During his final speech in court, Brand's lawyer Ian Winter KC said the 2023 Channel 4 Dispatches programme affected the case before it even reached trial.

He claimed the documentary encouraged women to come forward and changed the way people looked at Brand. He told the jury that the programme "poisoned the well of justice".

READ MORE: Russell Brand trial hears new claims from third accuser

Winter, however, also said that the women who are involved in the case were influenced by what they saw in the documentary.

He questioned how their claims can be treated as fully separate from the programme.

Brand is currently on trial at Southwark Crown Court over seven charges, which including rape and sexual assault but he, moreover, denied all those charges.

The lawyer also asked the jury to not to judge Brand for his personal life, sharing that having relationships with many women was not a crime.

READ MORE: Russell Brand leans on one person during major assault case

Winter also spoke about how the allegations affected Brand's family life as well as he reminded the court that a hospital refused to let him visit his baby son after his heart surgery in 2023.

article_text:
The Atlanta Falcons headed into Week 8 with a chance to dominate the NFC South but were instead shut out by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to fall to 3-5 for the season.

One week after they pulled off a surprise upset win over the red-hot San Francisco 49ers, the Falcons lost to a Bucs team that didn’t complete a single pass on offense.

On Atlanta’s side, Michael Penix Jr had a brutal game, throwing four interceptions just a few days after winning the NFC Offensive Player of the Week.

The heavy rain didn’t help Penix or the Falcons' defense, which looked a step slower attempting to stop Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell on Sunday, November 1, 2026.

Despite an 0-4 start, Tampa Bay is now poised to seize control of the NFC South at 3-5 with wins over the Falcons and the Carolina Panthers in back-to-back weeks.

As the Panthers head into NFL Week 9, they remain first in the division, but their lead over the Bucs is just half a game.

What are NFC South standings heading into NFL Week 9?

Carolina Panthers (3-4)

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-5)

Atlanta Falcons (3-5)

New Orleans Saints (2-5)

In NFL Week 9, the Falcons will play the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain, on Sunday, November 8.

The Bucs will travel to Chicago to play against the Bears on Sunday Night Football.

Whereas the Panthers will host the Denver Broncos on Sunday afternoon, while the New Orleans Saints are back in action after a week off and will play host to the Cleveland Browns.

headline: Olivia Rodrigo shows love to Phoebe Bridgers at Lost Tour amid her own tour
subheadline: Olivia Rodrigo and Phoebe Bridgers share a sweet bond of mutual admiration
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Olivia Rodrigo might be headlining her Unraveled Tour herself but she herself is a music fan inside and takes the time to enjoy music as a fan as well.

During her day off from her own tour, the 23-year-old pop superstar was found in the audience at Phoebe Bridger's final North American show of The Lost Tour in Los Angeles.

Since the Scott Street hitmaker has a strict no-phone policy at her shows, there were no pictures of the drop dead songstress, but many attendees took to social media and reported the event.

READ MORE: Phoebe Bridgers overwhelms fans with special guest during Lost Tour

Social media went wild about their two musicians interacting, writing, "MY GIRLLSSSSS," and "WHAT OMG."

While a third chimed in, "I want them to work together !" and "MY PARENTS."

Another added, "I'm in tears-" and "PHOEBELIVIA," gushed another.

headline: 2026 White Christmas weather predictions: Here's where snow can fall this holiday
subheadline: Snow can reach every US state this holiday season
author: Web Desk
article_text:
As the winter season draws closer, meteorologists have started studying whether large portions of the United States will be able to enjoy snow on the ground on Christmas Day, December 25.

The Climate Prediction Center, which is part of the National Weather Service, offers a map titled 'National White Christmas' with probabilities of having snow on the ground on Christmas based on climatology for the 30-year period from 1981 to 2010.

According to this data, in order to have a white Christmas, one should have at least an inch of snow on the ground, not just snowflakes falling from the sky.

Areas with the highest probability of having snow on Christmas include the Upper Midwest, Upper Northeast, along with some areas in the Northwest and mountainous regions. On the other hand, southern areas of the United States have very little chance of having snow, with Florida having the lowest probability of all.

According to the historical map, the places most likely to have a white Christmas are:

Upper Midwest: Such states as Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, and North Dakota.
Upper Northeast: Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, and northern New York.
Mountain West and Northwest: Such states as Colorado, Utah, Idaho, Montana, and Washington.

However, the southern states have a hard time achieving a white Christmas, while Florida is at the bottom of the historical map.

headline: Helen Flanagan fears she could be arrested after explosive clash with warden
subheadline: The Coronation Street star issued a fiery warning after clashing with a traffic warden who issued her a parking ticket over an innocent mistake
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Helen Flanagan has opened up about a heated confrontation with a traffic warden, admitting she fear she could end up being arrested.'

Taking to TikTok on Sunday, The Coronation Street star issued a fiery warning, declaring, 'Hell hath no fury if you get my wrath,' after clashing with a traffic warden who issued her a parking ticket over an innocent mistake.

Filming herself as she walked with her daughter, Helen appeared visibly frustrated as she recalled the incident during a trip to Manchester.

The altercation left her daughter worried that her mother might be taken away by the police

READ MORE: Helen Flanagan reveals reality of motherhood as she battles 'mum guilt'

Speaking to the camera, she said: 'I’ve got a courtesy car and I just parked in Manchester. I paid for my car park but because it's a courtesy car, instead of putting an 'O', I put a zero.

'I could see one of the traffic wardens trying to put a ticket on my car and I said, "no, I’ve paid for my ticket".

'I am due my period so like hell hath no fury if you get my wrath! Wow.' Helen's child was then heard tearfully exclaiming 'I don’t want to go back,' with the former Coronation Street star joking she may have potentially landed herself in hot water amid her clash with the civil enforcement officer.

She added: 'She thinks I’m going to get arrested. Mummy might actually. Honestly, I was like, "you are the most horrible man I’ve ever met. Karma for you!"'

Continuing her rant, she fumed: 'He knew that I'd made a mistake with one letter wrong because I had a courtesy car and he still gave me a ticket... honestly, he got my absolute wrath!

'And he deserved it! He deserved my wrath.'

Helen got back behind the wheel of her car for the first time in July last year following her six-month driving ban.

headline: ‘Resident Evil' to become 2026's second highest grossing horror hit
subheadline: 'Resident Evil' released in US theaters on September 18, 2026
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Resident Evil is almost ready to make another big mark at the box office.

The film is now just $600,000 away from passing Backrooms and becoming the second highest grossing horror film of 2026.

The latest Resident Evil movie earned around like $399.99 million all over the world after seven weekends in cinemas.

It has made $157.4 million in North America and another $242.6 million from other countries. Backrooms, whereas, is little ahead with $400.6 million but the gap between the two films is now very small.

READ MORE: 'Resident Evil' director reveals bold new direction behind upcoming film

Resident Evil, however, is still bringing people to cinemas as it made another $10 million over the past weekend alone.

The film appeared in 66 markets on more than 21,500 screens. This strong run can help it pass Backrooms within the next few days.

The film, moreover, already earned more than Sinners, The Nun and Weapons. It is now getting closer to The Exorcist, which made $430 million worldwide.

READ MORE: Russell Brand's defence makes shocking claim over 2023 documentary

China brought in the most money, with $71.4 million. The UK has added $19.4 million, while Japan and Mexico have each made $12.7 million.

headline: ‘I'm A Celeb 2026': Lineup, when it starts, what to expect
subheadline: Wayne Rooney, Joanna Page, and Ricky Wilson among rumoured stars to join ‘I’m A Celeb’
author: Web Desk
article_text:
As little as weeks away from the return of "I’m A Celebrity… Get Me Out of Here!," the full lineup for the 2026 show has allegedly been leaked, promising an all-star cast of former sports stars, soap opera actors, and internet celebrities heading to the jungles of Australia.

The latest information comes from a report in The Sun, which claims that the 12 celebrities participating in this year’s show include some really big names. Football superstar Wayne Rooney is said to be the show's biggest ever signing since his wife Coleen, who came second in 2024.

The full rumoured lineup is as follows:

Ade Adepitan (Paralympian)
AJ Odudu (TV host)
Chloe Burrows (reality star and presenter)
Claire Sweeney (actor)
Jack Skipper (comedian)
Joanna Page (actor)
Leigh Francis (comedian)
Leomie Anderson (model and presenter)
Mariella Frostrup (journalist and broadcaster)
Ricky Wilson (Kaiser Chiefs singer)
Sharmarke ‘Sharky’ Mohamud (content creator)
Wayne Rooney (football legend)

The rumored campmates consist of a diverse mix of talent. Paralympic athlete Ade Adepitan is likely to become the first contestant using a wheelchair, as the production company at ITV has modified the camp to suit his disability.

When Does It Start

Although ITV hasn't announced when exactly the new season is set to start, it's likely to begin within the next few days. Ant and Dec will be back to host the celebrity-filled event, with the celebrities starting to arrive in Australia soon. An official cast announcement is imminent.

What to Expect

It seems that viewers should prepare themselves for the usual harsh Bushtucker trials, with the rumor that this season's location will comprise a huge “House of Horrors.” With Wayne Rooney and internet sensation Sharky and Chloe Burrows among others, it seems that the show wants to attract both older and younger viewers.

According to ITV, “Any names suggested for I'm A Celebrity are just speculation.”

headline: Daisy May Cooper reveals heartbreaking reason she missed out on 'Celebrity Traitors'
subheadline: The star revealed she could not find childcare for daughter Pip, eight, and her sons Jack, seven, and Benji, two
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Daisy May Cooper showed off her stunning weight-loss transformation on This Morning after revealing that she had to turn down Celebrity Traitors because her children.

The actress, 40, appeared on the ITV show to discuss her debut novel What Took You So Long? and also revealed why she did not appear on the hit BBC show.

Speaking to Ben Shephard and Cat Deeley, the star revealed she could not find childcare for daughter Pip, eight, and her sons Jack, seven, and Benji, two.

READ MORE: ‘Celebrity Traitors' stars cannot escape the drama off screen

Revealing she was in line for the first series of Celebrity Traitors, she explained that once she learnt of the show's set up - including the stars staying in hotels - she had to drop out because nobody would look after her children.

Daisy, who lovingly dubbed the trio 'horrible' and 'a complete nightmare', split from Pip and Jack's father Will Weston 10 months after Jack's birth and she shares Benji with her current partner Anthony Huggins.

She said: 'This was for the first series, I was meant to do it and then I found out about the hotel and it wasn't a Premier Inn and I needed the basics of a Premier Inn and then nobody wanted to look after my kids because they're a complete nightmare.'

Daisy pleaded with viewers to purchase her book, saying: 'Please buy it, I need to feed my kids - my horrible kids.'

The This Country star is said to have lost a significant amount of weight by following a low-carb diet, dropping from a dress size 24 to a size 10.

headline: UK to make legal immigrants wait up to 15 years for settlement: Who will be affected?
subheadline: ILR allows foreign nationals to live and work in the UK without immigration time restrictions
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The British government is planning changes to the immigration settlement rules that could potentially make thousands of legal immigrants in the United Kingdom (UK) to wait for up to 15 years for permanent residency. The changes come under the leadership of Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood.

Mahmood is expected to outline the government's revised immigration policy in Parliament on Monday, November 2, 2026, with proposals that could double the standard waiting period for indefinite leave to remain (ILR) from five to 10 years.

Some lower-paid workers, particularly those employed in social care, could face a wait of up to 15 years under the original proposals.

However, the government is reportedly considering exemptions for foreign care workers already living in Britain following criticism from Labour lawmakers and concerns about staff shortages in the health and social care sectors.

ILR allows foreign nationals to live and work in the UK without immigration time restrictions and can eventually provide a route to British citizenship.

Under the proposed earned settlement system, migrants would no longer qualify simply by completing a fixed period of residence.

Instead, factors including earnings, English-language proficiency, good conduct and contributions to British society would influence how quickly applicants could obtain permanent status.

Highly paid professionals and entrepreneurs could qualify in as little as three years, while some skilled public-service workers, including doctors and nurses, could retain a five-year route.

One of the biggest unresolved questions is whether the longer waiting periods will apply to immigrants who entered Britain under existing rules.

The proposals have drawn more than 200,000 consultation responses, with critics warning that retrospective changes could disrupt the plans of families already working towards settlement.

The government has not yet confirmed the final exemptions, transitional arrangements or implementation dates.

Potential three-year route

Migrants who already hold ILR

Existing settled status unaffected

These are proposed routes, not a confirmed final schedule. The Home Office's previously announced higher English-language requirement is separately due to take effect in March 2027.

headline: Taylor Swift calls 'Eras Tour' the most 'exhausting' tour of her career
subheadline: The pop superstar, 36, reveals she couldn't get out of bed in-between her shows
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Taylor Swift made history with her record-breaking Eras Tour back in 2023 — and it took its toll.

Appearing on a Toy Story 5 Q&A panel in NYC on Sunday, November 1, the pop megastar detailed how she came to write the animated film’s end credit song, I Knew It, I Knew You, while simultaneously managing the gruelling demands of her tour.

“I was on a tour that was — a lot of things — but it was pretty physically exhausting,” she recalled, adding, “I’ve actually never experienced this level of exhaustion in between shows.” (Taylor played a total of 149 shows spanning 51 cities across five continents, with each show being three and a half hours long).

READ MORE: Taylor Swift shares sweet anecdote about friendship with Abigal Anderson

The 14-time Grammy winner revealed that whenever she wasn’t on stage, she would be in bed to rest and recover for her next show. So, when Taylor’s brother Austin, who manages elements of her music licensing for multimedia uses, first approached her about Toy Story 5, she was too exhausted to commit.

She told him, “I just tried to get out of bed and felt every bone in my foot crunch. So is there any leeway that I can have a little time to not be on this tour anymore and then I can go see it?”

For several months, Austin continued to push Taylor to go see the film during its production phase, and when she finally found the time, everything clicked. “Finally, it ended up being the right time where I had the bandwidth to absorb and to have any kind of creative output,” she recalled. “And when I saw this brilliant film that Andrew made, I realised exactly why [Austin] knew I would love it.”

Taylor explained that she could relate to “all the characters” and was especially drawn by the film’s focus of “female friendships.”

“It was a struck-by-lightening moment,” she recalled. “I have to go home, get to my piano, and write this song.”

Taylor previously revealed that she wrote, produced, and finished I Knew It, I Knew You in just five hours after coming home from the screening and getting the “songwriter zoomies.”

headline: Buckingham Palace shares Princess Anne's warm response to royal invitation
subheadline: Princess Anne’s private secretary shares how school could secure a royal return visit
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Abbot’s Hill School received an unexpected royal surprise after marking four decades since the opening of one of its most cherished buildings.

The school revealed that it had received a letter from Buckingham Palace after writing to Princess Anne to recall her visit on 9 October 1986, when she officially opened St Nicholas House Hall.

The letter, sent on the Princess Royal’s behalf by her Private Secretary, Colonel John W Boyd, thanked the school for sharing memories of the occasion and inviting her to return.

Read More: Princess Anne makes rare remark about power of connection

It explained that the Princess Royal’s diary is arranged six months in advance and suggested contacting the local Lord-Lieutenant, who could submit a formal request on the school's behalf.

The message also showed that Anne had taken an interest in how the hall has continued to serve the school over the years.

She was pleased to hear that it remains a central part of daily life, providing a gathering place for pupils during lessons, activities and important moments in the school calendar.

She also expressed her gratitude for a photograph taken during her visit in 1986 and sent her best wishes to the school's staff and pupils.

Sharing the letter on Instagram, Abbot’s Hill described it as a post-half-term surprise, it was a fitting way to bring its 40th anniversary celebrations to a close.

Abbot’s Hill School received an unexpected royal surprise after marking four decades since the opening of one of its most cherished buildings.

The school revealed that it had received a letter from Buckingham Palace after writing to Princess Anne to recall her visit on 9 October 1986, when she officially opened St Nicholas House Hall.

The letter, sent on the Princess Royal’s behalf by her Private Secretary, Colonel John W Boyd, thanked the school for sharing memories of the occasion and inviting her to return.

Read More: Princess Anne makes rare remark about power of connection 

It explained that the Princess Royal’s diary is arranged six months in advance and suggested contacting the local Lord-Lieutenant, who could submit a formal request on the school's behalf.

The message also showed that Anne had taken an interest in how the hall has continued to serve the school over the years. 

She was pleased to hear that it remains a central part of daily life, providing a gathering place for pupils during lessons, activities and important moments in the school calendar.

She also expressed her gratitude for a photograph taken during her visit in 1986 and sent her best wishes to the school's staff and pupils.

Sharing the letter on Instagram, Abbot’s Hill described it as a post-half-term surprise, it was a fitting way to bring its 40th anniversary celebrations to a close.

headline: Netflix's new heist thriller turns into a global sensation
subheadline: The Spanish crime thriller premiered on October 30, 2026
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Netflix found another film that viewers cannot stop watching as its new crime thriller Collision Course took the number one spot on the streaming platform around the world.

The film was released on October 30 and has quickly become a major hit in many countries.

The story starts with a group of thieves who rob a bank in Madrid, Spain. They manage to carry out the robbery but their plan takes bad turn when their getaway car crashes.

READ MORE: Keanu Reeves joins Netflix's 'Maelstrom' after casting shakeup

What happens next makes the story even more interesting, as the accident bring out secrets that the robbers was hiding from each other.

Set in 2013, the film, however, also shows a difficult time in Spain as the country was dealing with money problems, fewer jobs and political scandals.

These problems is the main background of the story, while the robbers face trouble of their own.

Directed by Daniel Sánchez Arévalo, the film features Laia Costa, Karra Elejalde, Luis Zahera and Tamar Novas.

READ MORE: Is Sydney Sweeney the next James Bond girl?

But not everyone has been impressed as some viewers have really enjoyed the twists and different ways of telling the story meanwhile others found the plot hard to follow.

Still, the mixed reactions have not stopped Collision Course from attracting a huge audience and becoming Netflix's biggest global hit.

headline: Lindsay Clancy faces fresh murder trial after 11-1 jury deadlock in children's murder case
subheadline: Clancy is charged with killing her children, Cora, 5; Dawson, 3; and 8-month-old Callan
author: Web Desk
article_text:
An American mother facing a murder conviction for killing her three young children may have to go on trial again after 11 out of the 12 jurors reportedly sided with her on insanity grounds.

Lindsay Clancy, 36, will appear before a Massachusetts court on Monday, November 2, as her lawyers try to get the charges dismissed, after one holdout juror kept the trial from reaching a unanimous verdict in September.

Clancy is charged with killing her children, Cora, 5; Dawson, 3; and 8-month-old Callan in their Duxbury home in January 2023.

Her defense argued that Clancy was suffering from postpartum psychosis, having hallucinations and was not in her right state of mind when she strangled her children with exercise bands.

Prosecutors, however, argued that Clancy knew what she was doing and meant to kill the kids.

A 12-member jury deliberated on the case for six weeks, held several votes over the course of six weeks but couldn’t reach a unanimous conclusion and it was declared a mistrial on September 4, 2026.

One holdout juror disagreed with 11 others who decided to acquit Clancy on grounds of insanity.

Her lawyers now argue that Judge William Sullivan should have investigated whether the holdout juror was following the court's instructions before declaring a mistrial.

They contend that putting Clancy on trial again would violate constitutional protections against double jeopardy.

Prosecutors have rejected that argument, insisting the judge acted appropriately and that they should be allowed to pursue another trial.

headline: Queen Camilla reacts to King Charles awkward rain moment
subheadline: The Queen playfully tests the King's patience, saying with her iconic move: 'I have given up'
author: Shehzad Hameed
article_text:
In a hilarious moment that left the British monarch awkwardly soaked in the rain, the Queen seemingly prioritised her own safety over a romantic couple moment under one umbrella even though the weather had given them a perfect opportunity to create an iconic memory together.

Instead of taking care of her beloved partner, the Queen playfully tested the King's patience. She left him getting wet to enjoy the rain herself and walked away to a sheltered spot.

She knew the moment would be captured on camera and would make headlines, as she was seen laughing and enjoying it to the fullest.

READ MORE: King Charles finally gets his umbrella — watch his hilarious reaction

Undopubtedly, it was classic Camilla creating the perfect topic for dinner-table discussion, as the royal couple often roast each other in the most funny and loving way.

The monet went viral and shared on social media with different captions.

In a delightful video that left royal watchers in stitches, Camilla couldn't stop laughing, gesturing to her damp dress and the humidity playing havoc with her frizzy hair, she jokingly declared: “I’ve given up.”

The monarch and his wife's later conversation will surely be featured in future documentaries and books. It is yet to be revealed how King Charles reacted to the Queen's playful gesture and what the two discussed afterwardsa s it was big moment for both of them during their crucial Caribbean tour.

Apart from this cheeky moment, Queen Camilla has been a steadfast and amazing pillar of strength for King Charles, standing by him as he bravely continues his fight against cancer, proving that behind every playful roast is a love that weathers every storm.

headline: Have Katie Price and Lee Andrews got back together?
subheadline: She later talked about their problems on Good Morning Britain
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Katie Price has once again left people guessing about her marriage to Lee Andrews after showing off her wedding ring at a Halloween party.

The sighting has raised questions about if the pair have put their problems behind them.

Katie married Lee in Dubai in January, just days after they met. At first, the couple seemed happy together but things soon changed when Katie started questioning his claims about being a millionaire.

The trouble, however, got massier when Katie reportedly ended their marriage through WhatsApp while Lee was in prison.

READ MORE: Lee Andrews sends romantic message to estranged wife Katie Price amid split

She later talked about their problems on Good Morning Britain in September.

During the interview, the reality star said she felt Lee fooled her by creating a false image of himself.

She explained that his claims about money sounded attractive but she also said she had genuinely fallen in love with him.

Lee also sent a voice message to the show as he denied lying about having $50 million in his crypto wallet and said he would never stop loving Katie.

Now, the pair have started raising questions again.

READ MORE: Netflix's new heist thriller turns into a global sensation

Katie was recently seen wearing her large diamond wedding ring while celebrating Halloween in Manchester. Both also shared the same romantic message online over the weekend.

headline: Gracie Abrams stuns onlookers with Halloween transformation for 'SNL' party
subheadline: Gracie Abrams leaves fans surprised with third Halloween costume after 'SNL'
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Gracie Abrams went full out this Halloween and served not one but several looks - including her two Saturday Night Live looks, and then a vampire costume for the afterparty.

The 27-year-old pop superstar left fans stunned on social media as the pictures of the afterparty went viral on the internet.

The Here You Come, There You Go hitmaker turned up in a white dress covered in blood with pale makeup and black long haired wig and looked nearly unrecognisable.

Fans flocked to X and reacted to the look, writing, "she ate i can’t even lie," and "my beautiful vampire."

A third chimed in, "She looks like a completely different person but she ATE," and "okayy queen," wrote another.

Someone exclaimed, "THE LONG HAIR OMGGGGGG," and another agreed, "i miss her long hair ngl."

headline: Hackers hit Ukraine and Russia's emergency apps, send fake nuclear alerts
subheadline: Ukraine temporarily suspends its air raid app after hackers sent fabricated emergency warnings
author: Reuters
article_text:
Ukraine and Russia said their emergency alert apps had been hacked overnight, sending false warnings to citizens about impending air raids and chemical and nuclear attacks.

The warnings coincided with the expiry of a six-day local ceasefire brokered by US first lady Melania Trump in a small area of southern Ukraine — the longest such pause in fighting since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.

Ukraine's public air raid app started to send false alerts just before 11 p.m. (2100 GMT) on Sunday for the capital Kyiv and other areas, warning of radiation and chemical attacks and also the risk of street combat in some areas.

Hours later, Russian state news agency TASS quoted the Emergencies Ministry in Moscow as saying that its own mobile app had also been hit by a cyberattack that resulted in fake public warnings being transmitted.

Reuters was unable to verify which groups were responsible. Experts have linked previous cyber security incidents during the almost five-year-old war to activist hackers as well as intelligence agencies on both sides.

In Ukraine, one of the alarms said Russia had launched a hypersonic Oreshnik missile — which is capable of carrying a nuclear warhead — and that a nuclear alert had been declared.

Ukraine's air force said shortly after on the Telegram messaging app that the alert system appeared to have been hacked by Russia, noting that the alerts were broadcast in Russian. The Ukrainian language is compulsory for all official communications in Ukraine.

"The air alert app appears to have been subjected to enemy influence," the air force said. "There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel!"

Kyiv residents unfazed by false alerts

All-clear messages were sent shortly afterwards for each alert and Ukraine's Ministry for Digital Transformation said the app had been temporarily suspended, but other means of alerting the public were functioning, as were air raid sirens.

Ukraine is suffering from a critical lack of air defences, particularly US-made Patriot interceptors that are its only effective defence against Russian ballistic missiles. The US on Friday announced a $2.1 billion deal to supply 500 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine, but two people briefed on the decision said it could take years for the missiles to arrive.

On the streets of Kyiv, residents played down the impact of the hack.

Artem Pyndyk, 37, a businessman, said he was briefly surprised to see the messages but then realised what had happened.

"This didn't trigger the kind of reaction in society that they expected," said Pyndyk, adding that family members and friends he had checked in with had also not panicked.

"You can laugh about it but, on the other hand, they gained a certain level of access and were able to hack the programme."

Oksana Vostrykova, 48, also shrugged off the incident.

"I am calm about it, I kind of immediately understood that it might be a false message," the pizzeria employee said. "You worry more not for yourself but for your children who are nearby."

Russian ministry says its app was also hit

Atesh, a pro-Ukrainian hacking group, posted a screenshot of the alert message seen in Russia on its Telegram channel early on Monday, with a message saying: "The Ministry of Emergency Situations app has been hacked!"

However, the Moscow ministry played down the impact, saying the app was not one of its main public warning system channels, but just what it called a supplementary source of information.

A fake message posted by the hackers, seen by Reuters, did not attempt to mimic an official communication and was laced with colloquialisms, profanities and derogatory language about Russia, calling its regions "swamps".

The fake message told Russians that nuclear warheads had been launched against all Russian regions and advised people to stock up on three weeks of food and shelter in their cellars.

The Russian ministry said its experts were working to restore the app to normal operation.

"We ask the public to remain calm and to trust only official sources of information — the Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations’ website and the department’s official social media accounts," it said.

Ukraine and Russia said their emergency alert apps had been hacked overnight, sending false warnings to citizens about impending air raids and chemical and nuclear attacks.

The warnings coincided with the expiry of a six-day local ceasefire brokered by US first lady Melania Trump in a small area of southern Ukraine — the longest such pause in fighting since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.

Ukraine's public air raid app started to send false alerts just before 11 p.m. (2100 GMT) on Sunday for the capital Kyiv and other areas, warning of radiation and chemical attacks and also the risk of street combat in some areas.

Hours later, Russian state news agency TASS quoted the Emergencies Ministry in Moscow as saying that its own mobile app had also been hit by a cyberattack that resulted in fake public warnings being transmitted.

Reuters was unable to verify which groups were responsible. Experts have linked previous cyber security incidents during the almost five-year-old war to activist hackers as well as intelligence agencies on both sides.

In Ukraine, one of the alarms said Russia had launched a hypersonic Oreshnik missile — which is capable of carrying a nuclear warhead — and that a nuclear alert had been declared.

Ukraine's air force said shortly after on the Telegram messaging app that the alert system appeared to have been hacked by Russia, noting that the alerts were broadcast in Russian. The Ukrainian language is compulsory for all official communications in Ukraine.

"The air alert app appears to have been subjected to enemy influence," the air force said. "There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel!"

Kyiv residents unfazed by false alerts

All-clear messages were sent shortly afterwards for each alert and Ukraine's Ministry for Digital Transformation said the app had been temporarily suspended, but other means of alerting the public were functioning, as were air raid sirens.

Ukraine is suffering from a critical lack of air defences, particularly US-made Patriot interceptors that are its only effective defence against Russian ballistic missiles. The US on Friday announced a $2.1 billion deal to supply 500 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine, but two people briefed on the decision said it could take years for the missiles to arrive.

On the streets of Kyiv, residents played down the impact of the hack.

Artem Pyndyk, 37, a businessman, said he was briefly surprised to see the messages but then realised what had happened.

"This didn't trigger the kind of reaction in society that they expected," said Pyndyk, adding that family members and friends he had checked in with had also not panicked.

"You can laugh about it but, on the other hand, they gained a certain level of access and were able to hack the programme."

Oksana Vostrykova, 48, also shrugged off the incident.

"I am calm about it, I kind of immediately understood that it might be a false message," the pizzeria employee said. "You worry more not for yourself but for your children who are nearby."

Russian ministry says its app was also hit

Atesh, a pro-Ukrainian hacking group, posted a screenshot of the alert message seen in Russia on its Telegram channel early on Monday, with a message saying: "The Ministry of Emergency Situations app has been hacked!"

However, the Moscow ministry played down the impact, saying the app was not one of its main public warning system channels, but just what it called a supplementary source of information.

A fake message posted by the hackers, seen by Reuters, did not attempt to mimic an official communication and was laced with colloquialisms, profanities and derogatory language about Russia, calling its regions "swamps".

The fake message told Russians that nuclear warheads had been launched against all Russian regions and advised people to stock up on three weeks of food and shelter in their cellars.

The Russian ministry said its experts were working to restore the app to normal operation.

"We ask the public to remain calm and to trust only official sources of information — the Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations’ website and the department’s official social media accounts," it said.

headline: Provision of loans to SMEs top priority of govt: PM Shehbaz
subheadline: Federal govt targets Rs1,500 billion in agriculture and SME loans by 2027
author: APP
article_text:
PM urges banks to accelerate lending to priority sectors.
Apna Ghar scheme secures Rs511bn in approved loans.
Premier directs SBP, FBR to resolve SME tax issues.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Monday that improvement in the economy and employment provision to youth through development of small and medium enterprises, housing and agriculture sectors was the top priority of the government.

He was chairing a review meeting on facilitation of credit provision to priority sectors.

In his remarks during the meeting, he said: "Banks that are performing well in facilitating credit provision to agriculture, housing and small and medium enterprises under government initiatives are commendable."

"The State Bank and the Ministry of Finance should not give concessions to banks that are slow in providing loans to farmers, small and medium enterprises and consumers under the Prime Minister's Apna Ghar scheme, a part of government initiatives," he added.

He said: "Banks are of key importance for the development of the private sector. Banks should extend cooperation in providing loans to priority sectors in the same way as the government and its agencies cooperate with banks."

"Small and medium enterprises have great potential to grow the economy, promote exports and create employment opportunities. The agriculture sector is the backbone of the country’s economy and efforts are being made to increase exports through value addition of agricultural commodities," he remarked.

He said: "Apna Ghar scheme will promote many industries related to the housing and construction sector."

The premier directed the finance minister to resolve issues related to financing of stakeholders of the SME sector, agriculture and housing sectors and formulate a comprehensive action plan.

The prime minister also directed the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to jointly resolve tax issues of small and medium enterprises and exporters.

He directed to formulate a comprehensive risk coverage strategy for easy provision of loans to small and medium enterprises.

During the briefing, the participants were informed that to increase the provision of loans to priority sectors, the SBP is working on three basic pillars, which include improving regulations, sharing of risks and costs between the government and banks, and promotion of digital facilities.

In this regard, the SME Connect digital portal has been recently launched for SMEs, through which business people will be able to apply for loans and also see the progress of their applications.

The meeting was told in the briefing that significant progress has been made by the central bank in providing loans on a priority basis to housing, agriculture and small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

As of October 23, loans worth Rs511 billion have been approved under the PM's Apna Ghar Program, while 86,899 loans have been approved, while loans worth Rs 91 billion have been issued to 15,584 applicants.

The total volume of loans in the housing finance sector has reached Rs455 billion and the number of beneficiary borrowers has reached 187,317.

The meeting was informed that the volume of loans in the agriculture sector is Rs1,329 billion and the number of beneficiaries is about 3.5 million, while the volume of loans in the SME sector has reached Rs1,148 billion and the number of entrepreneurs receiving loans has reached 342,458.

The meeting was informed that targets have been set to increase the volume of loans in the agriculture and SME sectors to Rs1,500 billion by the end of the financial year 2027.

The meeting was told that the government has also introduced risk sharing and credit guarantee measures for housing, agriculture and SME sectors, while work is also underway to simplify the procedure for obtaining loans, reduce the required documentation and improve access to financial resources through digital systems.

The participants were also presented performance indicators of commercial banks in the three priority sectors. The prime minister praised the banks showing good performance.

The meeting was attended by Federal Ministers Ahsan Iqbal, Rana Tanveer Hussain, Dr Musadik Malik, Mian Riaz Hussain Pirzada, Muhammad Aurangzeb, Attaullah Tarar, Shaza Fatima Khawaja, Advisor to the Prime Minister Haroon Akhtar, Minister of State Bilal Azhar Kayani, SBP Governor Jamil Ahmed, Members of National Assembly Hafeezuddin, Chaudhry Iftikhar Nazir and relevant senior officials.

The meeting was also attended by heads and representatives of leading commercial banks.

headline: Oil prices sink on US-Iran detente hopes ahead of midterms
subheadline: Brent crude falls 6% to $106.60, WTI drops 6.4% to $97.49 per barrel
author: AFP
article_text:
Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz, if conditions met.
Pezeshkian says Khamenei authorised govt for US talks.
Energy shares decline as gas prices also fall.

Oil prices sank more than 6% on Monday, the eve of crucial midterm elections in the United States, as signals that Tehran and Washington were ready to resume talks boosted hopes of ending the Middle East war.

Brent North Sea crude fell 6% to $106.60 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dropped 6.4% to $97.49 per barrel.

The Axios news outlet reported that US Vice President JD Vance had sent a letter to Iranian national security chief Mohsen Rezaei about possible new talks, marking the highest-level move in months.

Iran meanwhile said it was ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days should the United States agree to ending the war on all fronts, among other conditions related to the conflict.

Later, President Masoud Pezeshkian said the country's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei had granted "powers" to the government in its talks with the United States seeking to end the Middle East war.

Share prices of energy majors dropped as gas prices also fell, while many other sectors were boosted by the cooling fuel costs.

"We believe the (Trump) signals may be tactical ahead of tomorrow's US midterm elections," noted Arne Lohmann Rasmussen, chief analyst at Global Risk Management.

"Meanwhile, attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz continue (and) we maintain our higher-for-longer outlook for energy prices."

All eyes are on Tuesday's midterms, with Democrats expecting to win at least partial control of Congress that would impose political constraints on Trump for the first time in two years.

The loss of total Republican dominance would push the president into unfamiliar and uncomfortable territory: a lame-duck period beset with high inflation at home, the sputtering war against Iran and hostile Democratic investigations into his activities in Washington.

"Investors are bracing for a fresh round of turbulence ahead of US midterm election fireworks while they assess the extent that companies are burning through cash to keep the AI bonfires burning," said Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club.

Technology firms' share prices recovered modestly on Wall Street after Friday's sell-off, as more poorly received earnings from US titans fanned deepening concerns about the investment boom for artificial intelligence.

Results updates from Apple, which reports after the close of trading on Monday, as well as Advanced Micro Devices and software titan Palantir will be closely watched this week.

"With Apple starting things off, the earnings cadence will start with a bang, only we won't know until after the close if that 'bang' is a celebratory bang or a take-cover kind of bang," said analyst Patrick O'Hare at Briefing.com.

Concerns about the profitability of AI-related firms did not disappear altogether.

The share price of Japanese chipmaker Kioxia plunged nearly 16% on Monday after the company gave a cautious outlook that fell short of forecasts.

The company's stock has plunged about 70% from its record high set in June, though it is still up more than 200% since the start of the year.

Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies were steadier after Friday's retreat triggered by the world's biggest crypto exchange Binance suffering the sector's largest hack, of more than $6 billion stolen.

On the corporate front, shares in Alstom plunged over 25% after the maker of France's TGV trains said it had uncovered new production issues with its new Coradia Max regional trains.

That forced it to lower its profit targets for the second time in six months. Its market value is now just 5.3bn euros, compared with 12bn euros at the beginning of the year.

headline: Harry Styles bids goodbye to NYC residency with grand celebration
subheadline: Harry Styles commemorates MSG residency with overnight gala
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Harry Styles just concluded his memorable 30 nights run at Madison Square Garden, New York City, with the last show celebrating the city's culture - including Pizza Rat meme.

The 32-year-old musician ended the show with an emotional moment where even he could not hold his tears back.

Following the last show, the One Direction alum turned to Despacio and threw a party which lasted until 6am.

READ MORE: Harry Styles breaks down on stage after record-breaking MSG Residency

Pictures from the night showed the Coming Up Roses hitmaker celebrating the joy in a shirt which said, "I am a Rat."

Fans reacted to the pictures, writing on X, "And there were people who were sure he was going to run the NYC marathon today," and "what an amazing rat."

A third chimed in, "i have so much fomo," and another agreed, "I'm so jealous."

While someone applauded, "That run looked like an absolute movie from start to finish."

headline: Mckenna Grace opens up about vulnerability in being 'loud' about love life
subheadline: Mckenna Grace gets candid about publicly showing love to boyfriend Mason Thames
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Mckenna Grace and Mason Thames became friends to co-stars and co-stars to lovers, and the internet followed their journey because they hard-launched their relationship on social media.

The couple have since shared the screen multiple times and continue to show love to each other on the internet, and the Hunger Games star was asked about whether she thinks about the internet judgement before publicly showing her relationship.

Grace said, "I don't see the point in not celebrating who you're in love with. A lot of people's hesitation around this stems from the idea that if you post about someone a bunch and then you break up, that's embarrassing. But why would I even think about that? I'm just going to focus on the present."

The Regretting You actress continued, "It’s a terrifying thing in a relationship to surrender yourself to that thought of, I’m just going to be at my most vulnerable and trust you, and this part of my life is fully in your hands. But I don’t see the point in building a relationship based on fear. I am the biggest fan of the person I’m with, so why wouldn’t I be like, 'This is my person. I am so stoked I have this?' We’re always on each other’s sets anyway. He’s like an honorary member of District 12 at this point.”

READ MORE: Mckenna Grace channels Katniss with iconic ‘Hunger Games' dress

Fans flocked to X to react to the comments, and wrote, "Awwwww," and "If they marry young, I am okay with it."

A third chimed in, "There’s something refreshing about not letting the fear of how things might end stop you from enjoying what you have now."

Another applauded, "This is actually such a healthy way to look at relationships online. why should people hide who they love just because of internet judgment. the way people treat a young celebrity talking about dating like it's a major cultural event is wild."

headline: Tom Hardy, Olivia Colman's dark film returns to streaming
subheadline: Tom Hardy plays Mark, while Olivia Colman stars as Julie
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Tom Hardy and Olivia Colman have a film together that many people have missed but it is now getting another chance to reach viewers.

Their film London Road is available on Prime Video, bringing real and disturbing story back into the spotlight.

The film is based on a series of murders that took place near London Road in Ipswich, England. It, however, does not tell the story from the killer's side. but it shows what exactly happened to the people who lived in that area and how their lives changed after murders.

READ MORE: ‘MobLand' season 3 teases a new chapter for Tom Hardy

As reporters arrived and the neighbourhood came under public attention, local people had to deal with fear, questions and unwanted attention. The film also shows how they tried to bring their community back together.

What makes London Road different is that its songs are made from real interviews. The words spoken by residents, sex workers and reporters were used to create the film's music and conversations.

READ MORE: Have Katie Price and Lee Andrews got back together?

Tom Hardy plays Mark meanwhile Olivia Colman stars as Julie. The cast, moreover, also include Anita Dobson and Kate Fleetwood.

The film received positive reviews and got 76% score on Rotten Tomatoes.

headline: Supermarket freezers hacked across seven European countries: Here's everything to know
subheadline: Fridge hacks raise food security fears as spoiled stock piles up across Europe
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A suspected coordinated cyber-attack has disrupted refrigerator and freezer systems at dozens of supermarkets across at least seven European countries.

This forces stores to discard large quantities of spoiled food and prompts national cybersecurity agencies to issue alerts.

Around 40 Delhaize supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, along with fewer stores in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia, and Finland.

In Sweden, several ICA and Coop shops reported that freezer temperatures had been remotely set as high as 50 degrees Celsius, with one ICA branch in Sjöbo writing on social media that its refrigerators had been “hacked overnight.”

Ireland’s SuperValu confirmed a “cyber incident” at 13 of its 233 stores, while a Selver supermarket in Estonia and K-stores in Finland also reported malfunctions.

Sabcobel, the Belgian manufacturer responsible for Delhaize’s refrigeration systems, explained that the evaporators were defrosted and that the attack used the same tactic as the attack on French supermarkets the previous month. Company CEO, Stephan Moelans, stated that the company “had worked through the night and morning to disconnect the affected units from the network” and that the equipment needed hardware changes and not software updates.

UK's National Cyber Security Centre explained that it was working with international partners and industry to "fully understand details of an incident." The British Retail Consortium clarified that it was working with local businesses. So far, there have been no incidents reported in the UK. Christophe Hansen, the European Commissioner for Agriculture and Food, said that "it is a deliberate disruption attempt against the EU food system," though he insisted that food security is not an issue now.

Losses are mounting, with a Delhaize branch in Hoeilaart, Belgium, estimating €100,000 in spoiled produce, while a Swedish store manager reported ruined stock and uncontrolled temperatures. The hacker is still not identified.

headline: Maya Hawke addresses her wedding pictures being leaked: 'Kind of happy'
subheadline: The 'Stranger Things' star, 28, married musician Christian Lee Hutson, 35, on Valentine's Day 2026
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Maya Hawke never wanted her wedding pictures to run in the press, but she was strangely relieved when they did.

The Stranger Things star opened up about her Valentine’s Day wedding in a new interview with Cosmopolitan published on Monday, November 2, explaining why she opted out of running her wedding photos in the press like other celebrities.

“I’m not going to lie and be like, ‘I never for one second considered it.’ I genuinely thought about it,” she admitted. “But the only thing I’ve known that I wanted to do on my wedding day since I was a kid was walk with the whole wedding party.”

READ MORE: Maya Hawke shares her biggest lesson from wedding to Christian Lee

Hawke, 28, married musician Christian Lee Hutson, 35, in a surprise ceremony on February 14, 2026, in New York City. Their wedding party was photographed walking through the streets, with guests including Hawke’s parents, Ethan Hawke and Uma Thurman, and several of her co-stars.

According to Cosmopolitan, “only one lone paparazzo” managed to capture the procession, and the photographs were run in People magazine.

headline: PTI lawyer says Adiala officials facilitated 40-minute meeting with Imran, Bushra
subheadline: Barrister Safdar says Imran, Bushra briefed him on their health, living conditions and pending legal matters
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Lawyer meets Imran after seven months, Bushra after 11.
Couple gives fresh instructions on pending legal cases.
Imran remains imprisoned at Adiala jail since August 2023.

Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) lawyer Barrister Salman Safdar on Monday said Adiala jail authorities facilitated a 40-minute meeting with PTI founder Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, after repeated requests.

In a post on X, the lawyer said the meeting took place at 4:30pm, adding that he met the former prime minister after seven months and Bushra after 11 months.

"After repeated applications and requests, I met Khan sahib after seven months and BB after 11 months," Safdar wrote.

He said the meeting was insufficient to cover all pending cases and legal matters. However, both Imran and Bushra briefed him on their health and living conditions and gave him fresh instructions regarding certain cases.

Imran has remained behind bars at Adiala jail since August 2023, facing a series of corruption and terrorism-related cases following his ouster from power in April 2022.

He is currently serving prison sentences in the Al-Qadir Trust and Toshakhana (Bulgari jewellery set) cases. His convictions in two other Toshakhana references have been suspended pending appeals.

The PTI founder also faces several cases linked to the May 9, 2023 riots, which erupted following his arrest. The party has consistently rejected the allegations against him, maintaining that the cases are politically motivated.

Political tensions surrounding his imprisonment escalated in October when PTI launched a long march towards Islamabad, led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, who is now dysfunctional due to emergency measures in the province.

The march began in Lakki Marwat on October 4, with protesters demanding Imran's release and access to medical treatment, including a meeting with his personal doctor.

However, on October 11, President Asif Ali Zardari proclaimed an emergency and imposed governor's rule in the province on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, effectively suspending the PTI-led provincial government.

The federal government cited the deteriorating security situation and alleged shortcomings in the provincial administration's counterterrorism efforts.

Following the imposition of governor's rule, Afridi and several provincial cabinet members were taken into preventive custody.

The major opposition party also claimed that its provincial president, Junaid Akbar, had been arrested.

Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry subsequently confirmed the detentions, saying those facing cases would be charged and tried, while others would be released.

Meanwhile, restrictions on meetings with Imran at Adiala jail have repeatedly drawn criticism from his party and family, who have called for greater access to the incarcerated leader.

In September 2026, the Islamabad High Court (IHC) directed jail authorities to end the isolation of Imran and Bushra and ensure they were provided facilities in accordance with prison rules.

headline: Trump administration takes California ballot fight to Supreme Court
subheadline: Justice Dept seeks to prevent counting “disputed ballots” until each voter's citizenship status can be verified
author: Reuters
article_text:
Trump admin asks SC to halt California mail-in ballot count.
State says suit could disenfranchise many eligible voters.
Lawsuit marks rare federal intervention in voting process.

President Donald Trump's administration asked the US Supreme Court on Monday to temporarily block California from counting mail-in ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters who federal officials allege are likely non-US citizens.

Escalating a legal fight that could affect thousands of voters in the November 3 midterm elections, the Justice Department filed the emergency request as it seeks to prevent counting the disputed ballots until each voter's citizenship status can be verified.

A federal appeals court refused the request on Friday.

Trump's fellow Republicans are fighting to retain control of Congress in the midterms. California is the most populous US state and a Democratic stronghold.

The administration has intensified its focus on alleged noncitizen voting in the run-up to the midterms. Trump has made false claims about widespread US voting fraud, including in the 2020 election lost to Democrat Joe Biden. Multiple studies and state audits show that ineligible voting, including by noncitizens, is rare.

Constitutional questions

The US Constitution assigns the responsibility of administering elections to states, though the federal government has some oversight. The lawsuit marked a rare federal intervention in the voting process and signaled a willingness by the administration to contest the election results in court.

The administration already sought to restrict voting by mail — a mode of casting ballots used more often by Democratic-leaning voters — but the Supreme Court in September rebuffed that effort.

The list of 20,000 registered voters was amassed by the US Department of Homeland Security and sent to California officials and to Los Angeles County officials.

The Justice Department sued in federal court on October 15, claiming California is unlawfully preventing its enforcement of a 1996 US law that makes it a criminal offense for noncitizens to vote in federal elections. The department said California's action violated the US Constitution's Supremacy Clause, which holds that federal law generally preempts state law.

The administration asked the Supreme Court to order California to separate any ballots cast by people on the list from other ballots, and not to count them until those voters are verified as citizens.

"Once illegally cast ballots are counted and commingled with lawful votes, the resulting harm is impossible to remedy," the Justice Department wrote in a filing in the case.

California has said that the state's safeguards against noncitizen voting are robust and that the lawsuit threatens to deprive 20,000 people of their right to vote based on vague accusations. The administration's process for scrutinizing voter lists to identify noncitizens is flawed and likely rife with errors, it said in court papers.

'Bend to the will'

US District Judge David Carter in Los Angeles denied the administration's request on October 28.

"Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the executive branch," Carter wrote.

Carter raised concerns over the reliability of the administration's data, noting that people recently flagged by the federal government as noncitizens on voter rolls in other states have repeatedly turned out to be naturalized US citizens.

"If the executive can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger," Carter wrote.

The San Francisco-based 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals also refused on Friday to block the ballots, emphasizing the state's power over election procedures and California's "comprehensive statutory scheme to ensure the integrity of its elections," including a system for canceling registrations if a voter is shown to be ineligible.

Siding with the administration could result in disenfranchisement "and could jeopardize the county's entire election," the 9th Circuit said.

The Supreme Court's review of the administration's emergency request could take into account the short time frame before election day.

In September, the justices barred Missouri from using a redrawn map of the state's House districts designed to favor Republicans in the midterms. Reinstating that map "in the midst of an ongoing election would usher in electoral chaos," the court said in that ruling.

Administration demands

The administration has taken an increasingly aggressive approach toward how states run elections. The Justice Department has told election officials in all 50 states that they could face criminal prosecution if they knowingly allow noncitizens to remain on their rolls or cast ballots. It has lost a series of lawsuits seeking to obtain voter rolls, including sensitive personal information, from dozens of states.

A Reuters investigation published in July found just 129 cases in which noncitizens had been charged with voting illegally since the passage of a 1996 federal law criminalizing such conduct. Many appeared to stem from voter confusion or administrative errors, rather than intentional fraud.

Trump has made California a focal point of his sweeping immigration crackdown. California has 52 seats in the House of Representatives, more than any other state. Democrats need a net gain of four House seats to win a majority in the chamber.

article_html:
• Trump admin asks SC to halt California mail-in ballot count.
  • State says suit could disenfranchise many eligible voters.
  • Lawsuit marks rare federal intervention in voting process.

President Donald Trump's administration asked the US Supreme Court on Monday to temporarily block California from counting mail-in ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters who federal officials allege are likely non-US citizens.

Escalating a legal fight that could affect thousands of voters in the November 3 midterm elections, the Justice Department filed the emergency request as it seeks to prevent counting the disputed ballots until each voter's citizenship status can be verified.

A federal appeals court refused the request on Friday.

Trump's fellow Republicans are fighting to retain control of Congress in the midterms. California is the most populous US state and a Democratic stronghold.

The administration has intensified its focus on alleged noncitizen voting in the run-up to the midterms. Trump has made false claims about widespread US voting fraud, including in the 2020 election lost to Democrat Joe Biden. Multiple studies and state audits show that ineligible voting, including by noncitizens, is rare.

Constitutional questions

The US Constitution assigns the responsibility of administering elections to states, though the federal government has some oversight. The lawsuit marked a rare federal intervention in the voting process and signaled a willingness by the administration to contest the election results in court.

The administration already sought to restrict voting by mail — a mode of casting ballots used more often by Democratic-leaning voters — but the Supreme Court in September rebuffed that effort.

The list of 20,000 registered voters was amassed by the US Department of Homeland Security and sent to California officials and to Los Angeles County officials.

The Justice Department sued in federal court on October 15, claiming California is unlawfully preventing its enforcement of a 1996 US law that makes it a criminal offense for noncitizens to vote in federal elections. The department said California's action violated the US Constitution's Supremacy Clause, which holds that federal law generally preempts state law.

The administration asked the Supreme Court to order California to separate any ballots cast by people on the list from other ballots, and not to count them until those voters are verified as citizens.

"Once illegally cast ballots are counted and commingled with lawful votes, the resulting harm is impossible to remedy," the Justice Department wrote in a filing in the case.

California has said that the state's safeguards against noncitizen voting are robust and that the lawsuit threatens to deprive 20,000 people of their right to vote based on vague accusations. The administration's process for scrutinizing voter lists to identify noncitizens is flawed and likely rife with errors, it said in court papers.

'Bend to the will'

US District Judge David Carter in Los Angeles denied the administration's request on October 28.

"Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the executive branch," Carter wrote.

Carter raised concerns over the reliability of the administration's data, noting that people recently flagged by the federal government as noncitizens on voter rolls in other states have repeatedly turned out to be naturalized US citizens.

"If the executive can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger," Carter wrote.

The San Francisco-based 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals also refused on Friday to block the ballots, emphasizing the state's power over election procedures and California's "comprehensive statutory scheme to ensure the integrity of its elections," including a system for canceling registrations if a voter is shown to be ineligible.

Siding with the administration could result in disenfranchisement "and could jeopardize the county's entire election," the 9th Circuit said.

The Supreme Court's review of the administration's emergency request could take into account the short time frame before election day.

In September, the justices barred Missouri from using a redrawn map of the state's House districts designed to favor Republicans in the midterms. Reinstating that map "in the midst of an ongoing election would usher in electoral chaos," the court said in that ruling.

Administration demands

The administration has taken an increasingly aggressive approach toward how states run elections. The Justice Department has told election officials in all 50 states that they could face criminal prosecution if they knowingly allow noncitizens to remain on their rolls or cast ballots. It has lost a series of lawsuits seeking to obtain voter rolls, including sensitive personal information, from dozens of states.

A Reuters investigation published in July found just 129 cases in which noncitizens had been charged with voting illegally since the passage of a 1996 federal law criminalizing such conduct. Many appeared to stem from voter confusion or administrative errors, rather than intentional fraud.

Trump has made California a focal point of his sweeping immigration crackdown. California has 52 seats in the House of Representatives, more than any other state. Democrats need a net gain of four House seats to win a majority in the chamber.
