headline: 'Hunger Games' reveals massive surprise in 'SOTR' tracklist
subheadline: 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping' announces official tracklist and artists
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping official tracklist and artists has been announced, and it left the franchise's fans even more hyped for the upcoming movie.

The movie features none other than Jennifer Lawrence herself on the track, with a song called, Deep in the Meadow.

The complete list of the artist goes as follows:

Jennifer Lawrence
Whitney Peak
Mckenna Grace
Stevie Nicks
Noah Kahan
Noah Cyrus
Stephen Wilson Jr.
Bella Kay
Lizzy McAlpine
Sydney Rose
Ella Langley
Madeline Edwards
Kacey Musgraves
Billy Vincent
Gigi Perez
Hudson Freeman
The Smashing Pumpkins
Depeche Mode & Karyyn
Emelie Trahan
Kashus Culpepper
Scot Greenan
Carter Faith
Tyler Childers
Madison Cunningham
Violet Grohl
The Cure

READ MORE: 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' discloses major twist before release

Fans flocked to social media as soon as the tracklist was annoucned and wrote, "Jennifer Lawrence???!" another echoed, "JENNIFER LAWRENCE?"

While a third chimed in, "What do you mean Jennifer Lawrence!?!" and "KACEY MUSGRAVES STEVIE NICKS THE CURE AND THE SMASHING PUMPKINS IM DYING."

Another added, "STEVIE NICKS what," and "LIZZY MCALPINE?" as well as "THE HUNGER GAMES SOUNDTRACK IS ABOUT TO BE INSANE. This lineup already has me seated. We are so back."

Someone gushed, "Deep in the Meadow?? Oh tears will be shed."

headline: US Army rehearses digging mass graves for 2,400 soldiers a day as fears of major war grow
subheadline: Soldiers used heavy machinery to dig trenches designed to accommodate 20 bodies each
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The United States (U.S.) Army has initiated a strange exercise that involves training soldeirs to dig mass graves for thousands of fallen soldiers as Iran War continues. This marks the revival of battlefield burial procedures that haven’t been practised or needed since the Korean War in the 1950s.

Though the drills come at a time of escalating tensions between the U.S. and Islamic Republic, the military officials haven’t linked exercises to any particular conflict.

The traning dubbed as Operation Dragon Covenant Phase II involves military engineers, mortuary affairs specialists and chaplains to prepare for a war in which casualties could overwhelm the Army's ability to recover and transport bodies home.

According to the Army, crews operating eight bulldozers and four excavators could potentially prepare temporary burial sites for as many as 2,400 people within 24 hours.

During the exercise, soldiers used heavy machinery to dig trenches designed to accommodate 20 bodies each, completing individual trenches in an average of one hour and 15 minutes.

The military used simulated remains to test whether bodies could be buried without damage and later recovered for identification and repatriation.

Sergeant First Class Delbert Ruede, a senior fatality management official, said the exercise was intended to replace improvised wartime arrangements with procedures tested under realistic conditions.

During the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, American forces were generally able to transport fallen personnel home relatively quickly.

However, a future conflict involving a powerful or distant adversary could disrupt evacuation routes and force commanders to establish temporary battlefield cemeteries.

Military chaplains also participated in the drills, preparing for circumstances in which individual funeral services might not be possible.

The Army plans to conduct another phase of the exercise in spring 2027, incorporating additional medical and security operations.

headline: Who is Kimi Antonelli? Everything to know about F1's newest world champion
subheadline: Kimi Antonelli becomes F1’s youngest world champion at 20
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Kimi Antonelli has just made Formula 1 history, becoming the youngest World Champion in the sport’s history at 20 years and 68 days old.

Antonelli. He needed only a ninth-place finish to clinch the title, developing a composed drive through a chaotic afternoon at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, securing the championship with races to spare. He shattered Sebastian Vettel’s long-standing record of 23 years and 134 days, set in 2010.

Visibly emotional, he said: “It’s a long day I will remember forever. We did it, and without Mercedes and my family I wouldn’t be here. I’m speechless."

Andrea Kimi Antonelli was born on 25 August 2006 in Bologna, Italy, as the son of Marco Antonelli, who is a sportscar racer and owner of the AKM Motorsport team, and Veronica Pomaro. His second name is named after the Finnish racer, Kimi Räikkönen, although he clarified that he was not named after him as the 2007 World Champion.

Scouted by the Minardi Management at the age of eight, Antonelli became a member of the Mercedes Junior Team at the age of 12 in 2018. He won consecutive European karting championships in 2020 and 2021 and became the youngest ever senior European Champion at the age of 14.

Antonelli has become dominant in Italian and ADAC F4 series in 2022 and won a record number of 13 races in the Italian series and the gold medal of Italy at the FIA Motorsport Games while competing with a broken wrist. In 2023, Antonelli won the Formula Regional European and Middle East titles. In 2024, he finished sixth in F2.

In 2025, Antonelli replaced Lewis Hamilton at Mercedes and became the third-youngest driver in F1 history at the age of 18. He scored a podium finish in Canada and set several youngest-driver records, finishing 7th in the standings with 150 points.

headline: Lenny Kravitz addresses 'untrue' reports he died in Florida plane crash
subheadline: Kravitz’s rep clarifies the musician was not onboard the doomed Learjet 60 flight that killed nine people
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Lenny Kravitz was not on the doomed Learjet 60 flight that crashed in Florida.

The musician’s representative, Carleen Donovan, confirmed to BocaNewsNow that speculation about his death was false.

“The reports are untrue and incorrect,” Donovan told the outlet.

READ MORE: Lenny Kravitz shares wholesome moment with daughter Zoe's boyfriend Harry Styles

The rumours emerged after a Learjet 60 bound for the Bahamas crashed in Palm Beach County on Sunday, November 1, killing all nine people aboard. Kravitz, 62, was mistakenly linked to the flight after Florida-based pilot Emily Shelton shared a now-deleted Facebook post about flying him on a similar route.

“Honored to be flying the one and only Lenny Kravitz from [Austin-Bergstrom International Airport] to [North Eleuthera Airport, Bahamas] tomorrow. Looking forward to having him on board,” the post read.

Shelton also denied being the pilot involved in the crash.

“I would like to respectfully clarify I was not,” she wrote. “I ask that people please stop speculating and spreading misinformation on this tragedy and be respectful of those involved. My heart goes out to all those lost and affected.”

The jet crashed near Cresthaven and Greenacres around 12:50 p.m. ET, sparking fires and forcing approximately 600 mobile home residents to evacuate. No one on the ground was injured, while authorities have yet to identify all nine victims.

Shelton also denied being the pilot involved in the crash.

headline: UK to make some migrants wait 10 years to settle, eases rules for carers
subheadline: Care workers retain five-year route to permanent settlement under revised rules
author: Reuters
article_text:
High earners can qualify for settlement after three years.
Mahmood eases care worker rules after Labour backlash.
Labour seeks to avoid rebellion over tougher immigration rules.

Britain unveiled sweeping reforms to its immigration system on Monday, requiring some migrants to wait 10 years or more before they can settle, while granting concessions to some care workers to defuse a political row.

The reforms are the government's latest attempt to toughen the rules after the number of arrivals surged following Britain's departure from the European Union, with post-Brexit immigration policies leading to an influx of healthcare workers and students from around the world.

But government efforts to toughen the rules sparked a backlash from unions and parts of the governing Labour Party, leading interior minister Shabana Mahmood to soften the standard qualifying period for those working in the health and care sector from 10 to 5 years.

While high earners will be granted the right to settle in three years, the toughest restrictions were reserved for those who arrive by small boats across the channel.

"Those who contribute most will settle fastest," Mahmood said. "Those who don't play by the rules will be refused or wait longer."

Govt offers concessions after backlash

Previously, legal migrants had to wait for five years before they could be granted indefinite leave to remain, which allows people to live and work in Britain permanently and be entitled to some welfare benefits.

But the government had argued that changes were needed because around 350,000 lower-skilled workers and their dependants who arrived after Brexit were expected to become eligible for settlement in the coming years.

Under the new rules, most people will now have to wait 10 years before they can apply to settle permanently in Britain.

However, workers in the care sector will still be able to apply after five years, if they meet certain criteria such as having a high standard of English, no criminal record and a record of paying national insurance.

Those who earn more than £125,000 or those with certain visas will be able to settle in three years. Anyone arriving illegally via a small boat will have to wait up to 30 years.

The changes come in response to voter demands for lower immigration and after Nigel Farage's populist Reform UK party led the argument for stricter migration controls.

They are also designed to ward off a rebellion from Labour lawmakers.

headline: Binance clients pull $4.7bn after hack as crypto world studies fallout
subheadline: Hackers stole around $6.3bn of crypto platform in what could be the largest-ever financial heist
author: Reuters
article_text:
Binance's customers have withdrawn a net $4.72 billion from the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange since it reopened, after hackers stole around $6.3bn of crypto from the platform in what could be the largest-ever financial heist.

The exchange froze withdrawals for more than two days after the hack, which the FBI said was carried out by North Korea, then started allowing customers to withdraw again on Sunday morning.

The theft has underlined the vulnerability of digital assets to attacks and raised questions about the impact of the hack on Binance, which has vowed to repay customers in full.

Binance said the net outflows amounted to around 3% of the assets on its platform, a relatively modest figure that analysts said suggested customer confidence had largely held up. Most withdrawals from the platform were in the form of Tether's USDT stablecoin, Binance added.

The outflow compares with about $7bn withdrawn from Circle's USDC stablecoin over a week after the collapse of Silicon Valley Bank in 2023. Binance itself processed net outflows of about $6bn over 72 hours in 2022 after the collapse of FTX.

The attack marks a step-up in North Korea's crypto thefts. Blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs said North Korea-linked hackers have stolen $7.4bn so far in 2026.

Analysts and crypto experts said the fallout appeared limited so far, and there was little sign of an impact on broader financial markets despite deepening ties between crypto and mainstream finance in recent years.

"Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not our users," the company said in a statement on X.

Binance said it was covering the losses with company funds and had already raised $6bn from its corporate treasury, an insurance fund and reserves set aside for security breaches.

"It has not yet triggered widespread panic or a massive, concentrated withdrawal," said Tim Sun, a senior researcher at HashKey Group, a digital asset financial service company in Hong Kong.

Binance, which says it has more than 335 million users worldwide and average daily trading volumes of $95bn across digital assets and derivatives, said it had also seen $2.7bn in customer inflows since Sunday and that withdrawal volumes were stabilising after an "initial spike."

Data from data analytics provider DeFiLlama showed several crypto exchanges received notable inflows to their platforms since Binance opened withdrawals, although it was unclear what share came from users moving funds off Binance.

OKX recorded $284.87m in inflows in the last 24 hours, followed by Gate with $93.22m in inflows and Bybit, which saw $29.25m in inflows. Representatives for OKX, Gate and Bybit did not respond to requests for comment.

No rush to withdraw

Some traders told Reuters they were keeping their accounts on Binance.

Ryan Tan, a Binance user, said he was in no hurry to withdraw his funds from the platform, as he had already kept his account fairly light since the collapse of FTX four years ago.

"After the FTX collapse, I decided to hold everything on my wallet instead of leaving them on exchanges," said the 39-year-old.

After hitting a six-week low on Friday, bitcoin BTC prices recovered through the weekend to trade above $77,000 on Monday, while ether ETH also rebounded from a two-month low.

Stablecoin market capitalisations, often viewed as a gauge of money moving into and out of crypto markets, have fallen since Friday, suggesting some investors have shifted funds into cash or traditional assets. Binance started allowing US dollar cash withdrawals again on Monday.

'Highly complex' money laundering

The FBI said on Saturday that the North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack. Researchers describe the group as highly sophisticated and say its activities help fund the country's weapons programs.

Analysts said the attack's scale could curb institutional appetite for cryptocurrencies. Spot bitcoin ETFs recorded outflows of $643m on Friday, the largest daily withdrawal in October, while more than $1.3bn in leveraged positions were liquidated, according to Ari Redbord, global head of policy at TRM Labs.

"A hack at a crypto exchange is bank robbery at the speed of the internet, which creates an unstable risk profile for anyone responsible for other people's capital," he said.

About half of the stolen funds were held in stablecoins and have been frozen by issuers including Circle, which said on Monday it had frozen more than $1.1bn in USDC.

According to blockchain analytics firm Elliptic, the hackers still control around $3.28bn, mostly in bitcoin and ether, and only a negligible amount has been cashed out of crypto and into fiat currency. Elliptic described the laundering process as "highly complex and clearly automated."

Jonathan Benton, founder and chief executive at crypto asset recovery firm iSanctuary, said blockchain technology exists to trace stolen funds, but the challenge is turning that intelligence into rapid, coordinated action before those assets disappear.

"The future of crypto won't be decided by how much money enters the market, but by how safe that money is once it's there," said Benton, former head of the international corruption unit of the UK's National Crime Agency.

Ryan Tan, a Binance user, said he was in no hurry to withdraw his funds from the platform, as he had already kept his account fairly light since the collapse of FTX four years ago.

The FBI said on Saturday that the North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack. Researchers describe the group as highly sophisticated and say its activities help fund the country's weapons programs.

Spot bitcoin ETFs recorded outflows of $643m on Friday, the largest daily withdrawal in October, while more than $1.3bn in leveraged positions were liquidated, according to Ari Redbord, global head of policy at TRM Labs.

"A hack at a crypto exchange is bank robbery at the speed of the internet, which creates an unstable risk profile for anyone responsible for other people's capital," he said.

headline: King Charles office shares first post after monarch's angry outburst
subheadline: The King and Queen put viral moment firmly behind them
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles' office has shared a graceful new update from Antigua and Barbuda, putting the viral rain moment firmly behind them.

The Palace released details as the King and Queen were escorted through the museum by Dr. Reg Murphy, President of the Historical and Archaeological Society, where they also admired beautiful art created by students of The King’s Foundation Drawing School.

In the clip, shared on the royal family's official Instagram account, the Queen is seen holding an umbrella even under the roof, while the King is also in high spirits as if nothing had happened moments before.

READ MORE: Queen Camilla risks King Charles wrath

The historic heritage museum is situated inside the country's Government House, an important building associated with the nation's colonial administration, political history and independence.

READ MORE: King Charles, Prince Harry's 'secret' deal sparks public fury

headline: ‘Big Brother' star Rhianna breaks silence over Omar's 'toxic' behaviour
subheadline: Rhianna explains that she sometimes found herself apologising to Omar way to much
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Rhianna Collins has spoken about her relationship with Omar El Mayer after leaving the Big Brother house.

She admitted that some of the moments between them were much harder to watch than she had realised.

Since her eviction on Friday, Rhianna has watched clips of their arguments and said she was surprised by her own reactions. During a TikTok livestream, she explained that she sometimes found herself apologising to Omar even when she didn’t do anything wrong.

READ MORE: ‘Big Brother' hit by unexpected exit after contestant quits

She said, "why am I apologising right now?" after seeing some of the scenes again. Rhianna also admitted that she would never want a boy to speak to her in that way again.

Despite this, the reality star made it clear that she still cares about Omar and wants viewers to wait until the reunion before making up their minds.

Rhianna, however, also said that she feels there is a part of her wants to protect him but she knows she must protect herself as well.

READ MORE: Tom Hardy, Olivia Colman's dark film returns to streaming

Omar, whereas, received more than 22,000 complaints from viewers over the way he treated Rhianna.

Big Brother also talked to him about his behaviour inside the house and warned him to think about how his words could make others feel.

Omar defended himself, saying he had only tried to care for Rhianna.

headline: NASA releases eerie space photos showing 'evil eye', giant skull and Sun with creepy smile to celebrate Halloween
subheadline: NASA also included a creepy picture of the Perseus galaxy cluster
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) is celebrating Halloween by sharing some of the weirdest and creepiest pictures from throughout the cosmos. The newest released collection features a large skull, an enigmatic eye looking out into space and a Sun with a smile on its face much like a Halloween pumpkin.

The American space agency published pictures before Halloween, and one of the most dramatic photographs is a picture of the Sun looking like a jack-o'-lantern with two bright eyes and a crooked smile.

The image was actually taken by NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) in October 2014, during a time when the Sun's magnetic activity had produced unusually bright areas in the Sun's atmosphere.

The other image depicts a large formation of turquoise-green colour that looks like a vast eye, known as the Hourglass Nebula or MyCn 18 about 8,000 light-years from Earth.

The image was taken by the Hubble Space Telescope and shows a structure that is formed by the gas that has been ejected from a dying star.

NASA also included a creepy picture of the Perseus galaxy cluster, in which two gigantic dark holes are surrounded by glowing X-rays that look like eyes in a skull.

Strong activity around the massive black hole in the centre of the cluster created the cavities.

Other pictures show an odd eye-like structure around the star Fomalhaut, and the famous Face on Mars, which can be seen as a human face when viewed under certain lighting conditions.

headline: Wizz Air flight from Luton diverted to Budapest after bomb threat: See full details
subheadline: London-Sofia Wizz Air flight makes emergency landing in Hungary
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A Wizz Air flight travelling from London Luton Airport to Sofia was forced to make an emergency landing in Budapest on Monday, November 2, after receiving a bomb threat mid-flight, with a Hungarian fighter jet to escort the aircraft.

Wizz Air flight 4302 departed Luton at 08:33 GMT and was due to arrive in the Bulgarian capital at 13:25 local time. According to flight-tracking data, the Airbus A321 neo was flying over Bosnia and Herzegovina when it changed course and headed north towards Hungary, landing at Budapest Liszt Ferenc International Airport at 12:09 local time.

Hungarian Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi confirmed that a Gripen fighter jet from the Hungarian Defence Forces took to the skies “within minutes” to provide an escort for the passenger aircraft, before returning to its base at Kecskemet.

Control over the situation was handed over to the police on the ground.

According to the statement issued by Wizz Air, "the aircraft landed safely at Budapest Liszt Ferenc International Airport in compliance with the relevant security protocols and procedures, before taxiing to a stand, where the necessary security check was performed on the aircraft and the passengers."

Wizz Air clarified later that the "security check was completed and nothing was found." It was also mentioned that the aircraft would take off very soon in order to proceed to Sofia. Wizz Air assured the people that it is "fully cooperating with the authorities" and "safety of our passengers and crew remains our highest priority."

It is still not clear who made the threat or whether it was made onboard or on the ground. This incident has come at a time when there have been a number of threats in the world of aviation in the past few months, one of them being the hijack threat to a Flydubai flight in September.

headline: 'We're going to crash': Learjet crew's terrifying final 35 seconds captured on audio
subheadline: Flight-tracking data showed the aircraft's descent rate briefly exceeded 32,000 feet per minute
author: Web Desk
article_text:
“We're out of time.” Those were the final words heard from the cockpit of a private jet that crashed in Florida, killing all nine people aboard, as newly released audio revealed the crew's desperate attempts to save the aircraft in its final seconds.

The recording, obtained from air traffic control communications, captured the Learjet 60 crew initially reporting ice accumulation and moderate turbulence while flying towards the Bahamas on Sunday, November 1.

At first, the situation appeared manageable. The crew told controllers they were dealing with the ice but needed smoother flying conditions.

Less than a minute later, the routine conversation turned into an emergency.

"Mayday, mayday," a crew member radioed, warning that the aircraft was descending at 10,000 feet per minute.

Seconds later, the reported descent rate doubled to 20,000 feet per minute as the jet continued losing altitude.

"We're going to crash into the ground," the crew warned.

An air traffic controller attempted to maintain contact, telling the pilots: "I'm here with you. Talk to me."

The crew then reported descending at 22,000 feet per minute, with the aircraft banking sharply.

In the final moments, a voice reportedly shouted for someone named Jack to look outside before the transmission ended with the words: "We're out of time."

The exchange unfolded in roughly 35 seconds, according to Reuters.

Flight-tracking data showed the aircraft's descent rate briefly exceeded 32,000 feet per minute before it struck a residential area in Palm Beach County and exploded.

The jet had departed Austin, Texas, and was heading to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas.

The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating the crash. Although the crew reported icing and turbulence, investigators have not established what caused the aircraft to lose control.

headline: Pakistani-Americans among candidates in US state elections
subheadline: Candidates contest seats in Connecticut, Texas, Georgia, Pennsylvania, Nevada and Florida
author: Sibt-e-Arif
article_text:
Pakistani-Americans are contesting elections in several US states ahead of the midterm elections on November 3, 2026, with some seeking re-election to their state legislatures.

According to available election lists, Maryam Khan and Saud Anwar are contesting seats in the Connecticut State Senate. In Texas, Salman Bhojani and Suleman Lalani are seeking re-election to the State House of Representatives from Districts 92 and 76, respectively.

Farooq Mughal is contesting a state legislative seat in Georgia, while Tariq Khan is running in Pennsylvania. Hanadi Nadeem is also seeking a seat in the Nevada State Assembly.

In Florida, Imtiaz Mohammad is standing as a Republican candidate. Several other Muslim American candidates are also contesting elections in various states.

Most of the Pakistani-American candidates are running for seats in state legislatures or state senates. These are state-level elections and should not be confused with contests for the US Congress, which comprises the federal House of Representatives and the Senate.

headline: Man who left home at 29 returns at 57 after walking 31,000 miles around world
subheadline: Karl Bushby was also detained in Panama, Russia and held at gunpoint in Mexico
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A British adventurer who left home as a young man in 1998 has finally returned to his mother's doorstep after spending 28 years travelling around the world without using any transport to move forward.

Karl Bushby, now 57, was welcomed by hundreds of cheering supporters in his hometown of Hull on Monday (November 2), bringing an end to an extraordinary 31,000-mile journey across four continents and 30 countries.

His mother, Angela, broke down in tears as she embraced her son outside the family home, which had been decorated with a banner reading "Welcome Home Son".

"Where have you been?" she jokingly asked him.

Bushby was just 29 when he set off from Chile on November 1, 1998, carrying a tent, a few hundred dollars and a camera.

The former British paratrooper had initially expected the expedition to take around five years. Instead, it consumed nearly half his life.

During the journey, he survived dangerous jungles, crossed the frozen Bering Strait between Alaska and Russia, and spent 31 days swimming across the Caspian Sea.

He was also detained in Panama and Russia, held at gunpoint in Mexico and repeatedly delayed by visa restrictions, financial problems and the COVID-19 pandemic.

Bushby revealed that he spent only about 15 of those 28 years actually walking, with the remaining time consumed by paperwork, logistics and securing funding.

His final challenge came last month when he swam across the English Channel to complete the journey without taking a boat or plane.

Back home, his 36-year-old son and 12-year-old granddaughter, whom he had never met, were waiting to welcome him.

Reflecting on the journey, Bushby credited strangers across the world for helping him survive.

"I didn't do this alone," he told supporters, describing the expedition as a global effort.

article_html:
A British adventurer who left home as a young man in 1998 has finally returned to his mother's doorstep after spending 28 years travelling around the world without using any transport to move forward.

Karl Bushby, now 57, was welcomed by hundreds of cheering supporters in his hometown of Hull on Monday (November 2), bringing an end to an extraordinary 31,000-mile journey across four continents and 30 countries.

His mother, Angela, broke down in tears as she embraced her son outside the family home, which had been decorated with a banner reading "Welcome Home Son".

"Where have you been?" she jokingly asked him.

Bushby was just 29 when he set off from Chile on November 1, 1998, carrying a tent, a few hundred dollars and a camera.

The former British paratrooper had initially expected the expedition to take around five years. Instead, it consumed nearly half his life.

During the journey, he survived dangerous jungles, crossed the frozen Bering Strait between Alaska and Russia, and spent 31 days swimming across the Caspian Sea.

He was also detained in Panama and Russia, held at gunpoint in Mexico and repeatedly delayed by visa restrictions, financial problems and the COVID-19 pandemic.

Bushby revealed that he spent only about 15 of those 28 years actually walking, with the remaining time consumed by paperwork, logistics and securing funding.

His final challenge came last month when he swam across the English Channel to complete the journey without taking a boat or plane.

Back home, his 36-year-old son and 12-year-old granddaughter, whom he had never met, were waiting to welcome him.

Reflecting on the journey, Bushby credited strangers across the world for helping him survive.

"I didn't do this alone," he told supporters, describing the expedition as a global effort.

headline: Zayn Malik transforms into Jim Carrey's 'The Mask' character for Halloween
subheadline: The former One Direction star, 33, sports a prosthetic green mask along with the iconic yellow suit
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Zayn Malik has a ssssmokin’ Halloween costume this year.

The former One Direction star dressed up as Jim Carrey’s The Mask character, complete with a prosthetic green mask and the iconic yellow suit, unveiling his look in a series of Instagram posts on Sunday, November 1.

Malik, 33, also shared a behind-the-scenes video documenting the lengthy makeup process, which was handled by Gotham FX and RBFX Makeup Gallery.

READ MORE: Jim Carrey reacts to 'The Mask' director Chuck Russell's death

Fully embracing the character, the singer showed off a range of impressions, channelling everyone from The Terminator and Johnny Bravo to John Lennon and Hermione Granger.

“Shombody shtop mehhh,” he captioned the post, referencing one of the most memorable lines from the 1994 comedy, which also marked Cameron Diaz’s feature film debut.

The Mask follows Stanley Ipkiss (Carrey), a timid bank clerk who discovers a magical wooden mask connected to Loki, the Norse god of mischief. Once he puts it on, he transforms into a chaotic, green-faced trickster with reality-bending powers.

Malik’s Halloween reveal comes shortly after the conclusion of his Konnakol Tour, which supported his fifth studio album of the same name. The nine-date run began in London on May 23 and wrapped up in Lima, Peru, on October 14. The tour was originally scheduled to feature 32 shows, but the US leg, an Irish concert and two UK dates were cancelled due to the singer’s health issues.

READ MORE: Zayn Malik cancels US leg of tour one month after hospitalisation

headline: Four NASA volunteers see outside world after 378 days of living on 'Mars'
subheadline: The four-member crew included commander Ross Elder, Ellen Ellis, Matthew Montgomery and James Spicer
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Four volunteers who spent more than a year pretending to live on Mars have finally stepped outside their isolated habitat, seeing the outside world for the first time in 378 days.

The crew emerged from NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston on Saturday (October 31), ending an experiment designed to find out whether humans can survive the isolation, limited supplies and psychological pressures of a journey to the Red Planet.

For more than a year, the volunteers lived inside a 1,700-square-foot, 3D-printed habitat, where they grew crops, conducted simulated spacewalks and carried out scientific experiments.

They also had to communicate with the outside world through artificial delays, recreating the time it takes for messages to travel between Earth and Mars.

Even conversations with family members were restricted to emails delayed to mimic communication across millions of miles.

The four-member crew included commander Ross Elder, medical officer Ellen Ellis, science officer Matthew Montgomery and flight engineer James Spicer.

Speaking after emerging from isolation, Ellis described the experience as a year spent voluntarily cut off from the outside world.

The experiment, known as Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA), began on October 19, 2025.

Throughout the mission, NASA monitored how the volunteers managed their daily routines, physical health, teamwork and limited resources.

The crew will now undergo two weeks of medical evaluations and debriefings to help researchers understand how astronauts might cope with prolonged missions away from Earth.

This was NASA's second year-long Mars simulation, following a similar experiment completed in 2024.

The agency hopes the findings will help prepare astronauts for future missions to the Moon and eventually Mars, where crews could spend years away from home with little possibility of immediate assistance.

headline: Jessica Alba rushes to delete Halloween post after backlash over costume
subheadline: The actress, 45, recreates the brutal 1994 attack on Tonya Harding's figure skating rival Nancy Kerrigan
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Jessica Alba has sparked backlash over her Halloween costume.

According to the Daily Express, the actress dressed up as a battered Nancy Kerrigan with her friend as Tonya Harding, recreating one of sports’ most horrific moments. She has since appeared to have deleted her Instagram post showing off the costume.

Alba, 45, dressed as Kerrigan, 57, in a white outfit, ice skates and a bloodstained bandage around her knee. Her friend Kelly Sawyer dressed as Kerrigan’s rival, Tonya Harding, wearing a sparkly maroon ensemble and posing with a baseball bat.

The costumes were a reference to the 1994 incident in which Kerrigan was attacked with a police baton by Shane Stant, who was hired by Harding’s ex-husband. The assault happened shortly before Olympic qualifiers, forcing Kerrigan to withdraw. Harding was never criminally convicted over the attack but received a lifetime ban from the U.S. Figure Skating Association.

READ MORE: Jessica Alba enjoys 'out of this world' moment with Artemis II mission

The costume choice drew criticism from Alba’s followers, with one commenting, “Immature. We expect better, Jessica.” Another questioned the decision to revisit a traumatic incident, while a third wrote, “Wow, first Martha and now Jessica. Why are we being nasty this Halloween?”

Alba’s deleted post also featured her 8-year-old son Hayes dressed as a vampire. Her daughters, Honor, 18, and Haven, 15, celebrated Halloween too, with Haven sharing her unicorn costume online. Alba has been dating actor Danny Ramirez since separating from ex-husband Cash Warren last year.

READ MORE: Martha Stewart addresses backlash over her Halloween costume

headline: Scientists challenge long-held theory about how life began on Earth
subheadline: The possibility of comets delivering the necessary ingredients could not be ruled out entirely
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Scientists have raised fresh doubts on a popular theory that suggests some of the building blocks of life on Earth were brought here by comets, after they discovered that such cosmic objects could have wiped them out when they crashed into the planet billions of years ago.

For years, scientists have speculated that comets could have delivered organic compounds to the early Earth that contributed to the evolution of life.

But a new study by researchers at the University of Cambridge suggests that the theory has a major problem: the comets may have been travelling too fast for those chemicals to survive the impact.

The findings, published in Scientific Reports, are based on 100,000 computer simulations examining what happens when comets collide with a planet.

Researchers focused on compounds such as hydrogen cyanide, which can play an important role in the chemical reactions that produce amino acids, the building blocks of proteins.

Their calculations suggest that the extreme heat and pressure generated during most comet impacts would have destroyed these fragile compounds before they could contribute to the emergence of life.

Lead researcher Richard Anslow said the possibility of comets delivering the necessary ingredients could not be ruled out entirely, although it would have required unusually favourable circumstances.

The findings also raise questions about whether Mars might have been better placed to receive such chemicals, given differences in the conditions under which comets strike the two planets.

Scientists are now considering whether asteroids played a bigger role in delivering organic material to Earth, or whether the ingredients for life formed here through natural chemical processes.

The study does not explain how life began. It does, however, cast doubt on one proposed route by which some of its essential ingredients may have arrived.

headline: Vivienne Jolie-Pitt legally drops 'Pitt' from her last name
subheadline: Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt’s daughter Vivienne officially becomes Vivienne Jolie
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Vivienne Jolie-Pitt, the 18-year-old daughter of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt, has legally dropped “Pitt” from her last name.

The change was approved on Monday 2 November at a hearing in a Los Angeles courtroom.

Her name is now Vivienne Marcheline Jolie, rather than Vivienne Marcheline Jolie-Pitt. She has used “Jolie” as a professional name for more than two years.

Read more: Angelina Jolie fights Brad Pitt over new court demand

Vivienne filed in July to drop her father’s surname, citing “personal” reasons, according to Page Six.

Her attorney, Peter Kenneth Levine, appeared remotely, and Judge Virginia Keeny read out the names of the approved petitions, including hers.

The decree is expected in about a week from room 112 at the Stanley Mosk Courthouse.

Vivienne was first listed as “Vivienne Jolie” in the May 2024 Broadway Playbill for The Outsiders, on which she worked as a producer’s assistant.

Her mother was a producer on the musical.

She is the latest of the couple’s children to move away from the surname. Her twin, Knox, left it off his June 2026 high school graduation certificate, though he has not yet changed it legally.

Shiloh, 20, legally became Shiloh Jolie in August 2024, shortly after turning 18. Maddox, 25, and Zahara, 21, legally dropped the name earlier this year. Pax, 22, is the only sibling still using Pitt.

Brad Pitt has not commented publicly.

In a September interview with L’Officiel, Angelina Jolie said of her children: “They’re definitely individuals.” She added that a key parental goal is “to basically not get in their way.”

headline: Who was Nathalia Filgueiras? Everything to know about 20-year-old Learjet60 copilot killed in Florida
subheadline: Nathalia Filgueiras, 20, Identified as Co-Pilot in Fatal Florida Learjet Crash
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The co-pilot of the Learjet 60 aircraft which crashed and claimed nine lives in Palm Beach County, Florida, on Sunday has been identified as Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, an aspiring commercial pilot who obtained her private pilot’s license even before finishing high school at the age of 20.

According to the information released by Filgueiras’ mother and stepfather, Camila and Thiago Corteleti, to the New York Post, the young pilot, who was born and raised in Boca Raton, had clocked over 1,300 flight hours as well as working for Upper Jets – a privately owned airline based in Fort Lauderdale – as a commercial pilot for the last nine months.

The Learjet was flying from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas when it suddenly descended sharply, falling over 20,000 feet per minute and slamming into the ground near Greenacres, creating a crater from which smoke was seen rising. Disturbing air traffic control recording reveals how the pilot called out “Mayday” and then said, “We're going to crash into the ground.”

Filgueiras had texted her boyfriend only ten minutes prior to the incident, telling him that she was facing turbulence and icing, as per her stepfather. "I wanted her to fulfil her dream, but I understood very well that her dream was the thing that would make her leave me," her mother said. "I know she was following her dream."

Filgueiras hit the local news headlines in 2023 after she received a pilot's license when she was 17 years old, even before she got her driver's license.

Her education was financed by the School District of Palm Beach County's Aviation Academy. "I definitely do brag because people tell me, 'Oh, you can't drive,' and I say to them, 'Yes, I can drive, but I can fly as well,'" she said in an interview with CBS12.

No identity of the remaining eight victims has been released by the authorities yet. An investigation into the reason behind the crash is being conducted by the FAA and the NTSB.

According to the information released by Filgueiras’ mother and stepfather, Camila and Thiago Corteleti, to the New York Post, the young pilot, who was born and raised in Boca Raton, had clocked over 1,300 flight hours as well as working for Upper Jets – a privately owned airline based in Fort Lauderdale – as a commercial pilot for the last nine months.

The Learjet was flying from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas when it suddenly descended sharply, falling over 20,000 feet per minute and slamming into the ground near Greenacres, creating a crater from which smoke was seen rising. Disturbing air traffic control recording reveals how the pilot called out “Mayday” and then said, “We're going to crash into the ground.”

Filgueiras had texted her boyfriend only ten minutes prior to the incident, telling him that she was facing turbulence and icing, as per her stepfather. "I wanted her to fulfil her dream, but I understood very well that her dream was the thing that would make her leave me," her mother said. "I know she was following her dream."

Filgueiras hit the local news headlines in 2023 after she received a pilot's license when she was 17 years old, even before she got her driver's license. 

Her education was financed by the School District of Palm Beach County's Aviation Academy. "I definitely do brag because people tell me, 'Oh, you can't drive,' and I say to them, 'Yes, I can drive, but I can fly as well,'" she said in an interview with CBS12.

No identity of the remaining eight victims has been released by the authorities yet. An investigation into the reason behind the crash is being conducted by the FAA and the NTSB.

headline: Ariana Grande shares glimpse into life with Ricky Alvarez amid 'break'
subheadline: The pop icon, 33, shares sweet new photos with her boyfriend, 38
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Ariana Grande is enjoying life away from the spotlight with her boyfriend, Ricky Alvarez.

On Monday, November 2, the pop star shared a photo dump on social media featuring moments with Alvarez, her dogs, and friends. She kept the caption simple, adding a heart and three exclamation points.

Among the snapshots, Grande, 33, and Alvarez, 38, were seen embracing and gazing into each other’s eyes during a walk. Another photo captured the singer planting a gentle kiss on her boyfriend’s forehead. The couple rekindled their romance over the summer after first dating in 2016.

READ MORE: Ariana Grande, Ricky Alvarez level up relationship after matching tattoos

The post also offered a closer look at Grande’s dramatic new haircut. The singer recently traded her signature long locks for a bob.

Away from her romantic life, Grande has also been spending more time with her 10 dogs following the recent loss of Coco, her first-ever pet, who died last month after 17 years together.

The photo dump offers a rare glimpse into Grande’s life since wrapping up her Eternal Sunshine tour on September 1. Before the tour ended, her spokesperson told People magazine that the singer “looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny.”

headline: Pakistan Literature Festival brings writers, poets, scholars from three nations to Houston
subheadline: Discussions cover Urdu literature, Pakistani culture, journalism, cinema and social challenges in a rapidly digitising world
author: Raja Zahid Akhtar Khanazada
article_text:
HOUSTON: The third Pakistan Literature Festival, a two-day event organised by the International Academy of Letters USA, concluded on November 1 in Sugar Land and Stafford, in the Houston area of the US state of Texas.

Held on October 31 and November 1, the festival brought together writers, poets, journalists, intellectuals and artists from Pakistan, the United States and Canada. Discussions covered Urdu language and literature, Pakistani culture, journalism, cinema, television drama, the identity of the younger generation, social issues and challenges facing Pakistan.

Pakistan's Ambassador to the United States, Rizwan Saeed Sheikh, was unable to attend in person because of official commitments but addressed the gathering through a video message. Pakistan's Consul General in Houston, Aftab Chaudhry, also spoke at the event, which was attended by Canadian parliamentarian Sameer Zuberi.

The festival was organised by Ghazanfar Hashmi, president of the International Academy of Letters USA, who welcomed the participants.

The opening day began at the Ismaili Jamatkhana and Centre in Sugar Land with an inaugural ceremony, followed by panel discussions.

A discussion titled "Women's Voices in Urdu Literature" featured Professor Tahira Naqvi, Ishrat Afreen, Dr Saima Iram, Mona Shahab, Bina Goindi and Tasneem Abidi. Nasira Zuberi moderated the session.

Another discussion, "Two Cultures, Two Generations: New Concepts of Leadership", included Dr Mohsin Ansari, Canadian MP Sameer Zuberi, Dr Imran Sharif, Siraj Narsi, Maria Kari and Umar Khawaja. Ibrahim Javed moderated the panel.

Mental health, its challenges and possible solutions were discussed by Nasruddin Rupani, Dr Asim Shah, Dr Mohsin Ansari, Mahtab Muradi, Nusrat Haris and Asif Sinan. Mazhar Khawaja moderated the discussion, while Naveeda Hashmi delivered the opening remarks.

A panel on the past and present of Pakistani cinema and television drama featured Shahab Zuberi, Nilofar Abbasi, Noor Naghmi, Adil Murad, Kamran Ali Asdar and Yasir Raza. Najia Ashar moderated the discussion.

The day's cultural programme also included "Sham-e-Ishq" (An Evening of Love), featuring Sufi music performances by Hasnain Javed and Asif Sinan.

On November 1, the programme moved to the Tuscany Ballroom at the Spark by Hilton in Stafford, where literary and intellectual discussions continued.

A panel titled "Iqbal: A Poet for Every Age" featured Dr Muhammad Naeem Virk, Dr Saima Iram, Atif Tauqeer, Pervez Jafri and other scholars.

The discussion "Pakistani Media: Truth and Responsibility" brought together journalists Shahab Zuberi, Raza Rumi, Ashraf Shad, Fazil Jamili, Faisal Aziz Khan and Khurram Shahzad. Yousuf Chaudhry delivered the opening remarks, while Ghazanfar Hashmi moderated. The panellists discussed journalistic responsibilities, challenges facing the news media and changes in the media landscape.

Another discussion, "Reimagining Pakistan's Future: Challenges and Opportunities", featured Shabbar Zaidi, with Ghazanfar Hashmi and Nasira Zuberi as moderators.

The programme also included activities related to books, fine arts and Pakistan's cultural heritage.

The closing ceremony was followed by an international mushaira, a traditional Urdu poetry gathering, presided over by Khawaja Razi Haider and hosted by Mehboob Zafar. Several poets recited their work.

The festival offered members of the Pakistani diaspora a platform to exchange ideas on literature, language, culture and contemporary issues.

As the two-day gathering drew to a close, a key message emerging from the discussions was the need to pass on the connection to the Urdu language and literature to the next generation and strengthen intellectual and cultural ties.

headline: Dustin Hoffman calls making 'The Graduate' a 'terrible experience'
subheadline: Dustin Hoffman Reveals Mike Nichols’ 'Sadism' On The Graduate Set
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Dustin Hoffman has described the making of The Graduate, the film that earned him his first Oscar nomination, as a miserable experience, laying out a difficult relationship with director Mike Nichols in a new essay for The New Yorker.

“It was a terrible experience making the movie that changed my life,” Hoffman wrote in the piece, which was published over the weekend and is largely focused on his dealings with Nichols.

The actor says Nichols was warm and welcoming during rehearsals, but became a different person once cameras started rolling.

According to Hoffman, the director “was irritable with everyone, but with me a certain sadism seemed to creep in.”

One of the most striking episodes he recalls involves a scene in which co-star Katharine Ross had to slap him.

Nichols reportedly made the pair go through twenty-seven takes, and the moment never made it into the finished film.

The physical toll did not end there.

Hoffman writes that he punctured an eardrum while filming a pool scene in a wetsuit, and that he came close to losing consciousness while shooting the sequence in which his character runs to the church.

Looking back, Hoffman says he came to understand what was going on.

He believes Nichols was using him as a stand-in for his own feelings, particularly in the wake of the director’s split from his former comedy partner Elaine May.

In his words, he was “there to absorb Mike’s own self-loathing.”

The Graduate turned Hoffman, then a relative newcomer, into a household name, and it remains one of the most celebrated American films of its era.

His account of the shoot offers a very different picture of what went on behind the scenes of the 1967 classic.

Hoffman has himself faced allegations of inappropriate behaviour on various sets over the years, including a well-publicised incident involving a slap to Meryl Streep during the making of Kramer vs. Kramer.

headline: What happened at Boca Ciega high school? Everything to know
subheadline: Lockdown lifted at Boca Ciega high school after report of masked, knife-wielding suspects
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A report of people wearing masks with knives at a high school in Gulfport has sent students and parents into a state of panic on Monday after a lockdown was initiated for about two hours.

Around 10:15 am, the Gulfport Police Department received a call from Boca Ciega High School concerning three individuals "wearing ski masks and knives," said GPD. The school was locked down immediately, with the Pinellas County Sheriff's Office, Pinellas County Schools Police, Indian Shores Police Department and local firefighters converging on the location of the crime.

No threat was found by the authorities, but the individual described in the call has been captured by CCTV cameras leaving the school premises. Law enforcement is currently trying to identify the individual.

Fortunately, no one has sustained any injuries. The school was allowed to reopen at 12:22 p.m. After the lockdown ended, parents were informed about the case through a message sent out by the school, according to GPD.

Photos from the scene indicated that there was an increased law enforcement presence on the campus in the morning as the sweeps were carried out. There has been an alarm among the Gulfport community members after the news about the threat to the school reached the parents.

It is unclear whether the threat was real and whether the person who appeared on the surveillance videos had any intentions to cause harm. The investigations are still going on, and the police department has requested everyone who has information to contact them.

The lockdown happens against the backdrop of the current concerns regarding school security in Florida and in the country.
